parties:
Amin Md Lands Development Limited......Plaintiff-Appellant
vs
Monira Munni and others……….Contesting-Defendants-Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J : This appeal at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the judgment and decree dated 22-2-2018 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 54 of 2016 dismissing the suit for Specific Performance of contract. 

 2. Facts necessary for disposal of the appeal briefly, be put thus: Plaintiff Company Amin Mohammad Lands Development Limited instituted Title Suit No. 110 of 2009 for Specific Performance of Contract on 22-2-2009 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and respondent No. 3 as pro-forma defendant No. 3 which was subsequently transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 54 of 2016 alleging, inter alia, that the defendant No. 1 acquired the land measuring 2.85 acres as described in schedule 'ka' to the plaint was purchased by the defendant No. 1 by registered kabala No. 17274 dated 30-6-2005 from Adnan Co-operative Housing Society Ltd; that defendant No. 1 also purchased the land measuring 0.6264 Ajutansha described in schedule 'kha' to the plaint by way of registered kabala No. 16729 dated 30-6-2005 from Abdul Matin and Md Nazrul Islam; that while possessing the suit land comprising schedules 'ka' and `kha' to the plaint measuring total area of 3.4764 mortgaged the schedule land to defendant No. 3-Bank against the loan Case No. BASIC /DIL/CREDIT/2008/247 obtained by defendant No. 2, husband of the defendant No. 1 as security of the aforesaid loan; that at this stage, defendant No. 1 through her husband, defendant No. 2 offered to transfer the suit land to the plaintiff to redeem the schedule 'ka' and 'kha' suit land at a total consideration of Taka 3,07,31,200 whereupon the plaintiff company agreed to purchase the same, and accordingly, executed a registered "Bainanama Dalil" (বায়নানাম দলিল) on 10-4-2008 in respect of the suit land fixing the total value of the land Taka 1,15,00,000 out of which Taka 40,00,000 was paid by the plaintiff's company as earnest money through cheque No. 139325 of HSBC Bank; that on the same day (10-4-2008) another (চুক্তিপত্র) Deed of Agreement was executed between the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 and 2 for redeeming of the suit land which was mortgaged to the defendant No. 3-Bank; that in the said agreement total consideration was fixed Taka 1,92,31,200 for redeeming the mortgage land from the Bank and out which a sum of Taka 5,00,000 was paid in advance on 18-3-2008 and Taka 20,00,000 on 2-4-2008 in cash and at the time of agreement on 10-4-2008 paid a further sum of Taka 85,00,000 by cheque No. 1393256 dated 10-4-2008. Accordingly, the defendant No. 1 received total amount of Taka 1,50,00,000 against Bainanama and Deed of Agreement and on the same day delivered possession of the suit land to the plaintiff company; that after taking delivery of possession of the suit 'ka' and 'kha' schedule land defendant No. 1 further received Taka 5,00,000 on 29-5-2008 by signing a voucher and assured that she will redeem the suit land from the Bank within 15-10-2008. It was further stated that although the defendant No. 1 received total amount of Taka 1,55,00,000 but did not take steps to redeem the suit land from the bank as per bainanama and Deed of Agreement; that later on the plaintiff company enquired in the office of defendant No. 3-Bank and came to learn that the defendant No. 1 deposited only Taka 70,00,000 in the loan account against receipt of Taka 1,55,00,000 from the plaintiff company for re-payment of the loan of the defendant No. 3-Bank; that since the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 did not take step to pay the loan of the Bank, plaintiff-company sent a notice to the defendants and requested them to receive the balance amount after paying off the entire loan-liabilities and execute the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff-company; that after receipt of said letter, defendant No. 2 met with the Director of the plaintiff's company and again assured to execute and register sale deed after redeeming the mortgage; that while the plaintiff's company possessing the suit 'ka' and 'kha' schedule land by constructing boundary wall and also constructed one semi-pucca two roomed house inside the 'ka' schedule land and using the said house as site office and guard room of the "Ashulia Abakash No. 2" project; that on 08-2-2009 the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 sent a letter informing that since the defendants required more money than the money paid by the plaintiff's company to redeem their mortgaged land and due to non-payment of more money, they could not redeem their mortgaged land, moreover, the period of bainanama was already expired in the meantime, they are no more bound by the agreement and as such they requested the plaintiff company to execute "Bainapatra Return Deed" /"Deed of Recession of Bainapatra"; that the plaintiff company asked the defendant No. 1 to complete the transaction on receipt of the balance consideration but this was of no avail. On these allegations, the plaintiff brought the suit for Specific Performance of contract with a prayer for paying the loan of defendant No. 3-Bank after redeeming the mortgage of the suit land mortgaged with Bank from the deposited amount of Taka 1,52,31,200 deposited under Bangladesh Bank challan No. 10233 dated 24-2-2009 and execute the necessary sale deed in respect of schedule 'ka' and 'kha of the suit land after receiving the balance consideration money. In case of default by the defendant No. 1 and 2 in executing and registering the necessary sale deed in favour of the plaintiff company, directed the defendant No. 3-Bank to redeem the mortgaged property after receiving its loan money from the deposited amount of Taka 1,52,31,200 deposited in court at the time of filing of suit on 24-2-2009. 

 4. The proforma defendant No. 3, Basic Bank Ltd. contested the suit by filing written statement on 15-10-2009. The case of the defendant No. 3 is that the defendant Bank, has allowed an Over Draft facility in favour of its client namely Bushra Associate (hereinafter referred as the borrower) for an amount of Taka 22.00 lac (twenty two lac) vide its sanction letter No.BASIC/DIL/CREDIT/2005 /3107 Dated 27-8-2005, subsequently the said loan facility was rescheduled and enhanced on several occasions. It is pertinent to mention here that as security of the said Over Draft facility Mrs Munira Munni i.e., the defendant No. 1 of the instant suit has mortgaged her landed property (more specifically mentioned in the schedule-B) vide Registered Mortgage Deed being No. 20083 dated 31-8-2005 in favour of the defendant Bank and she also executed a Registered Power of Attorney being No. 20084 dated 31-8-2005 empowering the defendant Rank to sell the Mortgaged Property. That after availing the said loan facility the borrower failed to repay loan amount to defendant Bank. The defendant Bank has issued several reminder and request letters to the borrower to repay the loan liabilities but no effect as a result the total liability stands at Taka 2,35,51,987.20 as on 31-12-2009 including upto date interest accrued thereon. That it is also mentionable here that one Mr Khandaker Mehmood Alam Nadim has availed an Over Draft facility which now stands at Taka 68,26,000 only as 31-12-2009 where the defendant No. 1 of the suit has also executed letter of Guarantee in favour of the defendant Bank as security of the loan facility extended to said Khandaker Mehmood Alam Nadim. That it is further stated the plaintiff having knowledge regarding mortgage of the suit property and as well as the legal consequence of a mortgage formalities with a malafide intention inpleaded the instant defendant Bank as proforma-defendant No. 3 as such, the plaintiff has never entitle to get any relief against the instant defendant Bank. That it is humbly submitted that the defendant Bank has no knowledge regarding the alleged Bainanama and the defendant Bank has absolute interest upon the properties which is mortgaged to the Bank till adjustment of the loan liabilities or till the date when the defendant Bank execute a Deed of Redemption. 

 7. The learned Joint District Judge having heard respective parties and considered the evidence adduced by the parties dismissed the suit against the defendants by the impugned judgment and decree dated 22-2-2018 on the findings that admittedly the suit land was mortgaged to the defendant No. 3-Bank. But before executing the Bainanama defendants did not obtain permission from the defendant -Bank and defendant Bank is not a party in the Baina and Deed of Agreement as such the disputed Bainanama (Exhibit-2) is not a Bainanama in the eye of law and same is barred under provision of section 53D of the Transfer of Property Act. Thus the plaintiff is not entitled to get decree for Specific Performance of Contract as per Bainanama Dali I (Exhibit-2). 

 9. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant submits that as per terms of the Bainanama the sale deed would be executed and registered by the defendant No. 1 on payment of loan amount and after redeeming the suit mortgage land which was mortgaged to the defendant-Bank. In elaborating his submission, the Learned Advocate argues that in a contract where on either side there are promises to be performed and the promises are so connected to each other, performance of one is dependent on another, it is said to be condition precedent to the right of action on the reciprocal promise. Learned Advocate further submits that in the present suit mortgagee-Bank-defendant No. 3 was impleaded and requested to withdrew the loan amount from the deposited balance Taka 1,52,31,000 filed by challan dated 24-2-2009 on the date of filing of the suit on 24-2-2009. But the Bank without withdrawing the arrear loan amount from the said deposit of Taka 1,52,31,000 filed written statement stating that for non-payment/default of the defendant No. 2 the over draft loan of Taka 22,00,000 same was enhanced to Taka 2,35,51,987.20 as on 31-12-2009 and further stated another over draft loan of defendant No. 2, which has now stood Taka 68,26,000 as on 31-12-2009. So, the Bank is now entitled (Taka 2,35,51,987.20 + 68,26,000) = Total Taka 3,03,77,987.20 with interest till the mortgage is redeemed in future. Learned Advocate by referring section 47 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 next submits that the Bank in no circumstances claims more than 3 times against the principal loan i.e. Taka 22,00,000 x 3 = Taka 66,00,000 which can be easily adjustable from the deposit amount of Taka 1,52,31,000 remaining balance amount of Taka 86,31,200. On the other hand, another Over Draft loan now stood at Taka 68,26,000 with interest as on 31-12-2009 can also be adjusted from the balance deposited amount Taka 86,31,200. So, the Mortgage-Bank is in no way would be prejudiced. He also submits that since the Bank had not filed any suit claiming the loan amount, the same is barred under section 46 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Thus the court can easily decreed the present suit for Specific Performance of Contract as per prayer made in the suit directing the defendant No. 3-Mortgagee Bank to redeem the mortgage after receiving its due arrear of loan from the balance deposit amount of Taka 1,52,31,000 deposited in court on 24-2-2009 at the time of filing of the present suit. 

 12. AM Masum, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant No.3 Basic Bank Limited by endorsing the legal submission made by the learned Advocate for the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, submits that the plaintiff is not entitled to get relief in this suit. In support of his submission he cited two decisions reported in 57 DLR (AD) 64 and 63 DLR (AD) 326. He further argued that the present suit is barred under section 22 of the Specific Relief Act and on this point referred the decision of 53 DLR 535. Mr Masum by referring section 20 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 strenuously argued that no suit can be filed in any court challenging the decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 14. It appears that the registered Bainanama Deed dated 10-4-2008 (Exhibit- 2) on which the plaintiff have based its claim in the present suit for Specific Performance of Contract. Admittedly, the defendant No. 1 is the executant of this Baina Deed. By this Bainanama, its executant, defendant No. 1 stipulated to sell to the plaintiff the suit schedules ‘ka’ and ‘kha’ land having an total area of 3.4764 acres fixing total price of the land at Taka 1,15,00,000. It was further stipulated in the Baina amongst others that defendant No. 1 received Taka 40,00,000 from the plaintiff as earnest money and agreed to execute necessary sale Deed /Deeds in favour of the plaintiff or its nominee and get it registered within 6 months from the date of the Bainanama Deed and balance consideration Taka 75,00,000 will be paid at the time of registration of the sale Deed. On the date of Bainanama, defendant No. 1 also delivered khas possession of the suit land. In the Bainanama it was further agreed that since the suit land was mortgaged to the defendant No. 3-Basic Bank Ltd., the defendant No.1 and 2 jointly execute a deed of agreement dated 10-4-2008 (Exhibit- 3) and in the said agreement it was stipulated that defendant No. 1 and her husband defendant No. 2 will redeem the mortgaged property by paying loan liability together with interest from their own source and at their responsibility within a period of 2 (two) months and furnished the original title deeds to the plaintiff-company. It is also stipulated that if the defendants fail and/or neglect to execute and register the Sale Deeds, the plaintiff will be entitled to obtain the deed through the process of the court. 

 15. It further appears that a Deed of Agreement dated 10-4-2008 (Exhibit-3) was executed between the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2. In clause 5 of the said agreement, it was stipulated that the suit land was mortgaged to the defendant No. 3-Bank against the Bank loan in Loan Case No. BASIC/DIL/CREDIT/2005 /78 and Bank loan Case No. BASIC/DIL/CREDIT/2006/1035 and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 will redeem the suit land after paying the entire loan liabilities including interest within a period of two months and submits the original title deed to the plaintiff company. 

 20. On the close reading of the Bainanama Dalil (Exhibit-2) there is no gain saying that there is obligation on the part of the defendant No. 1 to comply with the conditions stipulated in the Baina. Though there is an stipulation to complete the transaction within a period of 6(six) months, this time limit was circumscribed by the fulfillment of the obligation by the defendant No. 1, who was not given unconditional power to rescind the Baina for non-payment of the balance consideration within 6(six) months. The defendant No. 1 is under obligation to deliver documents of title and other paper after redeeming the mortgage of the suit land and paying the outstanding loan amount of defendant No. 3-Bank. After completing the aforesaid obligations, then the Sale Deed /Deeds will be executed and registered on payment of balance consideration of money Taka 1,52,31,200. 

 21. Unless the defendant No. 1 performs her part of obligation, the plaintiff will not be able to get the registered Sale Deed and clear title of the suit land. The mortgaged property shall be redeemed first for purpose of completion of the transaction. The defendant No. 1 without contacting the plaintiff for completing the transaction for redeeming the mortgage of the suit land unilaterally rescinded the Baina on 8-2-2009. There is nothing on the record that the defendant No. 1 has intimated the plaintiff she has adjusted the loan and redeem the suit land from defendant No.3 Bank and there is no impediment for executing Sale Deed and she is ready and willing to execute the Sale Deed. 

 22. In a contract where on either side there are promises to be performed and the promises are so related to each other, performance of one is dependent on another, it is said to be condition precedent to the right of action on the reciprocal promise. The ordinary rule governing vendors and purchasers is that the payment of the consideration is to be simultaneous with the execution of the deed and shall be made at the time when the deed is executed by the vendor. Contracts are normally made up of various statements and promise on both sides, differing in character and importance; the parties may regard some of these as vital, others as subsidiary, or collateral to the main purpose of the contract. Where one of these is broken, the traditional approach of the court has been to discover, from the tenor of the contract or the expressed intention of the parties, whether the broken was vital to the contract or not. If the parties regarded the term as essential, it is a condition; its failure entitles the innocent party to treat himself as discharged from liability. In law in contracts consisting of reciprocal promises, the promises on either side are considerations for one another. In bilateral contracts, the parties not only exchange promises but also bargain for an exchange of the promised performances. 

 24. In a contract containing reciprocal promises, if one party fails to perform his part of obligation thereby he/she prevents the other party performing his/her promise and in such eventuality the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented and the party so prevented is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of non-performance of the contract. The reason is that one who prevents a thing from being done is not allowed to avail himself of the non-performance which he himself has occasioned, since it is his own act which has brought about that result, and, therefore, he cannot complain that he is damnified. No one can be permitted to find a claim upon his own inequity or to take advantage of his own wrong. Prevention by one party to fulfill the promise is tantamount to a fulfillment of the promise by the party prevented in a case of conditional contract or a contract containing reciprocal promises. 

 28. Now turning to the facts of the present case, the agreement that is Bainanama Dalil in question was executed on 10-4-2008 and though there was stipulation for completing the transaction within six months it was obligatory on the part of the defendant No.1 to handover collateral documents of title and after redeems the mortgage property which was mortgage to the defendant No. 3-Bank. The defendant No. 1 knows this term and without making his title perfect for sale, how he could claim the balance consideration amount within six months. The defendant No. 1 fails to deliver all the title deeds to the plaintiff that she has already adjusted its entire outstanding loan of defendant No. 3-Bank out of the money taken from the plaintiff and this fact shows that the defendant No. 1 is not ready to honour her part of the obligation. The defendant has breached the contract and thus, she cannot avoid the specific performance of contract. The fixation of time is secondary in this case and the parties have not intended the time as the essence of the contract, in as much as, obtaining the necessary deed of redemption from the defendant No. 3-bank is a condition precedent to the conferment of the perfect ownership upon the plaintiff. 

 29. From the above discussion, it is clear that the agreement between the parties is still subsisting despite its recission by the defendant No. 1 and that the defendant No. 1 was in error in treating it rescinded. A wrongful repudiation by one party cannot except by the election of the other party to treat it, put an end to an obligation, if the other party still insists on performance of the contract, that is to say, the parties are left with their rights and liabilities as before. What's more we can infer from the facts that the plaintiff company is willing and ready to perform it part of promise and therefore, the plaintiff is legally entitled to a decree for specific performance. 

 31. The aforesaid provisions contemplates that the word "Sale" appears in that section means transfer of ownership does not impose any bar in entering into an "agreement for sale" in respect of such a land as precisely has happened in the present case to repay the loan amount and then the Deed of Sale would be executed and registered. Moreso, such an agreement for sale in respect of the suit land executed between the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 is not void as the "Deed of Agreement for Sale" (বায়নানামা দলিল) (Exhibit-2) is not the "Deed of Sale" or "Deed of Transfer" as provided under section 53D of the Transfer of Property Act. This view of ours finds support from the decision in the case of SM Hossain vs Abdul Malek reported in 1985 BLD 590. That section 53D was introduced by way of amendment for protecting the mortgagee Bank for realization loan given by it. In the instant suit the mortgagee Bank was impleaded as defendant No. 3 and requested to take the loan amount from the deposited balance amount of Taka 1,52,31,200 in court by challan No. 10233 dated 24-2-2009 on the date of filing of the suit on 24-2-2009. But the defendant No. 3 without withdrawing the arrear loan amount from the said deposited Taka 1,52,31,200 rather by filing written statement claimed that the said loan was defaulted and turned to Taka 2,35,51,370.20 with interest as on 31-12-2009 and further stated that another overdraft loan taken by defendant No. 2, husband of defendant No. 1, the said loan has now stood at Taka 68,26,000 as on 31-12-2009. So, the defendant No. 3 is now entitled Taka 2,35,51,987.20 + 68,26,000 = Total 3,03,77,987.20 with interest till adjustment of the loan liabilities or when the defendant No. 3 redeemed the mortgage in future. 

 33. Now a question may arise whether the mortgagee Bank-defendant No. 3 is entitled to Taka 3,03,77,987.20 as claimed in its written statement. Learned Advocate for the plaintiff by referring section 47 Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 argued that there is limitation of imposing claim and the Bank in no circumstance can claim interest more than 3 times of its principal loan amount i.e. Taka 22,00,000 x 3 = 66,00,000 and another over draft loan of defendant No-2 which now stood at Taka 68,26,000 with interest as on 31-12-2009. Thus the mortgagee-Bank is entitled to claim at best (Taka 66,00,000 + 68,26,000) = 1,34,26,000 not Taka 3,03,77,987.20 and same can easily adjustable from the deposited amount of Taka 1,52,31,200 deposited at the time of filing present suit on 24-2-2009. Although the payment of loan to defendant No. 3 is a matter in between the defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 3 but since the excessive claim is illegal and barred under section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and ultimately it will affect the plaintiff in obtaining Sale Deed through the process of court. Furthermore, it appears from the record that till now the defendant No. 3-Bank had not filed any suit or taken any step for realization of the loan as per section 46 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which is barred under the said section. Thus there is no bar in decreeing the suit for specific performance either directing the defendant No. 3-the mortgagee Bank to redeem the mortgage of the suit land after receiving its due arrear loan from the balance deposit amount lying in the court. 

 35. In the case of Sekandar vs Janata Bank Ltd, 22 BLC (AD) 53. In that case it has been held —A suit for establishment of right, title and interest in respect of mortgaged property by a third party is maintainable because there is no bar either expressly or impliedly in Ain to file such suit. 

 40. We have already shown above that the plaintiff has able to established without any manner of doubt a genuine and straight forward contract was entered into between the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 on 10-4-2008 on the basis of written Bainanama Dalil executed by defendant No. 1 as well as Deed of Agreement executed by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 both the Deed was executed on 10-4-2008 and that contract was obtained from the defendant No.1 within the meaning of section 28 of the Specific Relief Act by any fraud, undue advantage, misrepresentation, concealment, unfair practice, influence or mistake of fact, misapprehension or surprise or that the stipulated price was in any way grossly inadequate with reference to the state of things existing at the date of contract. Explanation to section 12 of the Specific Relief Act specifically provides that unless and until the contrary is proved, the court shall presume that the breach of a contract to transfer immovable property cannot be adequately relieved by compensation in money. Illustration to clause (c) of section 12 of the said Act is as follows: "A contracts with B to sell him a house for Taka 1,000. B is entitled to a decree directing A to convey the house to him, he paying the purchase money". 

 43. The learned Advocate for the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 further submits that the plaintiff did not take any step for registration as per terms of Bainanama within 6 months from the execution of Baina dated 10-4-2008 but plaintiff did not take any step for registration as per Baina as time prescribed for registration as per section 54A of Transfer of Property Act is 6 (six) month. But the plaintiff failed to perform its part within 6 month time, consequently defendant Nos. 1 and 2 faced financial hardship and loss. But it was stipulated in the Bainanama that no specific time was fixed for performance of the Bainanama. Rather it was stipulated in clause 5 of the Baina that defendant No. 1 and 2 will pay the entire loan liabilities including interest of the Bank within 2 month from their own source and at their responsibility and redeem the schedule property and obtained those deeds and furnished original title deeds and document to the plaintiff company. Thus it is evident that the condition of performance of the contract is not absolute rather is dependent on the performance of the promisor-vendor. If the vendor has not performed his part of the contract he/she cannot bound the promisee-vendee-plaintiff company to perform its part of the contract and the contract in such case will remain enforceable as per section 51, 52, 53 and 54 of the Contract Act, 1872. Thus the time in a contract for sale of immovable Property is not the essence of the contract. Reliance may be placed in the case reported in 17 DLR (SC) 481/ 5 BLC (AD) 119, 19 DLR 791. 

 46. Mr Probir Neogi has referred to the decision in the case of Abdur Razzaque Mollah vs Md Qayum Mollah, 53 DLR 535. In this reported Case for specific performance of contract, the plaintiff entered into a Bainanama within defendant No. 1 on 7-6-1986 for sale of suit properties since the defendant No. 1 failed to execute and register Sale Deed, the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 52 of 1992 for suit properties which was mortgaged before hand to defendant No. 3, Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation against Loan Case No. Bag 8 of 1985 for loan of Taka 2,00,000 for construction house on the suit land within the knowledge of the plaintiff and the Mortgagee having obtained decree in Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. 5 of 1991 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge-cum-Artha Rin Adalat, Bagerhat, the instant suit for Specific Performance of Contract over the self same properties is not maintainable in law.

caseno: Civil Appeal Nos.30, 31 and 32 of 2017 with Civil Petition No.4232 of 2018
parties:
Noor Mohammad Khan and others ----------- Appellants (In CA No.31-32 of 2017)
VS
Raisa Aziz Begum and others --------- Respondents (In CA No.31 of 2017)
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J : Civil Appeal Nos.30-32 of 2017 and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 4232 of 2018 have arisen out of the common judgment and decree/Order dated 24th August, 2015 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.167 of 2010, heard analogously with Transfer Appeal Nos.7, 8, 9, 10 & 11 of 2014 disallowing First Appeal No. 167 of 2010, Transfer Appeal Nos.7 of 2014, 09 of 2014, 10 of 2014 and 11 of 2014 and thereby, affirming the judgment and decree dated 18-8-2009 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka (shortly, the trial court) in Title Suit Nos. 483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984 and 66 of 1990 dismissing the aforesaid suits but allowing Transfer Appeal No.08 of 2014 and decreeing Title Suit No.224 of 1997, thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 18-8-2009 of the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No.224 of 1997. 

 Jamila Khatun's case in Title Suit (TS) Nos.483 of 1974 as Plaintiff and as defendants of other suits 

 3. Plaintiff-appellant-Jamila Khatun (briefly, Jamila) on 27-9-1974 filed Title Suit No.483 of 1974 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka (the trial court) against Raisa Aziz Begum (shortly, Raisa) and others for specific performance of contract and also for some other reliefs stating, inter alia, that Raisa, defendant No.1 of the suit had entered into an agreement with plaintiff-Jamila on 20-1-1972 to transfer 29.36 decimals of land with buildings, structures and shop rooms standing thereon of Holding No.10, Purana Paltan, Dhaka, present Plot No.1184, Khatian No.217 of Mouza-Ramna being old Dag Nos.26, 27 and 28, Ward No.3, Sheet No.22 of Mouza-Sahar Dhaka, (hereinafter referred to as the suit property). The price of the suit property was fixed at Rs.1,10,000 and Raisa received a sum of Rs 3,000 as earnest money on the terms and conditions that Raisa would obtain necessary clearance certificates and complete all other formalities within six months and intimate the same to Jamila and Jamila, within three months of such intimation would pay the balance consideration amount of Rs.1,07,000 to Raisa and then Raisa would execute and register a sale deed in favour of Jamila. Subsequently, Raisa received Taka 92,000 from Jamila on different occasions between 15-3-1972 to 19-8-1974 and Raisa admitted/acknowledged about receiving of the said amount through some money receipts. Thus, Taka 15,000 remained outstanding out of the total consideration money. Raisa did not execute the sale deed on receiving the balance amount. Therefore, Jamila filed TS No.483 of 1974. 

 4. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 18-7-1978 against Raisa. So, plaintiff Jamila deposited the balance consideration of Taka 15,000 through Chalan No.561 dated 13-7-1978. Subsequently, Raisa filed Miscellaneous Case No.34 of 1979 to set-aside the ex-parte judgment and decree. Whereupon, the learned judge of the trial court by order dated 24-3-1980 allowed the said miscellaneous case, set aside the ex-parte judgment and decree and restored the suit to its original file and number. 

 Noor Mohammad Khan's(being dead his heirs) Case as plaintiff in Title Suit No.113 of 1984 (original Title Suit No.364 of 1982) and as defendants of other suits 

 7. Noor Mohammad Khan (Khan), defendant No.5 of Title Suit No.483 of 1974, as sole plaintiff, filed Title Suit No.364 of 1982 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Raisa, Badiur, Jamila and some others for specific performance of contract against Raisa on the basis of an agreement for sale dated 23-7-1969 as well as an agreement dated 10-7-1977 renewing the previous agreement for sale and also for khas possession of the suit property contending, inter alia, that Raisa for raising cash money wanted to sell the suit property. Whereupon, Khan offered to purchase the same at Taka 45,000. Raisa accepted the said offer. Thereafter, on receipt of Taka 15,000 as earnest money she entered into an agreement for sale of the suit property with Khan on 23-7-1969. Raisa's cousin Badiur was a witness to the agreement for sale. It was decided that after procuring clearance certificate Raisa would execute and register the sale deed in favour of Khan but Raisa could not procure all necessary documents for registration of the deed and on her request Khan paid her Taka 5,000 on 23-10-1970 but due to political disturbance at the relevant period Khan could not obtain the deed of sale from Raisa. After liberation of Bangladesh, Khan traced out Raisa and Badiur in September, 1973 and came to know from Raisa that some miscreants took over possession of the suit property and that the suit property was enlisted as an abandoned property. Raisa disclosed that after release of the suit property, she would execute and register necessary deed of sale in favour of Khan. At her request, Khan paid further amount of Taka 3,000 in the 1st part of January, 1977. Raisa and Badiur demanded a further amount of Taka 50,000 to meet the expenses for release of the suit property from the list of abandoned property and to evict the unauthorized occupants therefrom. Considering all those aspects another instrument was executed between them on 21-1-1977 in the form of an agreement. This agreement provided that Mr Yakub Ali, the learned Advocate for Raisa would take steps to release the suit property and Khan would pay Taka 50,000 for this purpose. Accordingly, Khan paid Taka 20,000 and a cheque of Taka 30,000 to Raisa and the said instrument was kept in the custody of Mr Yakub Ali. Subsequently, Raisa and Badiur told Khan that Mr Yakub Ali, trapped them and if the transaction of cash as well as the encashment of cheque was made with the knowledge of Advocate Mr Yakub Ali, he would keep a major portion thereof. They requested Khan to stop payment of the cheque. Subsequently, on mutual understanding Raisa issued a notice rescinding the agreement dated 21-1-1977 through Mr Yakub Ali and then Raisa and Khan entered into a new agreement dated 1-5-1977 fixing the price of suit property at Taka 4,50,000 out of which Taka 1,35,500 was paid earlier according to the previous agreement and Taka 92,500 was paid on 1-5-1977. It was also decided that Khan would pay Taka 60,000 for release of the suit property. Then, Raisa disclosed that she would go to Pakistan to attend the marriage ceremony of her daughter and she appointed her brother as her attorney by an instrument dated 17-5-1977 to complete the transaction. Badiur showed a photocopy of the said power of attorney to Khan. On 11-7-1977 Khan departed for London after paying Taka 10,000 to Badiur on 10-7-1977 for release of the property. He returned to Bangladesh in the middle of 1979 and Badiur told him that they were processing the matter. Badiur also asked him to pay further amount as Raisa was badly in need of some money. So, he again paid Taka 1,80,000 in cash out of the balance consideration money as well as Taka 10,000 to Badiur for the purpose of release of the suit property and then left for London. He returned in November, 1980 and requested Badiur to complete the transaction and paid Taka 40,000 in cash and further amounts on different dates against written money receipt issued by Badiur on behalf of Raisa. The suit property was accordingly released from the list of abandoned property on 12-1-1982. Accordingly, Memo No.Sec. XVI/AP-28/77/20 dated 21-1-1982 was issued by the abandoned property authority releasing the suit property from the list of abandoned property. So, Khan came back to Dhaka on 18-1-1982 for getting the sale deed registered from Raisa. He paid Taka 40,000 on 25-1-1982 to Raisa but again Raisa informed him that she would go to Syedpur for seven days and asked him to get ready with necessary papers for obtaining income tax certificate. Accordingly, Khan procured necessary papers but Raisa did not return in time. Thereafter, she refused to execute and register the sale deed in his favour. Subse-quently, Badiur also disclosed that he purchased the suit property from Raisa and he would not transfer it to him, unless he pays an amount of Taka 25,00,000. Then, on search he found out that Badiur has created a forged sale deed on 15-1-1982 and has been claiming the suit property through it illegally. 

 8. Title Suit No.364 of 1982 was subse-quently, transferred to the trial court and renumbered as Title Suit No.113 of 1984. 

 Khadiza Islam's case as plaintiff in Title Suit No.224 of 1997 (original Title Suit No.75 of 1996) and defendants of other suits 

 9. Khadiza, defendant No.7 of Title Suit No.483 of 1974, as sole plaintiff, filed Title Suit No.75 of 1996 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on 27-4-1996 impleading Md Waziuddin, Jamila, Salauddin, Mobarak Hossain, Noor Mohammad Khan and Bangladesh as defendant Nos.1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 respectively for cancellation of sale deed No.4722 dated 30-11-1982 obtained through Court by Md Waziuddin as well as for declaration of her right, title to and interest in the suit property and also for recovery of khan possession thereof by evicting Md Waziuddin therefrom and permanent injunction upon Md Waziuddin not to transfer the suit property to anyone stating that Raisa left the suit property under lock and key in the wake of liberation war of Bangladesh and in her absence, some miscreants took over possession thereof. The Government erroneously included the suit property in the list of abandoned property. However, on Raisa's application, the Government released the suit property on 12-1-1982 and handed over possession thereof to her. Then Raisa transferred the suit property to Badiur by a registered deed of sale dated 15-1-1982 in pursuance of an agreement dated 11-9-1969 and delivered possession to him. He got his name mutated and then with the permission of the Government sold it to Khadiza for a sum of Taka 10,00,000 by a registered deed of sale dated 4-9-1984. Badiur also delivered vacant possession of the suit property to her after execution of sale deed. She, after renewal of the lease deed from Government, had been in possession thereof till 5-5-1993, by using it as storage of construction materials of her construction company namely, Nirman Construction Company Limited (shortly, Nirman). Md Waziuddin (Waziuddin) disposses-sed her therefrom through Court on 5-5-1993 in Title Execution Case No.6 of 1992 arising out of the judgment and decree in First Appeal No.23 of 1984 arising out of Title Suit No.541 of 1982. Khadiza Islam was neither a party to Title Suit No.541 of 1982 nor in First Appeal No.23 of 1984 and she had no knowledge about the suit or appeal. Khadiza and the Managing Director of Nirman filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal (CPLA) No.195 of 1993 before the Appellate Division against the judgment and decree of First Appeal, but it was rejected as not being pressed. Thereafter, Khadiza filed the suit. In the plaint, it was further stated that according to the decree of First Appeal No.23 of 1984, Waziuddin was to deposit the balance consideration money within ninety days from the date of judgment and decree failing which the suit would stand dismissed. Waziuddin deposited the balance consideration money on 12-2-1992 by Challan No.24047, which was beyond the period of ninety days and, as such, the said suit stood dismissed but the execution case was filed on the basis of an inoperative decree and Khadiza was dispossessed from the suit property illegally. This suit on transferred to the trial court and was renumbered as Title Suit No.224 of 1997. 

 Title Suit No.112 of 1984 Plaintiffs-Salau-ddin and Mobarak's case 

 10. Plaintiffs Salauddin and Mobarak also filed Title Suit No.436 of 1982 before the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract against Raisa, relating to the suit property. The suit was transferred to the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka i.e. the trial court and renumbered as Title Suit No.112 of 1984. They claimed specific performance of contract relating the suit property on the basis of an agreement of sale dated 4-5-1979 with Raisa. 

 Written statement case of defendant No.1 Md Waziuddin in Title Suit No.224 of 1997 

 11. It needs be mentioned that previously in the year 1997, one Waziuddin filed Title Suit No.541 of 1982 before the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract against Raisa on the basis of an oral agreement for sale of the suit property. The said suit was dismissed. Then Waziuddin filed First Appeal No.23 of 1984 before the High Court Division and the said appeal was allowed and the suit was decreed. 'Thereafter, Waziuddin got the sale deed registered through Court on 30-11-1992 and in execution of the said decree got possession of the suit property. Whereupon, Khadiza filed CPLA No.195 of 1993 before this Division against the said judgment and decree but it was dismissed as not pressed by Khadiza. Subsequently, Khadiza, as plaintiff, filed TS No. 224 of 1997 challenging the said judgment and decree of Waziuddin as discussed hereinbefore. 

 12. Raisa filed written statement on 10-8-1976 denying all the allegations made in the plaint of Title Suit No.483 of 1974 and stating that she was not acquainted with Jamila and she did not enter into any agreement for sale with Jamila and that Jamila filed the suit with forged and created Bainapatra/agreement for sale and so, the suit is liable to be dismissed. However, Raisa eventually did not contest the suit. 

 14. The Government as defendant of Title Suit Nos. 483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984, and 66 of 1990 contested the suits by filing separate written statements denying all material allegations made in the plaints of the aforesaid suits. However, the Government admitted part of plaint case of Title Suit No.224 of 1997 filed by Khadiza. In the written statements the Govern-ment stated, inter alia, that original owner and possessor of the suit property was Norendra Mohan Sen by virtue of a long term lease granted by the then Secretary of the State for India Council through registered deed dated 24-4-1924. While Remendra Sen was in physical possession of the suit property, he transferred his lease-hold interest to Aswimi Kumar Bhowmik, who subsequently transferred the same to Raisa by Deed No.8497 dated 11-12-1957. Raisa being a non-bengali Urdu speaking person abandoned the suit property during liberation war. She was not traceable after liberation. So, the suit property was legally declared as abandoned property and some persons including the plaintiffs of the suits were trying to grab the suit property by creating forged bainapatra, deeds, etc. 

 Issues, trial and decisions in Title Suit Nos. 483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984, 66 of 1990 and 224 of 1997. 

 16. The following issues were framed by the trial courts together for deciding the merit of Title Suit Nos.483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984, 66 of 1990 and 224 of 1997, as the suits were being tried analogously. 

 17. The plaintiff of Title Suit Nos.483 of 1974 and 66 of 1990-cum-defendants of some other suits examined five witnesses in support of her case and they were cross-examined by the various defendants-cum-plaintiffs of some other suits. The defendants-cum-plaintiffs of some other suits examined totally fifteen witnesses in support of their respective cases, who were cross-examined by the contesting parties. The witnesses also produced some documents and those were marked as exhibits by the trial Court. 

 18. The trial Court on examination of the evidence on record by the common judgment and decree/order dated 18-8-2009 dismissed in Title Suit Nos.483 of 1974, 112 of 1984, 113 of 1984, 224 of 1997 and 66 of 1990 on contest against the contesting defendants and ex-parte against the rest. 

 19. Jamila filed Title Appeal Nos.454 of 2009 and 455 of 2009 before the High Court Division. The said appeals on transfer were re-numbered as Transfer Appeal (TA) Nos.09 of 2004 and 10 of 2004. 

 "In the result, the FA No.167 of 2010, TA No.7 of 2014, TA No.9 of 2014, TA No.10 of 2014 and TA No.11 of 2014 are dismissed without any order as to costs. The Transfer Appeal No.6 of 2014 arising out of Title Suit No.224 of 1997 is hereby allowed and the Title Suit No.224 of 1997 is decreed. The impugned Judgment and decree so far as it relates to Title Suit No.224 of 1997 is set-aside. The appellant of TA No.11 of 2014 is directed to handover vacant possession of the suit property in favour of Khadiza Islam, appellant of TA No.8 of 2014 within 6 (six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment, in default, the appellant TA No.8 of 2014 is at liberty to get possession of the same through process of law." 

 (I) Because, the High Court Division has committed a manifest error of law in not considering the evidences and materials on record adduced from the side of the plaintiff in Title Suit No.113 of 1984 and also judgment of the trial Court, particularly when the trial Court itself failed to consider those evidence and materials on record while dismissing the aforesaid Title Suit No.113 of 1984. and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree warrants interference by this court and therefore, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

 (IV) Because, the High Court Division misdirected itself in law in decreeing the respondent's Title Suit No. 224 of 1997 without considering the petitioners' case that the plaintiff-respondent purchased the schedule suit land with prior notice of the contract for sale (bainapatra) dated 23-4-1969, exhibit-B, executed by defendant No.1, the original owner of the schedule suit land in favour of the petitioners' predecessor, namely, Noor Mohammad Khan, the original plaintiff and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside." 

 Appellant of Civil Appeal No.30 of 2017 and Petitioner of CPLA No.4232 of 2018 (Plaintiff of Title Suit Nos.483 of 1974 and 66 of 1990 and defendants of other suits) 

 i) Jamila Khatun examined several witnesses to prove her case for specific performance of contract as well as cancellation of the deed of transfer infavour of Khadiza and lease renewal document in Khadiza's favour. She also produced the original bainapatra which is a document of more than 30 years old and submitted before the court from the custody of the proper person claiming the suit property. The witnesses of Jamila proved the case of execution of bainapatra by Raisa, admitted lease holder. The bainapatra was also proved through Ashfaq Ahmed (husband of Jamila) and other three witnesses. 

 iv) Raisa never sold the property to Badiur and the document of alleged sale by Raisa was a forged document and that is why Khadiza did not produce the original deed of such sale to Badiur by Raisa. Khadiza claimed that all the original documents were/are lying with her but she did not produce the most vital document of alleged sale by Raisa to Badiur as it was a forged document. The trial court legally dismissed the suit of Khadiza but the High Court Division allowed the appeal of Khadiza and decreed the suit in favour of Khadiza unlawfully without considering that the original deed of alleged transfer of the suit property by Raisa in favour of Badiur was not produced before the courts below. 

 Appellant of Civil Appeal No.31 of 2017 (Plaintiff of Title Suit No.364 of 1982 renumbered as Title Suit No.113 of 1984 and defendants of other suits) 

 28. Mr Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, the learned Senior Advocate for the heirs of Khan in Civil Appeal No.31 of 2017 takes us through the original bainapatra dated 23-7-1969 allegedly executed by Raisa in favour of Khan, legal notice dated 21-1-1977 allegedly issued by Raisa to Khan through her learned Advocate cancelling Bainapatra dated 23-7-1969, the agreement dated 1-5-77 i.e. the alleged Novation deed between Raisa and Khan, the other evidence on record and put forward the following arguments before us: 

 4) Khadiza, Badiur, Jamila and others crcated some fraudulent bainapatra/deed of sale, etc. after liberation with the knowledge about original agreement between Khan and Raisa. 

 5) Khadiza did not produce the original document of alleged sale to Badiur by Raisa as it was a forged document. Moreover, Badiur himself was a witness of the agreements of Raisa with Khan. 

 8) The trial court considering all the facts dismissed the suit of Khadiza but the appellate court without considering the material evidence on record erroneously allowed the appeal filed by Khadiza and decreed the suit in her favour. Therefore, the judgment and decree allowing Transfer Appeal No.8 of 2014 and decreeing Title Suit No.224 of 1997 are liable to be set aside and the judgment and decree of dismissal by the trial court of the suit is liable to be restored. 

 9) Khan's heir proved the agreement of sale by Raisa with Khan by a series of documents marked as exhibits by the trial court since the year 1969, long before liberation and by examining witnesses. So, suit filed by Khan (Title Suit No.113 of 1984) is liable to be decreed in their favour. 

 Appellant of Civil Appeal No. 32 of 2017 (Plaintiff of Title Suit No. 364 of 1982 renumbered as Title Suit No.113 of 1984 and defendants of other suits) 

 29. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate for the heirs of Khan in Civil Appeal No. 32 of 2017 adapts the arguments of Mr Nozrul Islam Chowdhury and adds that Nuru Miah as a witness of the novation dated 1-5-1977 proved deed of novation executed by Raisa apart from other witnesses. Khan also filed Title Suit No. 364 of 1982 on 20-7-1982, it was renumbered Title Suit No. 113 of 1984. Therefore, the suit was also filed by Khan long before the alleged purchase of the property by Khadiza. He next submits that Khan's heirs are entitled to have a decree for specific performance of contract as all other claimants to the suit property are bound by the contract, which was executed earlier on 23-7-1969, under section 27B of the Specific Relief Act. Therefore, Civil Appeal No. 32 of 2017 is liable to be allowed and the suit filed by Khadiza is liable to be dismissed by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division in Transfer Appeal No. 8 of 2014. 

 (Plaintiff of Title Suit No.224 of 1997, original Title Suit No.75 of 1996 and defendants of other suits) 

 32. Mr Murad Reza, the learned Additional Attorney-General with the leave of the Court appearing on behalf of the Government in all the appeals and the CPLA takes us through the materials on record, specially the original record/ file of abandoned property authority since middle of the year 1977, and submits as under: 

 1) It is clear from the record of abandoned property authority that once the prayer for releasing the suit property by alleged Raisa Aziz Begum was rejected by the Government, considering all the facts and circumstances of the case. The original file relating to the suit property from the beginning of 1972 up to part of 1977 was not traceable and missing. 

 3) Many documents in connection with this case were also seized by CID and now they are not traceable. Similarly, it is noted in the file that original file were sent to the then learned Government Pleader, but the said original file was not traceable and the learned Government Pleader denied to have received any such file. 

 4) The original alleged deed of sale by Raisa to Badiur was neither produced before the abandoned property authority/ Dhaka collectorate i.e. Khas Mohal property management authority nor in the Court by Khadiza in support of her case. She has not also filed the said most important document in any other court or Government authority. This clearly proves that Raisa did not sale/transfer her lease-hold right to the suit property to Badiur or anyone else. 

 6) Even if the suit property is released from the list of abandoned property, the suit property is a Government khas mohal property. Khadiza could not produce the original documents of alleged sale by Raisa to Badiur and, therefore, she was not entitled to extend the leasehold right as Raisa never transferred the property to Badiur. 

 7) As the original deed of purchase by Badiur could not be produced, Khadiza miserably failed to prove her title to or leasehold right to the suit property. Therefore, the subsequent extension of lease by Khadiza is exfacie collusive, illegal and void. 

 34. The suit property is the khas Mohal property of the Government vide plaint and the schedule of the plaint of Title Suit No.112 of 1984 filed by Khadiza. Norendra Mohan Sen (Norendra) was a long term lessee under the Government by virtue of a long term lease granted by the then Secretary of State of India Council through a registered deed. Norendra transferred his leasehold right to Aswini Kumar Bhowmik (Aswini) and Aswini transferred his leasehold right to Raisa by a registered deed dated 11-12-1957 vide judgments of the trial Court and the High Court Division, testimonies of DW 1 and other witnesses and the materials on record. Khan's heirs claim that Norendra was the owner of the suit property and he transferred it Aswini by a registered deed. Aswini then transferred the suit property to Raisa by a registered deed dated 11-12-1957. However, during their arguments before us, the learned Senior Advocates/ Advocates for all the contending parties admitted that the suit property is the Khas Mohal property of the Government and Raisa was a long term lessee under the Government. The suit property bearing Holding No.10 is situated at Purana Paltan, Dhaka i.e. at the heart of Capital and is a valuable property. All the plaintiffs of respective suits claimed the suit property through Raisa. Raisa was a non-bengali. So, immediately before liberation of Bangladesh, Raisa left the suit property. Whereupon, the suit property was declared as an abandoned property and was enlisted in the list of abandoned properties. The suit property being enlisted as an abandoned property was included in the `ka' list of the abandoned properties published in the Gazette Notification. But subsequently it was dropped from the list of abandoned properties by another Gazette Notification. It was released on prayer of a person allegedly claiming herself to be Raisa, the leaseholder of the suit property. 

 37. Khadiza filed a suit for declaration of her 16 annas title to the suit property, recovery of khas possession, perpetual injunction and some other relief. Therefore, we would first examine how far Khadiza has been able to prove her title to the suit property. 

 ৬। How can it be determined if they are old tenants or not without the original file ? The file from LC may be brought such for the purpose. 

 31. Minutes at para 30/N ante prepage bottom may kindly be seen. The original file as is already indicated under para 26/N ante was sent to the Court in connection with the suit (483/1974) for specific performance of contract. The alleged suit was brought by one Mrs. Jamila Khatoon for breach of contract by Mrs. Raisa Aziz Begum, the claimant of the property at 10, Purana Paltan. As the original file is missing the memo No. 1-E-52/72/296 dt. 20-5-76 is not available in the Ministry now. It appears that the previous petition was rejected because of the above mentioned suit in which this Ministry is not involved anyway. Further this suit reveals that the applicant Raisa Aziz Begum is the defecto owner of the, property in question. Being asked by this Ministry the papers submitted by Mrs. Raisa Aziz bear testimony that she is the original owner of the property at 10, Purana Paltan. Dacca, Now at this stage in pursuance of Article 16(2) of the PO 16/72, the property at 10. Purana Paltan, Dacca may be dropped from AP list in favour of Mrs. Raisa Aziz Begum, 

 32. Let us wait for the original file. 

 34. Receipt at pages 104-109/C received from Raisa Aziz Begum regarding her claim on the property at 10, Purana Paltan may kindly be seen. In this connection preceding notes from 25/N ante detailing the issue may also kindly be perused. As to the observation under para 32/N ante prepage bottom, it is already indicated under paras 12/N and 13/N ante that the original file is neither available in Ministry nor in the office of the CJP. In the office of the CJP extensive search was made in my presence, but the file was not found and there is little possibility of its availability as it is missing since 1974. Now in consideration of the papers made available by Raisa Aziz Begum in support of her right of claim on the property in question and the exposition made under para 31/N ante, the property at 10, Purana Paltan may be dropped from the AP list. 

 37. Minutes at para 35/N ante prepage bottom. In this connection page 110/C and the submission made by Raisa Aziz Begum may kindly be seen at page 112/C. It appears that Mrs. Raisa Aziz Begum has been claiming the title of ownership on the property at 10, Purana Paltan since 1972 and has been pursuing it continuously as it appears from the instant representation. Now in pursuance of the expectation made under para 34/N ante and the Article 16(2) of P.0.16/72, the property at 10, Purana Paltan may be dropped from the AP list. 

 a) The original file of abandoned property relating to the suit property is not traceable/missing for the period starting from 1972 up to part of 1977. 

 42. It be mentioned that the original deed of alleged transfer of the suit property dated 15-1-1982 by Raisa to Badiur was neither produced before the abandoned property authority nor before any Government Office or before any Court. 

 43. Khadiza had tried to establish a new case by examining DW 1 Awlad Hossain Chowdhury, a witness who deposed on her behalf. This witness stated that the original document of transfer by Raisa to Badiur is deposited with a bank at the time of marking a certified copy of the deed as exhibit vi(a) with objection. But this witness at the time of marking exhibit .4i (e) did not mention the name of the bank. He also stated that Nirman took loan from the bank after 1984 without mentioning the date of taking loan. 

 44. Further, the Bank Officer, DW 3 Kazi Md Adam All stated that the loan was taken from the bank, the present name of which is Eastern Bank Ltd and earlier known as BCCI Bank. From statement of this witness it also appears that he brought a certified copy and a photocopy was submitted before the Court and not the original. one. DW 3 the Bank Official did not say that the original deed was missing from the bank. Moreover, no other documentary evidence was/is placed before the Court to show that the original document was missing and that any action was taken by Khadiza over missing of this document by the bank or by any other means. 

 45. At the time of hearing, this Court inquired about the whereabouts of this original document and Khadiza's learned Senior Advocate replied that the original document is missing from the bank. 

 46. Therefore, it appears that Khadiza allegedly mortgaged the suit property for the purpose of taking loan from a bank but neither the mortgaged deed nor the original document was ever produced before the court or the Government authorities. The new case about mortgage of suit property to the bank is beyond pleadings as no such case was mentioned in the plaint, even by way of amendment. It appears that Khadiza suppressed a vital information in the plaint and did not bring this new case in the plaint by way of amendment. Perhaps it is due to the fact that she did not obtain any permission from the Government before mortgaging the suit property to the bank and that too by using a fictitious document. It is evident that Khadiza intentionally avoided to produce original document so that Raisa's signature could not be compared. 

 48. In consideration of the original file of abandoned property authority and non-production of the original deed of so-called transfer by Raisa to Badiur, we are fully convinced that Raisa never sold/transfer the suit property to Badiur for which the original document was not produced before the Government authorities or in any Court. Further, Khadiza claimed that her leasehold right was extended for 30 years but she prayed for declaration of her 16 annas title to the suit property again as a fraudulent device to grab the Government valuable property by practicing fraud upon the Court. 

 54. It be mentioned that the original file of abandoned property was/is not traceable/missing till date. The said file contained all notes and all records/documents from 1972 up to part of the year 1977. Thus, whether Raisa is a genuine person or not that could not be ascertained as all the documents containing her original signatures from 1972 up to part of 1977 are missing from the record. Therefore, the so called Raisa might be a fake person. Possibly, for that reason she was not examined as a witness in the court by Khadiza or any other parties in the suits. 

 65. We have already seen that Khadiza failed to prove her vendor's title/leasehold right to the suit property and, as such, the extension of lease in her favour by certain unscrupulous Govern-ment officials is also collusive and fraudulent. However, Khadiza's illegal extended lease period for 30 years has also expired meanwhile. 

 67. In the facts and circumstances, as discussed hereinbefore, we are of the view that the trial court correctly dismissed the suit filed by Khadiza so far as it relates to declaration of her right, title to the suit property, khas possession and permanent injunction. However, the High Court Division erroneously held that Raisa with the permission of the Government transferred the suit property to Badiur although Government witness DW 15 Md Mousur Rahman in cross-examination clearly stated,— 

 68. High Court Division without considering the evidence as discussed hereinbefore, erroneously allowed Khadiza's appeal as a whole, but curiously enough without declaring any title to or leasehold right of Khadiza in the suit property but simply directing Waziuddin to handover possession of the suit property to Khadiza within 6 months from the date of receiving copy of the judgment. 

 71. Noor Mohammad filed Title Suit No.364 of 1982, renumbered as 113 of 1984, for Specific Performance of Contract against Raisa on the basis of a Bainapatra dated 23-7-1969 as well as a deed of novation dated 10-7-1972, renewing the previous agreement for sale. He also prayed for khas possession of the suit property. Khan's heirs examined several witnesses to substantiate their case. 

 81. Thus, it appears that this witness has not seen Raisa on any other day except one day and on the date of execution of bainapatra dated 23-7-1969, he did not see her full face. So, evidence of this witness that Raisa Aziz herself executed the original Binapatra is of no value, as he did not know Raisa, who was a pardansin lady according to the previous witness Bidhan Chandra. 

 82. Moreover, in the original Bainapatra, signature of Raisa is in Urdu but in the deed of renewal of agreement all the signatures are in English. No reason was mentioned by the witnesses as to why the signatures in the deed of novation were in English. The money receipts could not also be proved in this suit. 

 83. In the above circumstances, it is crystal clear that the witnesses of this suit could not prove that the original Bainapatra was executed by Raisa herself for the reasons discussed earlier. 

 84. Thus, it is evident that Noor Moham-mad's heirs failed to prove that it was Raisa who executed the original Bainapatra on 23-7-1969. Since, the case of execution of original Bainapatra by Raisa falls through, the case of novation as continuity of the original Bainapatra is of no value. 

 87. Now let us examine the merit of the appeal filed by Jamila Khatun, which arose out of Transfer Appeal No.10 of 2014 and the said appeal arose out of Title Suit No.483 of 1974. 

 99. On the other hand, Jamila Khatun filed Title Suit No.66 of 1990 for cancellation of sale deed as well as lease extension deed in favour of Khadiza. The said suit as well as the appeal being Transfer Appeal No.10 of 2014, were both dismissed by the trial Court and the appellate Court respectively. Wherefrom, Jamila filed CPLA No.4232 of 2018. The suits for Specific Performance of Contract filed by Noor Mohammad (being dead his heirs) and by Jamila were dismissed and the appeals against the said judgments and decrees were disallowed. We have also found no merit in Civil Appeal No.31 of 2017 and Civil Appeal No.30 of 2017. 

 100. Ordinarily, in such scenario, it is not necessary to consider the appeal of the heirs of Noor Mohammad Khan and the CPLA of Jam ila but for the observations and decisions made hereinbefore on Khadiza's case, we find that Khadiza miserably failed to prove her valid title to or leasehold right in the suit property. As Khadiza failed to prove her case and Waziuddin is not now in the picture, it is necessary to consider the merit of Civil Appeal No.32 of 2017 and CPLA No. 4232 of 2018 in the unusual facts of the matters. 

 101. We have already seen that Khadiza could not prove her case and, therefore, she was not entitled to have a decree in her favour and the trial Court correctly dismissed it, but her appeal was erroneously allowed by the High Court Division with decree of khas possession. Therefore, her suit for declaration of her 16 annas title to the suit property, recovery of possession and permanent injunction have to be dismissed due to the reasons as discussed. However, if Khadiza's suit is dismissed as a whole, in such case Waziuddin's decree for Specific Performance of Contract would come into operation. Therefore, it is necessary to decide whether the decree in favour of Waziuddin is liable to be set aside for doing complete justice. 

 104. Thus, it appears that out of 4 witnesses, 3 witnesses of the money receipt are dead and he does not know the whereabouts of the other witness. About the oral agreement, the money receipt was the most important evidence, but Waziuddin failed to prove it by any independent witness. So, it appears that Waziuddin as defendant-appellant failed to prove that Raisa had entered into an oral agreement with him to transfer the suit property in his favour. Therefore, his suit being Title Suit No.541 of 1982 was legally dismissed by the trial Court but the High Court Division in FA No.283 of 1984 erroneously decreed the suit against Raisa for Specific Performance of Contract. As a result, Waziuddin got possession of the suit property through Court. 

 111. As the unlawful lease extension in favour of Khadiza expired meanwhile, we are of the view that Khadiza Islam is not entitled to get any further extension of her lease from the Government. She had no legal right for extension of Raisa's leasehold right at any time. We are further of the view that the Government must take over actual/physical possession of the suit property from Waziuddin/ Khadiza/ the persons/ person, whoever be in possession thereof within 60 days from the date of receiving the copy of this judgment in its present condition. 

 (5) Khadiza Islam would not be entitled to get Khas possession from Md Waziuddin and she would not be entitled to retain possession in the suit property, if there be any, by whatever means. 

 (6) Government Khas Mohal Authority shall takeover physical possession of the suit property presently measuring more or less 12 khatas of land with structures thereon of Holding No.10, Purana Paltan, Dhaka, Plot No.1184, Khatian No.217, present Mouza-Ramna, Old Dag Nos.26, 27 and 28 vide statement of witnesses and plaint of Title Suit No.224 of 1997 (Khadiza Islam vs Waziuddin), within 60 days from the date of receiving copy of this judgment from Md Wazi-uddin/Khadiza lslam-Nirman Cons-truction/any person/persons, in posses-sion of the suit property in its present condition and retain its possession in accordance with law.
