caseno: Civil Appeal Nos. 35 of 1997 and 36 of 1997.
parties:
Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka ------ Plaintiff-Appellant
Vs.
Abdur Rab, constituted Attorney of Zamila Khatun and ors Defendant ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Civil Appeal No. 35 of 1997, is from the judgment and order dated 19-6-96 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 175 of 1996 discharging the Rule and refusing thereby to interfere with the order dated 6-1-96 passed by a Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 19 of 1995 rejecting the appellant's prayer to stay further proceeding of the said execution case pending disposal of Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 (originally numbered as Title Suit No. 294 of 1982) of the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka. 

 3. Civil Appeal No. 36 of 1997, has arisen from the judgment and order dated 18-6-96 passed by the above mentioned same Bench of the High Court Division, in Civil Revision No. 3532 of 1995 making the Rule absolute and setting aside thereby the judgment and order dated 12-8-95 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1995, under Order 9, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, allowing the same and restoring thereby the aforesaid Title Suit No. 210 of 1991, which was dismissed for default on 4-6-94. 

 Late Al-haj Duliluddin Ahmed (died on 6-2-82), the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant-respondents of both the appeals instituted on 8-9-78 Title Suit No. 243 of 1978 in the court of then Munsif, 6th Court, now Assistant Judge, Dhaka for khas possession of the suit premises, against the custodian of vested property as defendant No. 1 and the present plaintiff-appellant, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, as defendant No. 2 alleging, inter alia, that on 26-12-61 he has auction purchased, in a certificate case under the Public Demands Recovery Act, the suit properties comprising of Municipal Holding Nos. 26 and 26/1, Kali Charan Shaha Road, within Sutrapur police station, District Dhaka. The auction sale was confirmed on 9-9-66 and formal symbolical possession was given to him on 22-7-71. But the defendants illegally kept the suit property under their possession. The suit was decreed ex parte on 3-6-80. The decree-holder then filed Title Execution Case No. 14 of 1981. The present appellant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1981, under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the said ex-parte decree, which, however, was dismissed for default on 15-6-81 and then his application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the said Miscellaneous case was also rejected on 27-2- 82. One MA Khaleque, who claimed himself as a monthly tenant in respect of the suit premises under the present appellant, on 11-5-81 instituted Title Suit No. 509 of 1981 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration that the aforesaid ex-parte decree was illegal, void, etc. making the present appellant as well as the Government of Bangladesh as defendant No. 5 and 3 respectively and on 13-7-81 got an order of temporary injunction restraining the decree-holder-respondent from proceeding with the said title execution case pending disposal of the suit. The suit was dismissed and the same was maintained by the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 10-3-83 passed in Civil Revision No. 116 of 1982. On 26-6-82 the present appellant filed Title Suit No. 294 of 1982, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 210 of 1991, for setting aside the aforesaid ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 243 of 1987 and the same was dismissed for default on 4-6-94. Against which the appellant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1994, renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 1995, under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit alleging, inter that on 4-6-94 the learned Advocate had been engaged in another court and accordingly, he filed an application for adjournment but the court dismissed the suit before noon without considering the prayer for adjournment. 

 5. The defendant-respondents opposed the aforesaid miscellaneous case by filing a written objection contending, inter alia, that the suit itself being barred by the principle of res-judicata the miscellaneous case was not maintainable as the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 243 of 1978 had already reached its finality and conclusiveness against the plaintiff, because of dismissal of his Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1981, filed under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the said decree and rejection of his subsequent application filed under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such, in view of the final, conclusive and binding character of the said ex parte decree upon the parties, if the Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 is restored the defendants will be driven to fruitless litigation and unnecessary harassment. It was also alleged that the Misc. Case had been brought upon making absolutely false statements that the plaintiff's concerned Advocate had been engaged on 4-6-94 in another court in connection with another case and that the plaintiff was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing in the suit when the same was taken up for hearing. 

 7. Upon hearing the parties the learned Subordinate Judge allowed the said Miscellaneous case by his judgment and order dated 12-8-95 and accordingly, Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 was restored to its original file and number. 

 8. The aggrieved respondents then moved the High Court Division in revision, and obtained Rule, Civil Revision No. 3532 of 1995. A learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 18-6-96 upon making the Rule absolute reversed the judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge and dismissed the Miscellaneous case holding, inter alia, that the plaintiff could not prove that he had been prevented by sufficient cause from not appearing in court when the suit was called on for hearing and that in the facts and circumstances of the case restoration of Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 would lead the parties to a fruitless litigation. Against the said judgment of the High Court Division Civil Appeal No. 36 of 1997 has been preferred. 

 9. The plaintiff-appellant also filed an application in the court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Execution Case No. 19 of 1995 (original execution case was Title Execution Case No. 14 of 1981) to stay its further proceeding till disposal of the aforesaid Title Suit No. 210 of 1991. But the same was rejected on 6-1-96. Against which the plaintiff moved the High Court Division and obtained another Rule, Civil Revision No. 175 of 1996. By a separate judgment dated 18-6-96 the same learned Judge of the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding, inter alia, that in view of his decision given in the other Rule, noted earlier, the latter Rule became infructuous, which has given rise to Civil Appeal No. 35 of 1997. 

 10. In connection with Civil Appeal No. 36 of 1997 leave was granted to consider whether the learned Singled Judge of the High Court Division was justified in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 1995 without setting aside the findings of fact arrived by the learned Subordinate Judge that on the date fixed for hearing of Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 the plaintiff had sufficient cause for his non-appearance and that whether the learned Judge did consider the evidence and materials brought on record in the said Misc. Case and that whether the learned Judge has travelled beyond his revisional jurisdiction upon tracing the history of litigation between the parties in passing the impugned Judgment and that whether the learned Judge by terming the appellant's suit as a "fruitless litigation" has condemned appellant and sealed the fate of the suit without hearing its merit. 

 12. Mr. Shahidul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant in both the appeals, submitted that the learned trial Judge on consideration of the evidence of PWs 1-2, OPW 1 and the documentary evidence namely, Ext. 1, the copy of the application for adjournment of hearing of the suit, Ext. 2 the case diary of the plaintiff''s advocate, Ext. 3, the gazette notification that the suit premises is a recorded evacuee property, held that the plaintiff had sufficient cause for his non-appearance in court on 4-6-94 and that for the dismissal of the suit for default the plaintiff suffered irreparable loss. Accordingly, the learned trial Judge allowed the Misc. Case set aside the order of dismissal of the suit for default and restored the same to its original file and number. Mr Alam then submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted illegally beyond his revisional jurisdiction by superimposing his appreciation of evidence in reversing the judgment of the trial Court without even reversing the finding of fact of the trial Courts, as noted above. The learned Advocate further submitted that the trial judge in consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record rightly held that whether Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 is maintainable or not and whether the same has been brought to harass the defendant will be considered by the trial Court itself upon the evidence to be adduced by the parties in support of their respective cases but in the disposal of a proceeding under Order 9 rule 13, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has travelled beyond his jurisdiction in holding that the said title suit is a "fruitless litigation" and thereby has, in fact, condemned the plaintiff and prejudged the fate of the suit before being heard on merit. The learned Advocate also submitted that the learned Single Judge upon misapplication of the decision reported in 1989 BLD (AD) 1, Sanatannessa Bewa vs Hipatullah Sarker & ors misdirected himself in holding that the decree dated 3-6-80 of Title Suit No. 243 of 1978 having already become final and conclusive the plaintiff's Title Suit 210 of 1991 is nothing but a fruitless litigation. 

 14. Mr Rab, thus, submitted that the learned judge of the High Court Division on consideration of the above mentioned materials on record rightly held that the trial Court had failed to apply its judicial mind on the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record in holding that the plaintiff could prove that he had been prevented by sufficient cause from appearing at the time of hearing of the suit, and, as such, the learned Judge is justified in holding that the impugned order having suffered from legal infirmity the same was not sustainable in law. Mr. Rab further submitted that the trial judge himself in his order No. 87 dated 4-6-94 noted that after the order of dismissal of the suit for default had been passed, the plaintiff at about 12-30 PM filed an application for time, which fact negative the case of the plaintiff that after filing the application for time PW 1 went to another court to conduct another case and that without disposing of the time petition, the trial Court wrongly dismissed the suit for default. Mr. Rab also submitted that there being no scope of preferring an appeal against the order of allowing an application under Order 9 rule 9 CPC the High Court Division, in the instant case with a view to preventing the causing of injustice, in its revisional jurisdiction has rightly considered the above noted materials on record in holding that the trial Court had failed to apply its judicial mind in allowing the Misc. Case. Mr. Rab lastly, submitted that in consideration of the finality and conclusiveness of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 243 of 1978 the High Court Division held in Civil Revision No. 116 of 1982, arising out of the Title Suit No. 509 of 1981, instituted by one MA Khaleque impleading the present appellant as a defendant, that the said suit was not maintainable and as such, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in the instant case has rightly relied upon the principles of law enunciated in 1989 BLD (AD) 1 in holding that the restoration of Title Suit No. 201 of 1991 will drive the parties to a fruitless litigation. 

 15. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge after taking note of all the relevant facts on record and believing the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 upon assigning reasons therefor and on consideration of Exts. 1, 2, 3 held that the plaintiff had sufficient cause for his failure to appear in Court on 4-6-94 and thereby the suit in question was dismissed for default and he also suffered loss for dismissal of the suit. In passing the impugned judgment the learned Subordinate Judge also took note of the impugned ex parte decree, which has been challenged in Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 and rightly held that whether the said title suit is a fruitless litigation or not and whether it is barred by the principle of res judicata will be decided by the trial Court after hearing the same on merit upon the evidence to be adduced by the parties. In that view of the matter the learned Subordinate Judge in the interest of justice restored the suit for setting aside the order of dismissal for default. 

 For the reasons recorded earlier we find substance in these appeals. Accordingly, both the appeals are allowed without any order as to costs. The judgments appealed from are set aside. In consequence thereof the trial Court's order of restoration of Title Suit No. 210 of 1991 be restored and further proceeding of the Title Execution Case No. 19 of 1995 pending in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka be stayed pending disposal of the aforesaid title suit.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury

parties:
Government of Bangladesh ----- Appellant
vs. 
Ashraf Ali @ Ashraf Ali and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Writ Petitioner-respondent No. 1's house at Holding No. 10-A/9-8, Mirpur was enlisted in the "Ka" list of Abandoned Buildings vide notification in the Bangladesh Gazette Extraordinary dated 23rd September, 1986. His case is that, the disputed building originally belonged to one Md. Yahiya who had acquired it by way of perpetual lease granted by the erstwhile Government of East Pakistan on 10-8-62 under a registered deed of lease. Md Yahiya possessed the disputed building and then died in 1970 leaving son Md. Nasim as his only heir. Md. Nasim was a national and permanent resident of Bangladesh and he used to possess the disputed building. Md. Nasim contracted to sell the disputed building on 18-1-72 to respondent No. 1 for a consideration of Taka 8,000.00 and after receiving the entire consideration money sold the disputed building to respondent No. 1 by executing a registered deed of sale on 10-9-73. Respondent No.1 got possession in the disputed building and had been in possession therein. He is also a national and permanent resident of Bangladesh and that neither he nor his vendor Md. Nasim ever ceased to possess, occupy, supervise or manage the disputed building. Respondent No. 1 leased the disputed building to one. Md. Sayed as a monthly tenant on 15-4-74. While in possession Md. Sayed was dispossessed by the Government and the disputed building was leased out to one Abdul Hakim Sarder, an employee of an Insurance Company. Respondent No. 1 submitted various representations to the Government and finally filed the case before the Court of Settlement. 

 3. Bangladesh entered appearance and contested the Writ Petition by filing an affidavit in-opposition supported by another supplementary affidavit-in opposition contending that the original owner Md. Yahiya left Bangladesh for Pakistan with members of his family some time in the year 1970 and his whereabouts were not known when President's Order No. 16 of 1972 came into operation. Md. Nasim was neither the son of Md Yahiya nor the owner of the disputed building. Md. Nasim never possessed the disputed building as he had no interest therein. Respondent No. 1 fraudulently obtained the sale deed from the said Md. Nasim and claimed the disputed building as his own. As the whereabouts of the original owner Md Yahiya were not known and as he had failed to possess, occupy, manage or supervise the disputed building when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation the disputed building became abandoned property under the provision of President's Order 16 of 1972 and vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and, as such, the enlistment of the disputed building in the "ka" list of abandoned buildings has been done in accordance with law. 

 5. The Court of Settlement found on consideration of the materials on record that respondent No. 1 could not provide any date of death of original allottee, Md Yahiya save and except asserting that he died in 1970. Respondent No.1 could not also produce any certificate from anywhere relating to the death of Yahiya in 1970. The Court of Settlement also found that respondent No.1 could not produce any document in support of his contention that Md. Nasim was the only son and legal heir of the lessee Md Yahiya. The positive finding of the Court of Settlement was that there was no evidence that Yahiya died in 1970 in Bangladesh and Md. Nasim was his only heir. Apart from those above factual determinations, the Court of Settlement found that Respondent No. 1 could not rebut the presumption attached to the property that it is an abandoned property as per section 5(2) of Ordinance 54 of 1985 and found the house in question to be an abandoned house within the meaning of President's Order 16 of 1972. 

 6. The learned Judges of the High Court Division while considering judgment of the Court of Settlement sat over the judgment as a court of appeal and reappraised the evidence and materials on record. In exercising the jurisdiction in certiorari the learned Judges sat over the judgment of the Tribunal as a court of appeal and reversed the findings of fact of the Court of Settlement. The learned Judges on consideration of the materials and evidences on record took a different view that Md Nasim was the son of original allottee Yahiya as the original title deed and original receipts showing payment of rent, taxes, etc. were produced from the custody of respondent No. 1. The learned Judges relied very much on this circumstantial evidence. The learned Judges also found that respondent No. 1 having failed to give the exact date of death does not ipso facto disprove the assertion that Yahiya died some time in 1970. The manner in which the learned Judges considered the material on record is in the fact the manner in which a court of appeal disposes of an appeal. The learned Judges of the High Court Division exceeded their jurisdiction while exercising their power under certiorari to interfere with the judgment of an inferior tribunal. 

 8. It has been held by this Division in various decisions that the enlistment of a building under section 5(1) of Ordinance 54 of 1985 raises a presumption in law that the property is an abandoned property under section 5(2) of the Ordinance. This presumption is, of course, a rebuttable presumption but respondent No. 1 failed to rebut this presumption. No rebuttable evidence could be adduced to show that original owner Yahiya was present in Bangladesh and he occupied, managed or supervised the disputed building when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation. Hence, the listing of the property as an abandoned property in the Supplementary Provisions Ordinance, 1985 was lawful as it was an abandoned property by operation of law.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury

parties:
Md. Ali Acorn alias Bahul and others ----- Defendant-respondent Petitioners 
Versus
Tahsilder, Union Bhumi Office, Poila, Ghior and others ----- Plaintiff-Appellant Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Parties No. 1-5 to show cause as to which the impugned judgment and decree 29.04.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, I' Court, Manikganj in Title Appeal No. 119 of 2005 allowing the appeal reversing those of dated 17.08.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 42 of 2002 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No, 42 of 2002 in the Court of learned Senior. Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj contending inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to the then Zamindars and during C.S. operation the land was recorded in the name of Zaminder Daraka Nath Chandra. The land being vacant was possessed by the people at large of the locality and after Slate Acquisition and  Tenancy Act, 1950 the land has become 'khash' tinder the government. During S.A. operation it was wrongly recorded in the name of some persons and on the basis of that wrong S.A. record the R.S. khatian being No. 122 was prepared wrongly. The people of the locality from the very beginning do possess the land in dispute. The R.S. and S.A. recorded tenants collusively got their names mutated in Mutation Khatian No. 1/87-88. The names of defendant-respondents in respect of the mutation khatian has been annulled pursuant to a Miscellaneous Case No. 3197 of 1997. The defendants filed a Title Appeal No. 21 of 1997 which was dismissed for default on 12.09.2000. Thereafter, for restoration of the suit a miscellaneous case was preferred which was also rejected but due to denial of plaintiffs title by the defendants the plaintiffs instituted the title suit for declaration of title in respect of the suit land. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants No. I-3 in short is thus that the suit land had been owned and possessed by one Foyezee Box ' alias Foyez Box and others. Thereafter the original owners died leaving their heirs and the defendants are the successive heirs of the original owners. The S.A. and R.S. record has been correctly prepared in their names. The recorded tenants transferred the land in favour of the defendants by registered kabla deeds and delivered possession. The defendants are paying rents to the government on the basis of mutation khatian. The plaintiffs having no right, title, interest and possession filed the suit on false allegation. 

 4. The 'ranted trial court dismissed the suit for default during its pendency and thereafter the plaintiffs preferred a Miscellaneous Case being No. 4 of 2000 under Order IX rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit vacating the order of dismissal. After rejection of that miscellaneous case the instant Title Suit No. 42 of 2002 has been brought on the basis of same cause of action. The learned Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj on completion of trial dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 17.08.2005. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred a Title Appeal No. 119 of 2005 in the court of learned District Judge, Manikganj, which was transmitted to the I" Court of learned Joint District Judge, Manikganj for hearing and disposal. The learned lower Appellate Court hearing the appeal allowed the same and after setting aside the dismissal decree passed by the trial court decreed the original suit on contest by the impugned judgment and decree dated 29.04.2007. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed illegality and without reversing the findings of the trial court on maintainability point of the original suit reversed the judgment illegally. The learned Advocate further submits that the trial court rightly after elaborate discussions over the facts and law as to Order IX rule 8 and 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure including the provisions laid down in Order XLIII rule I rightly decided the merit of the case against the plaintiffs on point of maintainability inasmuch as the original suit was not maintainable in the form of declaration under the purview of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It was the observation of the learned trial court that under the proviso of Rule I of Order XLIII of the Code of Civil Procedure in the instant case the original suit was barred by law and on the same cause of action a fresh suit cannot he instituted. On the contrary; the appellate court below illegally held that there is no legal bar in institution of the fresh suit on the same cause of action as it does not attract the provisions laid down in Order XLIII, Rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule controverter the argument advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that the appellate court rightly and legally decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the appellant and as the original snit was dismissed for default for the lack of taking step from the side of the plaintiffs and due to the lacking of the party concerned in taking step the suit was dismissed on technical cause there is no scope to invoke the provisions laid down in Order XLIII, Rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submits that the earlier suit inasmuch as for want of taking step was dismissed under Order IX rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the learned appellate court below in his observation and findings legally and properly held that the earlier suit being No. 21 of 1997 was filed by the plaintiff-appellants on a cause of action which was occasioned at the fag-end of the month of 'Chaitra', 1403 B.S. and the satiric was dismissed for default on 12.09.2000. Subsequently; the miscellaneous case was preferred for restoration of the same which was also rejected. Therefore; obviously the original suit i.e. the Title Suit No.42 of 2002 was quite maintainable. 

 10. On perusal of the case records in consultation with the submission given from the side of the learned counsel of the parties; the pertinent question which is raised is such as to whether the original suit was maintainable under the purview of law. In this regard; having gone through the relevant case records 1 find that the Title Suit 21 of 1997 was dismissed for default due to the fault of the concerned 'mohorar' on behalf of the plaintiffs. I have come across from the contents of the connected papers that the Title Suit being No.21 of 1997 was fixed for show cause including return of postal summon-notices, but due to lack of taking any step from the side of the plaintiffs the learned court below dismissed the suit for default of the plaintiffs. With regard to this; the provisions laid down in Rule 3 of Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure contemplates, where neither party appears when the suit is called on for hearing the court may make an order that the suit be dismissed. This type of dismissal order not being a decree is not appealable and the remedy lies on an application under Order IX rule 4 or institution of a fresh suit. There is no scope to entertain Review application here. Secondly, under the proviso laid down in Rule-8 of the said Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure enjoins, where the defendant appears and the plaintiff does not appear and the suit is called on for hearing the court shall make an order that the suit be dismissed. Here in the instant suit No. 21 of 1997 it is apparent from the face of the papers that there was no occasion for appearance of the defendant after service of summons inasmuch as the service of summon-notices was not done or took its effect or that the process was completed. The date was fixed for taking step from the side of the plaintiffs with regard to postal notices upon the defendants as well as reply of a show cause from the side of the plaintiffs but admittedly no step was taken from the side of the plaintiffs and accordingly the suit was dismissed for default. Under the ambit of Order XLIII Rule I and the proviso laid down in Rule 1(C), an order under rule 9 of Order IX rejecting an application for an order to set aside the dismissal of a suit and fd) an order under Rule 13 of Order IX rejecting an application ( n a case open to appeal) for an order to set aside a decree passed ex parte an appeal shall lie. The learned Advocate Mr. Selim Reza Chowdhury in this connection cited some decisions given in the case of Soneli Bank -vs.- Nurad Kader and another 46 DLR 21, Maung Ahmin -vs.-Maung Sating and another A.I.R.1938 Rangoon 360 and Sheikh Mahammad As: Mt. Rukinina Kunwar and others A.I.R. 1946 Allahabad 506. 

 13. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 29.04.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court, Manikganj in Title Appeal No. 119 of 2005 allowing the appeal and reversing those of dated 17.08.2005 passed. by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Gheor, Manikganj, in Title Suit No. 42 of 2002 is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Syed Aynul Akhter Chowdhur ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Sanjit Kumar Bhowmik and other ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Kashefa Hussain J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party Nos. 1-4 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 24-10-2000 passed in Title Appeal No. 38 of 1998 by the Learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Magura affirming those dated 22-3-1998 in Title Suit No. 120 of 1983 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, should not be set aside. 

 One Rajendra Nath Dhar as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 120 of 1983 seeking a decree Tor declaration that the registered Deed No. 5029 dated 5-6-1969 is a mortgage deed and not a sale deed in respect of the properties, namely plot No. 612 comprising an area of 0.33 decimals and plot No. 1045 comprising an area of 0.31 decimals being a total area of 0.64 decimals of land and the consideration of the deed amounted to a sum of total Taka 2,000. That the plot No. 1045 was an agricultural land and plot No. 612 was low land, but the plaintiff used half portion of plot No. 612 for residential purposes by filling earth and the rest was used to rear fish. 

 3. The defendant in the Suit in defence raised the grounds in contrary, that the defendant's two storied building comprising of an area of 0.82 decimals was purchased in the year 1968 for a consideration of Taka 8600 and where he has been living with his family since his purchase in 1968. The defendant in his defence also states that the ground floor was occupied by the original plaintiff late Rajendra Nath Dhar since before purchase of the plaintiff and even after his purchase of the residential house from the plaintiff, the defendant allowed the original plaintiff to continue to live in the ground floor of the house, but that after some time it became inconvenient for them to live in the same building with a tenant from a different community , and, therefore, the defendant-petitioner requested the plaintiff opposite parties to live in the adjacent plot No. 612, half portion of which he had developed by filling earth by creating a ditch. He also stated in his defence that he had even given some used (পুরাতন) CI Sheets to the plaintiff to construct temporary huts in the raised portion of Plot No. 612 and allowed him to stay there till he could find out an alternative accommodation. 

 4. That the Assistant Judge who tried the Suit on the first occasion after consideration of  evidence and other relevant documents came to the finding that the deed was not a mortgage deed but a sale deed, and, therefore, dismissed the Suit vide Judgment and Decree dated 27-2-1988. Thereafter, being aggrieved by the said Judgment and decree the plaintiff opposite parties filed Title Appeal No. 57 of 1988 and the Appellate Court vide judgment and order dated 27-4-1991 allowed the Appeal and remanded the suit for a fresh Trial. 

 5. Upon remand, the Court of the Assistant Judge decreed the Suit hearing the parties and adducing evidence, recording further evidence decreed the Suit vide his Judgment and Decree dated 22-3-1998. Thereafter, being aggrieved by the Judgment and Decree dated 22-3-1998 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar the defendant-petitioner preferred an Appeal before the District Judge, Magura and which upon transfer to the Court of Sub-Ordinate judge, 2nd   Court, Magura, the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court Magura after hearing both sides by his Judgment and Decree dated 24-10-2000 dismissed the Title Appeal No. 38 of 1998 affirming the Judgment and Decree dated 22-3-1998 passed earlier by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Magura, the defendant as petitioner obtained the present Rule in this Revisional Application. 

 14. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties while making his arguments primarily relied upon the oral evidences that were deposed by the witnesses in the Trial Court. The Learned Advocate for the opposite parties argues that the defendant No. 1 in the Original Suit in his written statement did not state anywhere that the plaintiff was a "tenant" under the defendant upon the Suit land and he also submits that rent receipts marked as exhibits "C" series could not lawfully be considered as a piece of evidence as per the provision of Order VI, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 15. The Learned Advocate for the opposite parties also raised an issue of "adverse possession" before this Court upon Title and Ownership. In course of his argument claiming Title by way of adverse possession, he submits that the impugned deed was executed and registered on 5-6-1969 and the Title Suit No. 120 of 1983 was filed on 27-2-1983 and, as such, a period of 12 (twelve) years had elapsed from the date of the Kabala till filing of the Suit, while the plaintiff-opposite-parties have been in possession of the suit property prior to the kabala and therefore the right to claim title by way of adverse possession has accrued upon them. 

 17. We have heard the learned Advocates from both sides, perused the application, documents and judgment of the Courts below and other materials on record placed before us for our scrutiny. Upon such perusal and scrutiny we have found that the impugned deed dated 5-6-1969 is the main bone of contention and issue in question wherefrom the cause of action in the original suit had ensued, ultimately leading to the instant Civil Revisional Application therefore, let us first focus our attention towards the document itself. 

 18. From our perusal and examination and from what transpires from the record, we find that it is an admitted fact by both parties that a deed was signed by the parties having full knowledge of the contents thereof and we also find that both the original plaintiff being the present opposite parties in no way denied the contents in the recital of the said documents and have at no stage denied its validity. While scrutinising the registered document, the decision reported in 10 DLR 1958 in the case of Ganu Mia vs Abdul Jabbar was cited by the Learned Advocates for the parties and placed before us for our appreciation thereof. We have read the case and we have also perused the impugned registered deed. While so doing, we have compared the recital contained in the registered deed with the conditions laid down in the said case, reported in 10 DLR as the test applicable for the purpose of determining a mortgage by conditional sale. Upon comparison, it is our considered opinion that the Courts below in relying upon that case upon a misconceived notion misinterpreted the intention of the court in laying down the conditions set out for the test applicable for the purpose of determining the documents to be a mortgage by conditional sale. The conditions set out in the said decision in 10 DLR 636 in the case of Ganu Mia vs Abdul Jabbar has been reproduced as under; 

 27. Now on this point also we cannot agree with the opposite parties. In our opinion, the defendant-petitioner have not deviated from the scheme of Order VI, rule VII of CPC, given that he has not made any substantive departure from his claims. The opposite parties according to the petitioner were earlier residing in that house upon permission of the defendant-petitioners i.e. as licensees and eventually they became their tenants by paying rents and started residing upon the suit land in the capacity of tenant. We do not find anything unreasonable or inconsistent in this statement of the petitioner. Such an arrangement is quite reasonable under the circumstances and the conversion of a person who had originally started living upon a property as a licensee and eventually converted into a tenant by paying rent is very much possible and probable under the circumstances and may not call for further enquiry. 

 28. The Appellate Court in its Judgment has made an observation in the terms of “নালিশী ৬১২ দাগের জমিতে মূল বাদী ও তার ওয়ারিশ পূর্বাপর বসত বাড়ী হিসেবে ভাগ ভাগ দখল করে আসছে। আদৌ ঐ জমির দখল হস্তান্তর করেন নাই” This observation of the Appellate Court is based upon a misconceived notion. The Courts below tried to justify its finding upon the rationale that the defendant was not in possession of the suit property and that it has all through been in the possession of the plaintiff opposite parties. But, we feel that the question of possession by the petitioner is not very relevant here in that after purchasing the property from the plaintiff-opposite parties, the defendant-petitioner had continued to let them reside in the property first as licensees and subsequently in the capacity of tenants by payment of rent and as we have already opined it is reasonable and very much possible under the particular circumstances of this case. Further our view is that, nobody is denying the fact that the opposite-parties were in possession even after execution of the impugned registered deed No. 5029 dated 5-6-1969, but the Courts below failed to comprehend the fact that they, the plaintiffs after the execution of the registered deed dated 5-6-1969 were allowed to reside therein initially as licensees with permission to live there and then subsequently in the capacity of tenants subject to payment of rent. Therefore our finding is that though the literal physical possession is still under the plaintiffs, but the ownership had passed to the defendant-petitioner after the execution of the deed. We must not confuse possession with ownership or title to property. Ownership and title to property can only be determined by the construction of the deed or document itself and not by any extraneous considerations. 

 29. As is apparent from the Judgment of the District Judge, The Courts below had also arrived upon the erroneous finding that the defendant had no Title to the suit property relying upon the ground that the suit property comprising of Dag No. 1045 was subsequently acquired by the Government under the Act and against that acquisition nobody had ever come to claim or receive any compensation money from the government and that the defendant No. 1 neither tried  to receive the compensation money nor did they file any suit against them. Placing their reliance upon this ground, the court below committing a fallacy in law decided that the defendant's Title to the suit land could not be proved. We do not agree with this reasoning of the Courts below given that as it transpires upon perusal of the judgment itself, the land was acquired by the Government between the years 1984-1985. As is also evident from the records, the original Suit was filed in 1983 that is prior to the acquisition of the land by the government. Therefore, since the land was acquired between 1984-1985, that is after the Original Suit being Title Suit No. 120 of 1983 was filed in the year 1983, it was already a pending litigation for declaration of ownership and Title to the property, and therefore, Title to the property being a Subjudice matter, it can only be reasonably concluded that the question of receiving the compensation money by either parties cannot arise under the laws. 

 31. The Learned Courts below have also relied on the plaintiff opposite parties' assertion that the plaintiff-opposite parties repaid the so called "mortgage" loan which the original plaintiff had received from the petitioner. We find that here the lower Courts below while relying upon such claim had relied only upon the oral evidences as has been given as deposition of the witnesses and not on any proper legal documents. Here we can only repeat that repayment of loan cannot be sustained in law in the absence of any document to prove such claim and when there is another legal document in existence, in this case the impugned registered deed itself that indicates otherwise. 

 32. The opposite parties, while making their submissions before us, had also in the course of their arguments before us made a plea of adverse possession. The contention of the Learned Advocate for the opposite parties is that they are entitled to claim acquisition of Title to the property through adverse possession. The Learned Advocate for the opposite parties argued that the impugned registered deed was executed and registered on 5-6-1969 and the instant suit was filed on 27-2-1983 and twelve (12) years had elapsed from the date of the Kabala till filing of Title Suit No. 120 of 1983 and the Plaintiffs having been in possession of the Suit land even long before that and the defendant-opposite parties having full knowledge of the plaintiff's possession never opposed to such possession and had not mutated the defendant's name on the basis of the alleged Kabala and that hence the Plaintiff-Opposite parties have acquired Title through adverse possession and that the Courts below lawfully decreed the suit in favour of the Plaintiffs. 

 35. Regarding the claim of the opposite parties of acquisition of Title by adverse possession, we find it very much pertinent and necessary to point out the fact that in the present case it is obvious from the materials on record, other documents and the submissions made on behalf of the opposite parties, that the plaintiff-opposite parties at the very outset, in limine, brought the suit relying upon the claim that they are the original owners of the Property and that the Title to the property was never transferred and that the registered deed No. 5029 dated 5-6-1969 that was executed by them in favour of the defendant was only a "mortgage-deed", and, therefore, legal ownership and Title to the Suit land had always remained with them. But after making such a claim all through, suddenly at this stage, before us, they take up the plea of acquisition of Title through Adverse possession. Now there are various incidents attached to a claim that may determine a title through adverse possession. Adverse possession is inter alia a way of gaining or acquiring legal title to property by the hostile, exclusive continuous possession of the property within the knowledge of the true owner for a certain period as prescribed under the law and if the real owner fails to bring a suit within the statutory period, title shall be acquired by the person in adverse possession. Adverse possession therefore as was also observed by our Apex Court in the above mentioned decision in Mohammad. Abdul Jalil Minh vs Nirupamer Ritchil reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 63 = 49 DLR (AD) 61. 

 36. In the present case, the Plaintiffs-Opposite parties did not at any stage of the Suit rely upon the claim that they were living in that property in hostile possession as to the title or ownership of the true owner. They never said anywhere that they were not the original owners but had acquired Title by adverse possession of more than twelve years that is the statutory period of limitation. Their prayer for declaration of Title has been based on their claim that they had been the lawful owners of the property all through. Therefore, their claim at this stage that they have acquired Title through Adverse Possession is an absurdity and cannot be sustained under the law. On the one hand, the opposite Parities claim that they are the Original lawful owners holding Title and on the other hand they claim that they have acquired Title through Adverse possession. We regret to say that such claims run counter to each other and the plaintiff-opposite parties are not themselves certain about their legal standing as to the suit property and is thus making inconsistent and contradictory statements to that effect and according to their own convenience and such arguments and claims cannot be sustained in law and is hence not acceptable to us. 

 38. Therefore, under the aforesaid facts and circumstances stated above and upon perusal of documents and other materials on record and the Judgments of the Courts below, we find substance in the Rule and in the submissions made by the Learned Advocate for the petitioner, and, therefore, the Rule is made Absolute without any order as to costs and the Judgment and Decree dated 24-10-2000 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Magura in Title Appeal No. 38 of 1998 affirming those dated 22-3-1998 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Magura decreeing the Suit in Title Suit No. 120 of 1983 are hereby set-aside and the said suit stands dismissed.

parties:
MA Hashem ------ Appellant 
Vs.
Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and anothers ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J : Erstwhile Dhaka Improvement Trust, shortly DIT, now Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha, shortly RAJUK, allotted plot No.CWN(B)34, New plot No.113 of the lay out plan of Gulshan Residential Model Town, the quantum of land is more or less 1(one) bigha, 1 (one) katha, 14(fourteen) chattaks, on 21-3-1962 to Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza. To grab this land through legal process 3(three) suits have been filed, first of which is Title Suit No.51 of 2004 was filed by MA Hashem on 8-2-2004 for Specific Performance of a Contract against Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza second one, Title Suit No.176 of 2004 was filed by a person claiming to be Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza for a direction upon RAJUK to issue sale permission and third one, Title Suit No.81 of 2006 was filed by the plaintiffs claimed to be the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar for declaration that their father was the real allottee and for permanent injunction. Although aforesaid three suits are for three different distinct reliefs but the parties allowed disposing of the suits on the basis of oral evidence on adaptation but on different exhibits. 

 2. On a reading of the judgment of these three suits passed separately I am of the view that the judgments are not too satisfactory and also I am annoyed with the conduct of RAJUK, erstwhile DIT but since these appeals are from original decree, section 107 of the Code of Civil Procedure gives mandatory power to determine a case finally, as the Appellate Court shall have the same powers and shall perform as nearly as may be the same duties as are conferred and imposed by this Code on Courts of original jurisdiction in respect of suits instituted therein and since depositions and exhibits before my hand as such, I can dispose of the suits without sending the same to the trial Court for remand. It is also to be noted here that in three suits, 4 (four) sets of apparently original documents i.e. allotment letter of DIT, standard lease deed agreement of DIT and receipts of National Bank of erstwhile East Pakistan showing payment of installments against letter of allotment have been filed but it is curious to note that plaintiff of each of the suits did not take any step for ascertaining which one of these four sets of apparently original documents and deeds are original real and which one is forged. 

 3. The cases before me are unique cases of forgery. Allottees, 3 in number are of same name, same parentage, similiar hand writings with similiar apparently same documents but 3 persons claiming the plot of RAJUK of them one must be genuine with original papers and others are not. I have taken a strong heavy burden to single out that genuine person with original documents. 

 4. At first let me proceed with Title Suit No.51 of 2004 filed by MA Hashem for Specific Performance of Contract. 

 5. In the cause title of the plaint the defendants are Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of House No.11, Line No.6, Section 6/A, Mirpur, Dhaka and 3 others i.e. Md. Akhtaruzzaman, Director, Eastern Housing Limited as principal defendants and Chairman, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha, RAJUK Bhaban, Dhaka and the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka as proforma-defendants. The suit is valued at Tk. 1,65,00,000 and it is stated in the plaint that schedule property was allotted by erstwhile DIT in favour of defendant No.1 vide allotment letter No.DIT/ Gulshan/2409 dated 2-3-1962 and it was registered between DIT and the principal defendant No. 1 vide lease deed No. 7198 dated 1-8-1962 and possession was handed over to the principal defendant No. 1 who duly mutated in respect of the suit land his name and has paid rents and taxes regularly to the government and having right, title, interest and possession, constructed some temporary structures in the schedule property and while principal-defendant No. 1 was in possession having right, title, interest thereto entered into agreement with the plaintiff on 29-12-2002 for sale of the scheduled property for a total consideration of Tk. 1,65,00,000 and a deed of agreement for sale was signed and executed on 29-12-2002 by principal defendant No.1 upon receipt of advance amount of Tk. 35,00,000 in cash, handed over all in original documents to the plaintiff in presence of witnesses. It was stipulated in the agreement that seller shall apply for obtaining all necessary permission, clearance certificate from RAJUK and other relevant authorities for sale of the land in favour of the plaintiff and plaintiff will be responsible for payment of transfer fee to RAJUK, gain tax, stamp duty, registration fee and all other charges and incidental costs and expenses and the execution and registration of the sale deed by the principal defendant No. 1 in favour of the plaintiff shall be completed within one year and the balance amount of Tk. 1,30,00,000 will be received by the principal defendant No. 1 from the plaintiff at the time of registration of the sale deed and that upon failure of the principal defendant No. 1 to execute and register the deed of sale in favour of the plaintiff, plaintiff shall be entitled to get the sale deed executed and registered through Court. Plaintiff informed RAJUK by letter dated 6-1-2003 about transfer of the schedule property by the principal defendant No.1 in favour of plaintiff on the basis of the said deed of agreement. Plaintiff by letter dated 1-8-2003, received by principal defendant No. 1 on 3-8-2003 requested him to take immediate steps i.e. permission from RAJUK for registering the deed of sale in his favour. After letter dated 1-8-2003 of the plaintiff, principal defendant No. 1 informed the plaintiff by letter dated 11-8-2003 that he having been suffering from physical and mental difficulties he could not take appropriate steps for registration of the sale deed and requested plaintiff No. 1 for further payment of Tk. 5,00,000 towards consideration, money on assurance that he will take appropriate steps immediately for executing and registering sale deed and shall also inform the plaintiff very soon thereabout. On 12-8-2003 plaintiff paid Tk. 3,30,000 to principal defendant No. 1 vide cheque. Cheque was given through a covering letter dated 12-8-2003 wherein request was made by the plaintiff to the principal defendant No.1 to take all necessary steps immediately, so that he can register the deed of sale in favour of plaintiff within the time schedule i.e. by 28-12-2003 and further requested defendant No. 1 to inform the plaintiff about the steps taken by principal defendant No.1. But up to 1-12-2003 principal defendant No. 1 failed to inform plaintiff about any development regarding executing and registration of the deed sale. Plaintiff always been ready and willing to perform his part of the obligations under the deed of agreement and there being only 27 days left of the time limit for registration the deed of sale as per agreement and out of consideration money defendant has received Tk. 38,20,000, plaintiff thus constrained to issue a notice on 1-12-2003 through his lawyer upon the principal defendant No. 1 requesting him to complete all formalities for registration of the deed of sale within 20-12-2003. It has been mentioned in the plaint that on 9-12-2003 plaintiff was shocked and surprised to learned from a biggopty (notification) published in the Daily Janakantha on 18-11-2003 which runs as follows:— 

 g) Any other or further order or orders, relief or reliefs the plaintiff may be entitled to get in law, equity and justice. 

 10. In a simple suit for Specific Performance of Contract, the activities of the parties led to so many knots by which it is difficult to find which is the original knot by which the tie was tied. 

 14. In the written statement defendants totally denied the plaint case. It is their case that disputed property was allotted to their father, deceased Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza who was BSc Engineer, originally residing at India and after creation of Pakistan, came to Dhaka and purchased six kathas of land at 157, Bara Mogbazar and constructed 3-storied building where he reside till his death. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza visited foreign countries for higher training and while he was in service in C&B department, he was allotted a land on 21-3-1962 and he paid installments on 26-3-1962, 26-6-1962, 7-1-1963, 5-3-1964 and 3-2-1966 and allotment letter was converted to lessee in lease deed no 7848 as per rules and regulations of RAJUK, a copy of the lease deed is retained by RAJUK and original copy of the lease deed was given to the lessee i.e. serial No.7848 was given to the original allottee, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and next one i.e. serial No.7849 was retained with RAJUK. In 1964 he joined Eastern Housing Ltd. and after constructing some construction on the allotted plot, he let out it to different organizations i.e. Agency for International Development, Mr. DM Franking and Alippene ott, Mr. Lloy F. Gonyea, Mr. MM Abu Zeiad of United Nations Development Programme, Mr. Fred HW Petrini, Swedish International Services, Dr. Martin W. Bloem of Helen Keller International, Uttara Bank Ltd. and Aftab Multinational firm Ltd. It has further been stated in the written statement that their father joined the Uttara Bank Ltd. as Director and also thereafter, he joined and was a director of BDC an organization of Islam group till death. Thereafter, their father applied for converting the aforesaid allotted plot to a commercial plot on 30-1-2001 and on 14-8-2001 he paid convertion fees of Tk.38,28,125. Thereafter, executed an irrevocable power of attorney on 21-12-2003 in favour of defendant No-2. The said power of attorney was approved by defendant No.3, RAJUK and after eviction of Aftab Multipurpose firm Ltd., the original structure was dismantle and passed a plan for constructing six storied commercial building and that end in view, towards middle of 2003 the construction was started. The aforesaid bainama was created on false personation of a person whose address was given at House No.31, Lane No.02, Section 6/A, Mirpur, Dhaka. When their father came to know the aforesaid ill transaction, a caution notification was published on 18-11-2003 in the daily Janakantha, Ittefaq, Observer, Inquilab and Protham Alo. After about one month of the publication of the aforesaid notification, plaintiff published a notification on 10-12-2003. Their father went to meet with the plaintiff with the original papers on 10-12-2003 at Sena Kollyan Bhabon and tried to convince that he stel real Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza and bainama entered with a person named Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza is a fake and false person. MA Hashem, plaintiff asked him that he will not claim the suit property on the basis of the aforesaid bainama but instead, to his surprise, MA Hashem published a corrigendum that the father's name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was wrongly published in the notification as Mohammad Hossain instead of Md. Yeadul Hossain. It has further been stated that the suit property is valued more that Taka 20 crores but in the bainama it is shown at 1(one) crore 65 (sixty five) lacs. Principal-defendants prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 15. In this suit defendant Nos.1(a) to 1(e) filed application for adopting the depositions of PWs 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 of Title Suit No.81 of 2006 in the instant suit which was allowed. 

 17. Before I enter to consider the case of the plaintiff, I will have to take notice of the written statement filed by the defendant No1(a) to 1(e). Defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) did never accept defendant No.1 of the plaint i.e. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur as described by the plaintiff in the agreement for sale i.e. bainama and also the original plaint, to be their father. The dispute came up to the High Court Division twice, one in Civil Revision No.4608 of 2004 and another in CO No 3422 of 2008. Although normally in case of Specific Performance of Contract, 3rd party cannot be added as it relates between two parties of the agreement i.e. vendor and vendee but in some cases where there exists a special case, 3rd party can be added. Reference may be made to the case of Ejhar Minh vs Shaher Banu, 2 BLC AD 20 = 49 DLR (AD) 85, where it has been held that subsequent purchaser should be added so that along with Specific Performance of Contract, title of the property can be effectively passed. In the instant case in my hand defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) ought to be added as party on the ground that in their hands they have original deeds and also they are the heirs of original allottee as such this is a better case than that of Ejhar Miah's case and they be added on their own foot, no as substituted heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur. In the written statement filed by the added defendants they have stated as:— 

 23. On the question of why the plaintiff mentioned the address of defendant No.1 as Mirpur in the plaint, learned Advocate submits that in Exhibit-6 i.e. agreement for sale defendant No.1 mentioned his Mirpur address as such in the plaint said address was used. On the question of what is the father's name of the vendor i.e. the grand father of defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) Mr. Fida M. Kamal submits although in the notification published in Janakantha on 10-12-2003 it was mentioned as Md. Hosain but on the very next date on 11-12-2003 the plaintiff published corrigendum in the same news paper stating the correct father's name of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza as Md. Yaidul Hosain with single 's' in Hosain. Mr. Fida M. Kamal, learned Advocate submits that whether there was single 's' or 'ss' is not matter but matter is that Md. Yaidul Hosain was the father of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza, the plaintiff successfully stated that the father of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza was Md. Yaidul Hosain. On the question whether the agreement was proved or not, learned Advocate submits that, in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract Court it is to be seen whether there was existence of contract between plaintiff and defendant; whether plaintiff was ready and willing at all materials dates to perform his part of the contract and whether the contract was enforceable. Learned Advocate on this points submits that plaintiff have proved all the 3 ingredients by adducing PW 1 to PW 3 and documentary evidence proved the existence of contract for sale, plaintiff was ready and willing to perform his part of the contact. Learned Advocate further submits that, 3 witnesses the agreement of them plaintiff examined PW 2, Md. Sadrul Huda, and PW 3, Hasan Imam Chowdhury who proved execution of the deed in accordance with the provision of the Evidence Act together with passing of consideration money. Learned Advocate on the question of using different stamp papers which does not appear chronologically submits that agreement for sale/bainapatra was written on 5 pages of which one in hundred Taka non judicial stamp and another one of fifty taka non judicial stamp as such there are different serial numbers in these stamp papers and also submit that there is seal and name of the stamp vendor and also the name of MA Hashem in the back side of the non judicial stamp. On the question of payment of consideration money learned Advocate submits that in the bainapatra it was written Tk. 35,00,000 was paid and was received by the vendor towards consideration money of Tk. 1,65,00,000 and further Tk. 3,20,000 was paid through cheque, photocopy of the same lying with the plaintiff's office and payment of consideration money was supported by witnesses Nos. 2 and 3. Learned Advocate further submits that plaintiff was ready and willing at all material time to perform his part of the contract i.e. Exhibit-6. Learned Advocate further submits that since time has running out plaintiff through his learned Advocate issued letter, thereafter, legal notice fixing 29-12-2009 for execution and registration of the kabala which the defendant No. 1 having not been done, the suit was filed. Learned Advocate further submits that defendants witnesses appeared on behalf of defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) made mere statements that defendant No.1, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza did not execute the deed of agreement for sale dated 19-12-2002 but PWs in their depositions stated that in their presence deed exhibit-6 was executed and consideration money was passed as such it is proved beyond reasonable doubt Exhibit-6 was valid agreement for sale. Learned Advocate here referred to section 67 of the Evidence Act where requirement of the signature how proved and also section 68 of the Evidence Act in support of proving of signature and submits that plaintiff examined two attesting witnesses of the deed of agreement i.e. P.Ws. 2 and 3 who proved exhibit 6 to its hilt. Learned Advocate further submits that adoption of any evidence from one suit to another suit is permissible under Section 33 of the Evidence Act but learned Advocate submits that depositions of 3 suits and using them in each of the suits by the learned Judge is not supported by any law as three suits are completely of different in nature. Learned Advocate further submits that plaintiff MA Hashem did not depose in other suits. Learned Advocate further submits that in the written statement of defendant 3, RAJUK upon which learned Judge relied is not substantive evidence in the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that the present suit of the plaintiff is maintainable for Specific Performance of Contract as suit for Specific Performance of Contract cannot be converted to a title suit. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) being successor of the vendor of the plaintiff, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza they are bound to execute the sale deed, as the learned Advocate further submits, plaintiff has proved the requirement of law for Specific Performance of Contract. Learned Advocate further submits that using of Indian stamp in 1964 is not illegal as at that time Indian Stamps were used in Pakistan and.submits that deed of lease produced by the plaintiff is not forged document for using Indian stamp in 1964 and further submits that plaintiffs documents in support of his claim are genuine documents. 

 24. Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate, appearing for the heirs of Shamsul Kabir humayun Reza of Mogbazar submits that original lessee of the plot never lived at Mirpur and he always lived in 157, Bora-Mogbazar and he never used two addresses and plaintiff failed to prove that at any point of time, Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza lived in the address of Mirpur. Learned Advocate further submits that even it is taken for argument sake that Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza received consideration money but plaintiff failed to prove the said fact. Learned Advocate further submits that witnesses of the agreement for sale, Exhibit-6, are office staffs of plaintiff MA Hashem and their depositions does not hold that such huge amount of money Tk. 35 lacs was transacted on the date of execution of the deed. Learned Advocate further submits that at the relevant time in 2004 one katha of land at Gulshan area was sold at more than taka one crore as such, one bigha one katha of land would be sold at least Taka tweny crores or more but in the agreement for sale it was shown to be sold at Tk. 1,65,00,000 which has itself shown falsity of the bainapatra. Learned Advocate further submits that plaintiff did not prove execution of bainaparta, passing of consideration money and other incidentals for Specific Performance of Contract. 

 25. Learned Advocate relied on number of decisions, on question of burden of proof of documents 4 BLC (AD) 191, 39 DLR (AD) 237, burden of proof of transaction, AIR 2000 (SC) 1203, 3 SCC 2000, 312, on status of titleless person, 61 DLR (AD) 116, on adverse posses sion, 11 MLR (AD)151, on power of appellate Court in deciding the suit finally instead of sending it on remand, 9 MLR (AD) 169, 4 MLR (AD) 1, 11 MLR (AD)119, on verification of signatures, 56 DLR (AD)117, DLR (AD) 117, on unspecified suit land , 12 MLR (AD) 105, 31 DLR (AD) 219, on evidence beyond pleadings, 38 DLR 39, on maintainability of the suit for simple declaration 16 DLR 272, 46 DLR (AD) 148, 2 XP (AD) 194, on adaption of deposition, AIR 1966 (SC) 1072 and on institution of criminal proceeding for using forged document 14 MLR (AD) 52-55. 

 6) original deed coming from whose possession 

 34. The next fact that plaintiff carrying with Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur which appears from the facts that the prayer he made for decree for Specific Performance of Contract from defendant No. 1 and also a direction upon defendant No. 1 to obtain necessary sale permission from RAJUK in favour of the plaintiff against defendant No. 1. Had the plaintiff disowned defendant No. 1 then after substitution or addition of defendant No. 1(a) to 1(e) the prayer and other incidental statements of the plaint ought to be amendment but the plaintiff did not amend the plaint showing that he still claims with original defendant No.1 i.e. Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur. Thereby it can safely be concluded that so called bainanama or agreement for sale was entered into by plaintiff with the person whom the plaintiff by his own act some time did and some time did not recognize as his vendor as plaintiff allowed defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) to substitute in place of defendant No.1 who did not recognize defendant No. 1 as their father as defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) did not step aside from their original position that they are not substituted heirs of defendant No. 1 of Mirpur but they are the heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Moghbazar against whom the suit has not been filed and no agreement or bainapatra was arrived at by plaintiff. 

 35. Having come to know from defendant No. 2 about filing of the suit for the properties in which the predecessor of defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) was original allottee, defendant No.1(a) to 1(e) filed application for being added as party but at first, they were substituted, against which they went to the District Judge and Additional District Judge who heard the revision, added them as a party, not substituted heirs of defendant No.1. against which plaintiff, MA Hashem came before this Court and this Court according to me, gave a wrong direction that in suit for Specific Performance of Contract 3rd party cannot be added and whatever the defendant Nos.1(a) to 1(e) have in their pocket, should be placed as in heirs of defendant No.1. From the conduct of the plaintiff it is clear that plaintiff in order to grab the property at a meagree price of 1,65,00,000 some time accept Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Mirpur as his Vendor and some time Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar as his vendor and having in dilemma, lastly gulped Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of Bara Mogbazar as his vendor by accepting the heirs added/substituted in place of Defendant No. 1 but without amending the material statements or prayer of the plaint. 

 37. I am of the view that the decision passed by the learned High Court Division in Civil Revision and in civil order are not correct. In the case of Ezhar Miah vs Shaher Banu and others, 49 DLR(AD) 85= 2 BLC (AD) 30 where it has been held that Court can direct subsequent purchaser to join in the conveyance so as to pass on the title which resides in him to plaintiff. That is a case of 3rd party who was trying to be added as party on the ground that he is subsequent purchaser. This case is on better footing than that case and in the instant case defendant No. 1(a) to 1(e) filed application for being added as party as the heir of original lessee Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Maghbazar with original deeds in their pocket and the written statement filed by the defendant Nos. 1(a) to 1(e) was filed as not substituted heirs of defendant No.1 but as heirs of Shamsul Kabir Humayun Reza of 157, Bara Maghbazar and as added defendants. From the aforesaid discussion it appears that there is total mystery as with whom plaintiff entered into agreement for purchasing the suit property. 

 38. Now let me consider the agreement i.e. bainapatra itself. The agreement is made in five pages, of them, two pages are of stamp papers, one at serial 2366 and other at 2414 of 29-12-2002 and three others are of curtridge papers. It has been argued by the defendants Lawyer that there is no serial maintained in the stamp papers. Mr. Fida M. Kamal, learned Advocate, submits that since stamp papers are of two different denomination as such serial were not maintained as different registers are main-tained for stamp papers of different denomination. This is not correct position. Correct position is that Registrar of Treasury supply register book to each stamp vendor giving his seal, signature and mentioning the page numbers and stamp papers of whatever denomination sold the stamp vendor shall enter the same one after another giving serial numbers. In a document where several stamp papers required then it will be numbered chronologically from one to another. I am of the view that if there be different serial numbers of stamp papers then it will create doubt as to its originality and moreso, when it is unregistered documents it creates more doubt.
