The learned Munsif however found that the petitioner had no locus standi to proceed with the execution case on the ground that he was not an assignee of the decree-holder Against the aforesaid order the petitioner preferred an appeal and the learned District Judge set aside the order or the learned, Munsif and allowed the appeal and directed the execution case to proceed in accordance with the law. Hence, the present appeal at the instance of the opposite party. 

 4. From the judgment of the learned District Judge it appears that the suit was decreed on 26-4-68 and the decree-holder transferred his entire interest in the suit land by two Kabalas dented 29-4-68 and 4-5-68. Thereafter; the  opposite party-appellant filed, the title appeal in which the petitioner-respondent was allowed, by the learned Subordinate Judge to be added as a respondent. It is not disputed that the decree-holder transferred his entire interest, the suit property by the two Kabalas to the petitioner-respondent. The learned Advocate has tried to argue that transfer of the suit property does not amount assignment of the decree as content plated under Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C. am afraid I am unable to appreciate the logic of the argument. This transfer by the decree-holder passed to the petitioner the entire rights of the decree holder-vender in, the suit property including all rights under the subsisting deecree for specific performance against the appellant, otherwise the transfer would be meaningless. This transfer by written document namely the kabalas therefore, in my opinion was an assignment of the interest of the decree-holder, in wilting as contemplated under Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C. 

 5. Apart from this, even assuming for the sake of argument that Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C. is not applicable, in the, instant case, the petitioner would Still be entitled to invoke the aid of section 146 C.P.C. and execute the decree as a person claiming under him, namely, the decree holder since it is not disputed that all rights and interests of the decree-holder-vender in the suit property stood transferred to the petitioner-respondent by the aforesaid Kabalas. 

 7. The petitioner-respondent was allowed by the Court to join in the title appeal as respondent under Order 22 rule 10 C.P.C. If the appellant had any objection or grievance against the petitioner being added as a respondent in the title appeal he could have challenged the order since the order was appealable. On query from the court, the learned Advocate admitted that no appeal was filed against the aforesaid order under Order 22 rule 10 C.P.C. on further query from the court, the learned Advocate also admitted that no second appeal was filed against the judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court in the title appeal. Having regard to all these facts and circumstances, I am clearly of opinion that the said Order under Order 22 rule 10 C.P.C. having remained unchallenged, the petitioner-respondent was fully entitled to file the application under Order 21 rule 16 C.P.C. and proceed with the execution case and that there was an assignment of the interest of the decree holder as contemplated under the said order of the C.P.C. It was therefore clear from the above discussion that even a person benefit Of the decree not by assignment but by virtue of transfer of property which is the subject matter of the decree, is entitled to execute the decree.
justice_names: Mr. Justice A.F.M. Abdur Rahman Chowdhury

lawyer:
Golam Robbani, Advocate, instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellants. 
None Represented—For the Respondent.
parties:
Bhadu Pramanik and others ---------- Appellants
Vs
Md Abbas Ali Pramanik -------- Respondent
full_judgment:
2. Facts leading, to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the respondent herein as plaintiff filed the Other Class Suit No.899 of 1984 seeking declaration that he is the exclusive owner in possession of the suit land on the averments that Samir Gaine was the owner in possession of the suit land and he died leaving behind two sons, namely, Jomir, Sobir and a daughter, Suborna Bewa, and later on Jomir died leaving behind his brother Sobir and sister Suborna and then Sobir died leaving one unmarried daughter Sorodini and sister Suborna and then Sorodini also died unmarried and thus, Suborna became the owner of the suit property and she, by deed of hiba-bil-Ewaz dated 30-4-1958, corresponding to 17 Baishakh, 1365 BS, transferred the suit property to the plaintiff and further the plaintiff also acquired 10 decimals of land by way of Korfa Pattan from Jotindranath Sil and also acquired 0.47 acre of land by way of exchange from Belo Bewa and Sadibullah in lieu of 0.10 acre of land and thus, the plaintiff became owner of the suit property but the same had been wrongly recorded in the name of the defendant which castes a cloud upon the title of the plaintiff. 

 3. The defendant contested the above suit by filling written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that, Suborna, the mother of the plaintiff and the defendant, was the owner of the suit property and she decided to transfer the suit land to both of them in equal halves by way of sale but the plaintiff fraudulently procured a deed of hiba-bil-Ewaz in his favour showing transfer of the entire suit land in his favour and thus, the above deed of hiba-bil-Ewaz is void and the plaintiff also did not acquire 0.10 acquire of land from Jatindra Nath Sil by way of Korfa Pattan dated 27 Kartik, 1352 BS and also not get 47 decimals of land by way of exchange from Belo Bewa and Sadibullah. The plaintiff and the defendant are co-sharers in the suit property in equal halves and Suborna, by inheritance, got the suit property and subsequently, she having been remarried, left her former place and thereafter, for her own necessity she had decided to sell the suit property and both the plaintiff and defendant agreed to purchase the same in equal shares and then the defendant, who is a illiterate person, asked the plaintiff though for taking necessary steps to get the sale deed registered but on the day of registration, the plaintiff himself did not go to the registry office but managed to get the suit land transferred in his name making the defendant understood that a sale deed had been executed and registered in their joint names and the record of rights also stand in their joint names in equal share and on that basis, the defendant also owned and possessed the suit property on payment of rents regularly. His further case is that his brother also inherited 0.10 acre of land out of 0.20 acre and subsequently, 7.85 acres of land including the said 0.20 acre of land was put in auction for failure of payment of rent by the tenant and then the father of the plaintiff and the defendant took "Korfa" Pattan of the same in the name of the plaintiff and the defendant and then the record of right was duly prepared in the name of the plaintiff and the defendant in equal halves and thus, the acquisition of 0.47 acre of land by the plaintiff, on the basis of exchange as claimed by the plaintiff, is also false and concocted and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. On conclusion of the trial, the Trial Court, considering the evidences and documents on record, dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 24-1-1987. 

 9. Mr Golam Robbani, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submit that the High Court Division committed error in arriving at the finding that the Courts below dismissed the suit on misreading and misconstruction of evidence and on erroneous view of the provisions of sections 58, 65 and 73 of the Evidence Act and further the High Court Division without at all considering that in a suit for declaration of title, the onus lied upon the plaintiff to prove his title by producing evidence and the Courts below found that the plaintiff could not discharge his onus of declaration of title over the suit property. He further submits that the plaintiff over the suit land have been sought for declaration of title by the plaintiff on the basis of deed of hiba-bil-Ewaz dated 30-4-1958 but he in his deposition stated that he did neither go to Registry Office at the time of registration of the said deed nor he has given the Holy Quran to his mother as a consideration for the gift and he merely stated that he gave Taka 30 to PW 2 to purchase the Holy Quran whereas PW2 in his deposition could neither say the price of the Holy Quran alleged to have been given to him by the plaintiff nor could produce the receipt showing purchase of the Holly Quran and accordingly, the learned Courts below rightly found that the deed of Hiba-bil-Ewaz has not been proved. He next submits that the High Court Division, on misreading the evidence on record erroneously held that the defendant, having admitted the existence of the said hiba-bil-Ewaz deed, the plaintiff, in view of the provision of section 58 of the Evidence Act, was not required to prove said deed and the High Court Division also committed an error of law in not considering the fact that the land measuring an area 47 decimals of land purported to have acquired by the plaintiff on the basis of exchange with Belo Bewa and Sadibullah has not been proved in view of the fact that the plaintiff has neither produced any documents in support of the above exchange nor impleaded the heirs of the said Belo Bewa and Sadibullah in the suit. He finally submits that the Appellate Court being a final Court of facts found that the deed of Korfa Settlement is not an old one as written in 1352 BS and it has been written for purpose of the suit depriving the defendant from his legitimate share and even Jotindra Nath, the Vendor of the said deed has not brought before the Court to prove the execution of it and the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that the deed has been executed by the Vendor placing reliance on the evidence of PW 4 and committed serious illegality in making the Rule absolute and thereby set-aside the judgments and decrees of the Courts below and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed. 

 11. We have heard Mr Golam Robbani, the learned Advocate for the appellants. Perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected materials on record. 

 13. Now let us carefully scan the evidence on record, ascertain the facts and circumstances of the cases, and decisions of the three (03) Courts below, whether judgment and order of High Court Division is justified or erred which calls for interference by this Division. 

 23. In the instant case, on conscientious searching into the judgments of the Trial Court and lower Appellate Court it become obvious to us that the Trial Court reached into the decision as to that the pivotal assertions of the plaintiffs that he owned the suit land through Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed, Korfa deed and exchange with Belo Bibi and Sadibullah was disproved on the basis of proper appreciation of the evidences on record. The lower Appellate Court affirmed the same findings on apposite evaluation of the materials on record. 

 24. Our considered view is that High Court Division on misreading the evidence on record erroneously held that the defendant, having admitted the existence of the said Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed, the Korfa deed is valid and the respondent-plaintiff got some suit land with exchange from Belo Bibi and Sadibullah. 

 25. As such, this Division finds no non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence on record or an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice or such finding is found to have resulted from glaring misconception of law or misconception, misapplication or misapprehension of law in the judgments and decisions of the Courts below. 

 26. Rather, we find that the High Court Division committed error of law in disturbing the concurrent findings of facts arrived at by both the Courts below and on misreading of the evidence on record. Hence, we compelled to approve the submission of the learned Senior Counsel that the High Court Division gave appalling discovery upon non-consideration of the findings of facts recorded by the Courts below.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 845 of 2016
lawyer:
Probir Neogi Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners 
A.M. Amin Uddin Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Ashraf-uz-Zaman Advocate-on-Record -----For Respondent Nos.1, 8, 10 & 14 
Respondent Nos. 2-7, 9, 11-13, 15-30 ------ Not represented
parties:
Ramesh Chandra Das and others ----- Petitioners
Vs
Gopal Chandra Majumder being dead his heirs: 1(Ka) Sureshwar Majumder and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal, are that Gopal Chandra Majumder, the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.1-7 and respondent Nos.8,9 and 12-16 herein as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.484 of 2012 impleading the present petitioners and respondent Nos.17-28 as defendants praying for declaration of title in the 'ka' schedule property and further declaration that registered deeds of sale No.4132, No.4134, No.4130, No.4139 all dated 07.09.1996 and No.3510 dated 31.08.1998, as described in the "kha" schedule to the plaint are inoperative, valueless, ineffectual and the plaintiffs are not bound by those deeds and also to pass a decree for evicting defendant Nos.1-11 from schedule Ga(1)-Ga(5)land. 

 4. Challenging the notices, the defendants instituted Title Suit No. 98 of 1984 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge Dhaka, which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 237/90 and lastly as Title Suit No. 93 of 1991, wherein they filed an application for amendment of plaint claiming to have purchased the suit land from Narayan Chandra Roy through registered deed of sale, but their application for amendment of plaint was rejected. They preferred Civil Revision No. 1810 of 2000 before the High Court Division. In the plaint they admitted to be tenants, but subsequently they claimed ownership to the suit land by filing amendment application and as such their claim was rightly rejected. The plain-tiffs have been holding and possessing the suit land, but due to creation of collusive deeds, title of the plaintiffs was clouded, hence, they issued notice under section 106 of Transfer of Property Act. But in spite of getting notice, the defendants did not pay heed thereto which constrained the plaintiffs to file the instant suit. 

 5. Defendant Nos.1 and 2, 10-12 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that Satish Mohon Roy being owner of the suit properties died leaving behind two sons namely Sushil Mohon Roy and Narayan Chandra Roy, wife Naresh Bala Roy and four daughters, namely Tanu Bala Roy, Shadeshi Bala Roy, Bina Bala Roy and Purno Sashi Das. The defendants were tenants under the original owner and, subsequently, under Narayan Chandra Roy son of Sushil Chandra Roy. Thereafter, they used to pay rent to Narayan Chandra Roy through plaintiff No. 1. Narayan Chandra Roy transferred .017 acre of land on 07.09.1996 in favour of Romesh Chandra Das vide deed of sale No. 4131, .0175 acre of land in favour of Nur Mohammad Gazi vide deed of sale No.4132, .0175 acre of land in favour of Shanti Ranjan Sarker vide deed of sale No.4133 and .0175 acre of land in favour of Khorshed Alom vide deed sale No. 4134 and, thereafter, transferred .1697 acre of 1 land in favour of Shanti Ranjon Sarker and aforementioned other purchasers vide deed of sale No.3510 dated 31.08.1998. Defendant Nos.1-2 in the meantime filed Civil Suit No.94 of 1984 before the Subordinate Judge, First Court Dhaka, praying for declaration of title and challenging notice dated 06.03.1984 issued from the office of Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for evicting defendant Nos.1-2. Satish Mohon Roy without executing any Will died leaving behind his aforesaid heirs and hence, the Will as mentioned in the plaint is fraudulent and the plaintiff probated the Will through deceitful means without serving any notice to the next of kin of Satish Mohon Roy. With a view to grab the suit property, the plaintiffs created the deed of sale showing Subol Chandra Das as vendor, who had no saleable interest in the suit land and as such the suit is liable to dismissed. 

 7. Mr. Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that the plaintiffs failed to prove the existence of the probate case and while the trial Court during trial called for the records of the pro-bate case, the concerned office could not produce the records and it transpires that the Will as well as probate case is totally false and forged. He further submitted that the plaintiffs claimed that Satish Chandra Roy executed a Will in favour of his daughter Purna Shashi Dasya on 03.01.1962 by appointing Subol Chandra Das as executor and they got probate on 01.07.63, but at that time the legal heirs of Satish Chandra Roy were not made party in the probate proceeding, and as such the probate was illegal and no right accrued in favour of Purna Shashi against the right of inheritance of Narayan Chandra Roy, and as such the impugned judgement and decree is illegal and cannot be sustained in law. He also submitted that the High Court Division failed to notice that the daughter of the executor of the Will had no right to transfer any land to any body and daughter of Satish Mohan did not execute any deed in favour of the plaintiffs and even did not give any power for which the plaintiffs never acquired any right, title and interest in the suit land and as such the instant suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession is not maintainable, but the High Court Division erred in decreeing the suit and thus the same is liable to be set aside. 

 10. We note from the judgement of the trial Court that upon elaborate discussion of the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record it was found that the predecessor of the plaintiffs obtained title to the suit land through probate of the Will executed by the original owner of the land, namely Satish Mohon Roy. It was observed by the trial Court that the suit property was recorded in the name of Purna Shashi Dasya, daughter of Satish Mohon Roy, in the S.A. Khatian and neither the defendants nor the predecessor of the defendants namely Narayan Chandra Roy raised any question regarding the S.A. Khatian. It was further observed that neither Satish Mohon Roy nor any of his heirs challenged the Will executed by Satish Mohon Roy. It was also observed that the name of Puma Shashi Dasya was recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 2529 and on her behalf her husband Subol Chandra Das transferred the suit land by way of 5 separate deeds in the year 1981 in favour of the plaintiffs, who thereafter mutated their names in respect of the suit land. The trial Court concluded that Narayan Chandra Roy therefore had no title to transfer by way of the disputed deeds dated 1996 and 1998. Accordingly, the trial Court decided that the plaintiffs were able to prove their title in the suit property and decreed the 5 disputed deeds detailed in schedule that to the plaint as void. 

 11. In the course of its elaborate discussion the trial Court noted that upon receiving notice from the Martial Law Authority to vacate the suit properties, the present defendants as petitioners instituted Title Suit No. 93 of 1991 wherein they admitted that they were tenant under the plaintiffs and their predecessor. However, they subsequently sought to amend their plaint claiming that they have purchased the suit property from Narayan Chandra Roy. However, that application for amendment was rejected up to the revisional Court. 

 12. The High Court Division observed that in challenging the eviction notices by way of Title Suit No. 93 of 1991 the defendant intended to assert that they tendered rent to the plaintiffs on behalf of Narayan Chandra Roy, son of Satish Chandra Roy, but that contention is not sustainable as they failed to submit any paper showing payment of rents to Narayan Chandra Roy. Subsequently, they sought to amend the plaint claiming purchase of the suit property from Narayan Chandra Roy by a registered instrument. The High Court Division concluded that the above conduct of the defendant shows that they shifted from their earlier position raising a claim of ownership and thereby forfeited rights as tenant in the suit property. 

 13. It is clear from the facts and circumstances discussed above that the defendants by their own admission made in Title Suit No. 91 of 1993 (originally Title Suit No. 98 of 1984) were tenants in the suit property. It is also apparent from the evidence and materials on record, as observed and decided by the trial Court, that Purna Shoshi Dasya's name was recorded in the record of rights in respect of the suit property and that she had title in the suit property by way of Probate Case No.19 of 1963. The trial Court found that Narayan Chandra Roy did not have any title to pass to the defendants and hence, the disputed deeds were void.
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Razia Sultana and another ------ Petitioner
Vs. 
Mir Shahinul Islam and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 18-11-2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 201 of 2013 rejecting the application filed by the defendants No. 1-3 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus that the present opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit being No. 201 of 2013 in the Court of learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession in the suit property contending inter alia that the disputed property had been owned and possessed by the plaintiff in his exclusive 16 annas share. In the disputed land there exist 4 (four) shops of the plaintiff in which the tenants are one Md Shafiullah in shop No. 1 and in shop No. 2 the other tenant was one Monjur Mia and the shops No. 3 and 4 respectively were possessed by the plaintiffs tenants Manju Mia and Rafique Mia. The defendants No. 1-3 claiming the property as of their own from their predecessor-in-interest Dr Sirajul Islam. The remaining defendants No. 4-8 are also claiming title in the disputed property on the basis of their papers. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the defendants to the suit denying the plaintiffs title dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property including his shops on 3-12-2009. The defendant's claim in the disputed property on the basis of waqf is baseless, at which the title of the plaintiff has been clouded. To dispel that cloud the plaintiff instituted the original suit for declaration of the title-and recovery of khash possession. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants No. 1-3 in short is thus that the plaintiff to the suit having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the disputed property on the basis of false allegation filed the original suit and the defendants had been owning and possessing the disputed properties including the shops therein in their own interest and knowledge of all from the very beginning. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata as for the same suit-premises earlier a Title Suit being No. 158 of 2010 have been filed against the same parties and the earlier suit have been dismissed on contest vide judgment and decree dated 31-7-2012. 

 4. During pendency of this suit the defendant-petitioners filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the trial court for rejection of the plaint on the ground that in respect of the self-same suit properties earlier the plaintiff in the 3rd court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka filed a Title Suit being No. 158 of 2010 and in that suit the plaintiff have failed to establish his case and also failed to prove his right, title and possession in the disputed premises. As a result of which the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka by his judgment and dismissal decree dated 31-7-2012 dismissed the suit on contest and, as such, the present suit is not tenable in the eye of law which is barred by the principle of res-judicata. 

 9. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that in passing the impugned judgment and order dated 18-11-2013 the learned trial court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision in not considering that the plaintiff to the suit prior to the present suit for declaration of title filed a Title Suit being No. 158 of 2010 and in that suit the plaintiff prayed for eviction of the defendants from the suit land on the ground that the plaintiff is the owner of the suit land but the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka dismissed the suit on contest on 31-7-2012 and thus the present suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata as provided in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka having failed to appreciate the actual proposition of law arrived at an erroneous view that the provision of law as incorporated in Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable in the instant suit and it is a mailer of evidence by virtue of which the matter agitated from the side of the defendants can be adjudicated and finally settled. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned trial court erred in law as well as in facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is not sustainable. 

 10. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel of the petitioners the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the learned Advocate of the petitioners and submits that the trial Judge, viz. the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka during passing the impugned judgment and order committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant suit at the present moment there is no scope to entertain such application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and it is apparent from the face of the papers that the earlier suit which was filed by the plaintiff in the third court of learned Assistant Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 158 of 2010 was not between the same parties and the matter-in-issues are quite different and the points for determination on which that suit was disposed of are different with that of the present suit. The learned Advocate also submits that the earlier suit was not a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession. Hence; the provision laid down in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure is very much inconsistent for its application in the instant suit as the principle of Res judicata itself provides that, "No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a court competent to try subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised and has been heard and finally decided "by such court." 

 11. Therefore, the former suit being Title Suit No. 158 of 2010 was quite different and the matter for adjudication therein is not identical with the present suit being Title Suit No.201 of 2013. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned trial Judge rightly held that at this stage; there is no scope for rejection of the plaint as the matter of res-judicata and the point of limitation is a mixed question of facts and law. 

 12. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates and have perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned trial Court i.e. the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.201 of 2013 including the judgment and dismissal decree passed in the earlier suit being No.158 of 2010 along with the connected papers as well as the application filed under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 13. Having gone through the connected papers it transpires that the former suit i.e. the Title Suit No.158 of 2010 was instituted by the present plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 for eviction of tenant from the suit premises and the subsequent suit which is Title Suit No.201 of 2013 is a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession. It further transpires from the connected papers that the learned trial Judge in the former suit framed four issues for decisions and those were as follows: 

 15. We have come across from the instant Title Suit being No. 201 of 2013 that this suit is a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession. In the said suit the proposed issues from the side of the plaintiff were as follows: 

 16. Obviously, in view of the nature of the present suit the issues which have been proposed from the side of the plaintiff deserve consideration of the trial Judge inasmuch as the matter of controversy between the parties to the suit is encircled within the right, title, interest and the matter of possession and dispossession of the concerned parties. Besides this; the provision laid down in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides as many as five conditions, which are necessary to constitute res-judicata. These are: (1) 'The matter directly and substantially in issue" in the former suit must be the same in the subsequent suit, (ii) The former suit must have been between the same parties or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, (iii) The parties in the subsequent suit must have litigated under the same title in the former suit, (iv) The Court which decided the former suit must have been competent to try the subsequent suit, (v) The matter directly and substantially in issue in the subsequent suit must have been heard and finally decided in the former suit. 

 17. On meticulous consideration of the application for rejection of the plaint in connection with the former suit and the present Suit being No.201 of 2013 it is apparent from the face of the papers that the matter in issues are not at all identical with the former suit and it is not directly or substantially in issues which has been heard and decided finally by a competent court of law. Apart from this; it transpires that the parties to the suits are not same. Beside this; it is a decided matter that the question of res-judicata as well as the question of limitation is a mixed question of facts and laws which is required to be adjudicated and decided during trial of the original suit. The learned trial Judge with regard to this; relying upon the decision of our Apex Court reported in 20 BLD (AD) 82 = 52 DLR (AD) 49 rightly held that there is no scope at the present stage to entertain such application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 19. In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned judgment and order dated 18-11-2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 201 of 2013 rejecting the application filed by the defendants No. 1-3 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure stands good.

parties:
Kazi Md. Salamatullah & others..... Petitioners
Vs.
The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh & others .... Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Succinctly, the facts of the case, as stated in the writ petition, are that on 01.08.1991  the RAJUK (respondent no. 2) under the signature of its Deputy Director (respondent no. 5)  allotted the case land in favour of Md. Asar Uddin and the possession thereof was handed  over to him on 25.10.1992. Thereafter, the said allottee, Md. Asar Uddin, executed a  bainapatra with Kazi Suriya Begum, who is the predecessor of these petitioners, for selling  the case property and after receiving the advanced earnest money when the said allottee was  dilly-dallying to register the said plot in favour of Kazi Suriya Begum, the latter filed Title  Suit no. 259 of 1998 in the 1st Subordinate Judge Court, Dhaka for specific performance of  contract. Eventually, on 25.09.2002 the suit was decreed exparte and sale deed was executed  and registered through Court in Execution Case no. 02 of 2003 in favour of Kazi Suriya  Begum vide registered deed no. 10233 dated 27.06.2004. Pursuant to the Court’s order  passed in Execution Case no. 2 of 2003, Kazi Suriya Begum paid transfer fees and filed an  application to the RAJUK for mutation of the land in her favour. Thereafter, Kazi Suriya  Begum made a Will in favour of these petitioners vide the Will dated 27.08.2009. These  petitioners, then, approached RAJUK for mutating the property in their names, but the  RAJUK has remained silent. In the premises, they approached this Court and hence this Rule. 

 3. Respondent no. 6 has filed an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter-alia, that the  petitioners have managed to obtain the instant Rule by suppressing the following facts  namely; the exparte decree passed in Title Suit no. 259 of 1998 on 25.09.2002 was obtained  and the execution of the same vide Execution Case no. 02 of 2003 on 24.02.2005 was done  by practicing fraud upon the Courts below. Coming to know about the exparte decree and the  Execution Case this respondent, on 24.02.2005, instituted in the trial Court Miscellaneous  Case no.18 of 2005 for setting aside the said exparte decree and its execution on the ground  that the receipt of summons, as has been recorded in the order sheet, is concocted and the  appearance of this respondent no.6, as shown in the order sheet, is also a forged one. The said  Miscellaneous Case having been renumbered as 46 of 2006, then, as Miscellaneous Case no.  34 of 2006 was allowed on contest on 09.08.2007 by the learned Joint District Judge,  (Arbitration Court), Dhaka, upon setting aside the exparte decree dated 25.09.2002 together  with its execution and, accordingly, Title Suit no. 259 of 1998 was restored to its original file  and number. Thereafter, the predecessor of these writ petitioners, Kazi Suriya Begum, filed  Civil Revision no. 3984 of 2007 in the High Court Division whereupon a Rule was issued  and, later on, the same was discharged on 27.04.2008, against which she filed Civil Petition  for Leave to Appeal no. 680 of 2009 and during pendency of the said Civil Petition for Leave  to Appeal, when she died on 31.08.2009, these petitioners substituted themselves in the said  Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal which was finally rejected on 14.12.2010. That is how the order passed by the trial Court in Miscellaneous Case no. 34 of 2006 was upheld by the Appellate Division by restoring the said Title Suit no. 259 of 1998 to its original file and number. Thereafter, respondent no. 6 made an application before the learned trial Court under Section 144 of the Civil Procedure Code (CPC) for restitution and the same having been registered as Miscellaneous Case no. 20 of 2011, was allowed on 08.10.2012, against which these petitioners approached the High Court Division having filed the Civil Revision no.  3397 of 2012 wherein a Rule was issued and, later on, the same was discharged on 25.07.2013. Against the said order of the High Court Division, these petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal no. 114 of 2014 which was also rejected on 15.06.2015 and, lastly, they filed Civil Review Petition no. 131 of 2015 before the Appellate Division and the same is pending before the said Court. 

 9. Being faced with this avalanche, the learned Advocate for the petitioners harped on his explanation that after receiving the copy of the application for vacating the order of status quo he endeavored to contact his client to receive his instructions but he is yet to receive any instructions. He contends that at the time of filing this writ petition, even at the time of moving the application for injunction, he was not aware of the facts that the original suit is pending in the concerned civil Court as the exparte decree in question, on the basis of which this writ petition is filed, has already been set-aside by the Apex Court. He vehemently claims that he came to know about these facts only on 23.08.2015 after receiving the copy of the application for vacating the order of status quo. 

 16. In adjudication upon the Rule on merit, the only issue required to be examined is whether the petitioner is entitled to have an order of direction from this Court compelling the  RAJUK to mutate their names on the case land. From the submissions made and grounds  taken in the writ petition, it appears that the writ petitioners’ basis for seeking such a  direction is the exparte decree dated 25.09.2002 passed in Title Suit No. 259 of 1998 in  tandem with the registered deed no. 10233 dated 27.06.2004, obtained through Execution  Case No.02 of 2003. In the light of the fact that it, now, appears from the papers annexed to  the application for vacating the order of status quo that the exparte decree in question has  been set aside by the Apex Court on 14.12.2010 and the original suit being Title Suit no. 259  of 1998 is pending before the trial Court upon being renumbered as Title Suit no. 25 of 2013,  there can be no legal basis to pray for a writ of mandamus, for, this Court shall be competent  to direct the RAJUK to do something, only when it will be established that the RAJUK was  required by law to do. Given the disclosure of the true position of the mutation of the case land, RAJUK being not legally bound to mutate the names of the petitioners, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 18. As per the statements of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, the certified copy of  the order of Civil Review Petition no. 131 of 2015 passed by the Appellate Division was  picked up by his clerk on 10.08.2015 and, therefore, there is no scope for the learned  Advocate for the petitioners to refute that he had the knowledge of setting aside the exparte  decree in question, its execution, restoration of the original suit which is now pending in the  concerned trial Court and the fact of allowing application for restitution at least on  10.08.2015, if not at the time of filing the writ petition. With all the above information in his  hand, he ought not to have prayed for injunction before this Court on 12.08.2015 by  suppressing the series of events that took place centering the Title Suit no. 259 of 1998. After  finding him to be a false statements-maker for the facts happened upto 10.08.2015, no one  would believe his forceful claim as to not having information about the past facts of this case  at the time of filing this writ petition. With the said revelation of making untrue statements,  no sign or reflection of remorse for committing such an offence by him was noticed in his  demeanour, rather he was insisting on delivering judgment. His apparent U-turn to pray for  non-prosecuting the case is nothing but an attempt to escape from the aspersions which were  being recorded in delivering this judgment. Prior to that, despite the sporadic adverse  observations made by this Court regarding the learned Advocate’s conduct in handling this  case, he was boldly maintaining his position that he came to know about these episodes only  on 23.08.2015 after receiving the copy of the application for vacating the order of status quo  and until this Court proved his statements to be untrue by showing the date of procurement  of the Apex Court’s order by his clerk on 10.08.2015 with the date of obtaining the order of  injunction on 12.08.2015 and the date of receiving the copy of the application for vacating  the order of status quo on 23.08.2015, he did not feel conceding the misdeeds committed by him in collusion with these writ petitioners. If he is taken to be an Advocate with the least professional knowledge, even as a naive one, his sense in no way can dictate him to pursue a writ petition in this Court with an expectation to obtain mutation of a land which is registered in the names of other persons who had been possessing the same upon mutating their names  and obtaining a building plan from the RAJUK.  19. This is, thus, a clear case of practicing fraud upon the Court and a sheer example of extreme abuse of the process of the Court and, accordingly, the learned Advocate for the petitioner as well as the petitioners deserve to be exemplarily penalized. 

 (i)	The Title Suit No. 25 of 2013, which was originally numbered as Title  Suit No. 259 of 1998, shall be disposed of within 6 (six) months from  the date of receipt of this order with appropriate costs upon these  petitioners, if it surfaces that their claim of entering into agreement  with Asir Uddin is fabricated. 

 37. The learned District Judge, Dhaka is directed to probe into the occurrences took place  in showing the service of summons as well as appearance of respondent no. 6 of this writ  petition in Title Suit no. 259 of 1998. He is further directed that upon detecting the persons involved in the incident, he shall take appropriate legal action against them.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Muhammad Khurshid Alam Sarkar

caseno:
Civil Revision No. 2506 of 2014
With 
Civil Rule 702 (Violation) of 2014
parties:
Goolshan Ara Begum   ------ Plaintiff-Petitioner 
Vs.
Syed Maroof Ahmed   ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
2. Material facts of the case, briefly, are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed title suit No. 368 of 2005 for declaration of title in respect of 1 ¼  decimals of land (2nd schedule of the plaint) and recovery of khas possession in respect of 0.14 acre i.e. more than 1/4 decimal of land ( 4th schedule of the plaint) against the defendant. The said suit was subsequently renumbered on transfer as title suit No.107 of 2012. Ultimately, the suit was decreed by ex parte judgment and decree dated 7-11-2013 and thereafter, the decree holder plaintiff-petitioner put the decree into execution by filing execution case No.1 of 2014 in which the plaintiff decree holder got possession of total 0.1721 acres of land instead of 1 ¼  decimals of land. 

 10. On scrutiny of the record, it appears that the present petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.368 of 2005 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. The said suit was subsequently renumbered on transfer as Title Suit No.107 of 2012 and ultimately the suit was decreed ex-parte and thereafter, the plaintiff-petitioner filed Execution Case No.1 of 2014 to execute the ex parte decree dated 7-11-2013 and during the pendency of the said Execution Case the present opposite party No.1 as 3rd party-applicant filed an application under Order XXI, rule 100 CPC for restoration of possession which was registered as Misc. Case No.5 of 2014. Soon there- after, the 3rd party-applicant, Haji Syed Maroof Ahmed filed an application under section 151 CPC for restoration of possession mainly on the ground that the possession was delivered beyond the schedule land of decree by evicting the 3rd party-applicant through Court and, as such, the 3rd party-applicant is entitled to get back possession of his land. It further appears that the executing Court by its order dated 25-6-2014 allowed the application for restoration of possession on the finding that "it is difficult to understand how a 3rd party could be evicted from his owned land which is not disputed matter in the suit" and the revisional Court below in its turn affirmed the said order of the executing Court. 

 11. On a close perusal of the entire materials on record, it appears that 14 decimals of land under plot No.428 is a disputed plot in the original title suit being Title Suit No. 368 of 2005 and the said suit was admittedly decreed ex parte by ex parte decree dated 7-11-2013. Therefore, I fail to understand that why the executing Court abruptly arrived at a finding that "it is difficult to understand how a 3rd party could be evicted from his owned land which is not disputed matter in the suit" and, on this finding allowed the application under section 151 CPC for restoration of possession. It further appears the learned District Judge, Sylhet arrived at a finding that "তাহার স্বত্ব দখলীয় ২০ শতাংশ জমির মধ্যে এস এ ৪২৭ নং দাগের ডিক্রিদার পক্ষের কোন দাবী নাই। ডিক্রিদার পক্ষ ৪২৮ নং দাগের ১৪ শতাংশ ভূমিদাবী করিতেছেন মর্মে প্রতীয়মান হইতেছে।" But in the end the learned District Judge rejected the civil revision summarily by the impugned judgment dated 29-6- 2014. So, the executing Court appears to have misconceived the facts and law inasmuch as the miscellaneous case under Order XXI, rule 100 CPC for restoration of possession preferred by the 3rd party applicant still remained unresolved question of fact. The order of the executing Court dated 25-6-2014 is liable to be set-aside only on the ground that whole relief granted to the 3rd party applicant on an application under section 151 CPC before disposal of the miscellaneous case under Order XXI, rule 100 CPC for restoration of possession without taking any evidence as well as without giving any chance to the decree holder plaintiff to file written objection, which is against the basic norms of adjudication and principles of natural justice. 

 12. The proposition of law is by now settled that the executing Court cannot travel beyond the decree. I have already indicated that 14 decimals of land under plot No. 428 as described in the schedule of the plaint is disputed plot in the original suit in which ex parte decree was passed. Therefore, I find no hesitation to hold that the learned District Judge, Sylhet in its turn acted illegally in rejecting the revision summarily and affirming the order of the executing Court dated 25-6-2014.

parties:
Nur Mohammad Sarker ----- Plaintiff-Petitioner
Versus
Md. Abdus Salam and others ----- Defendant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. A.N.M. Bashir Ullah J:- This Rule on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the CPC) at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner was issued calling upon the opposite party nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 04.04.2006 (decree signed on 12.04.2006) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Natore in Title Appeal no. 178 of 1998 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment dated 12.07.1998 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gurudaspur, Natore in Other Class Suit no.35 of 1987 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the opposite party no.10 Mrs. Ayesha Khatun Bibi instituted Other Class Suit no. 468 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, Natore for partition of the suit land seeking a saham for 1.88 acres of land with a further declaration that the partition deed being no. 20913) dated 21.04.1975 of Rajshahi Sadar Sub-Registrar Office is collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon her contending inter-alia that 6.88 acres of land appertaining to C.S khatian no. no. 102 corresponding to S.A khatian no. 240 and R.S. Khatian 467 originally belonged to Jitu Prang who had two sons Pachan and Soleman. During the life time of Jitu Prang, his son Pachan died leaving daughter Ayesha Khatun Bibi. Jitu Prang died on 25e February, 1962 leaving son Soleman and daughter of pre-deceased son Pachan. In view of the provisions of Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 Soleman and Ayesha Khatun Bibi had inherited equal share in the properties left by their predecessor Jitu Prang. 

 4. After filing of the suit there appears a decree on compromise against the defendant nos. 1-9 by the judgment and order dated 12.06.1978. The record further shows that. Ayesha Khatun Bihi flied Title Suit no. 621 of 1978 for cancellation of the aforesaid compromise decree dated 12.06.1978 alleging some fraud on her in order to obtain the exparte decree and the said title Suit no. 621 of 1978 was decreed by its judgment and order dated 15.05.1984 setting aside the decree passed on 12.06.1978 on the basis of solenama and concomitantly the Title suit no. 468 of 1977 was restored and was re-numbered as Title Suit no. 35 of 1987 on 23.03.1987. 

 7. On-06.07.1987 plaintiff Ayesha Bibi filed a petition for withdrawal of the suit. The trial Court with some remarks allowed the said petition subject to deposit of Taka 3,000/- as costs within 23.7.1987. But the record does not show any such deposit on behalf of Ayesah Khatun Bibi as a result the conditional order of withdrawal of the suit at the instance of Ayesha Khatun Bibi was not affected. On 16.11.1988 on a prayer of defendant no.7 Nur Mohammad Sarker he was transposed as plaintiff in to the suit and the record further shows that on an application filed by the added plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi was transposed as defendant no.7 by the order of the Court dated 22.06.1997. 

 8. At trial, the trial Court framed as many as 5 issues to dispose of the suit. The plaintiff examined 6 witnesses while the defendants examined 5 witnesses and both the parties filed some documentary evidences which were marked as exhibits. The trial Court by its judgment dated 12.07. I 998 dismissed the suit. The plaintiff against the said judgment preferred Title Appeal no. 178 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge. Nature which has 'been heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Natore who by his impugned judgment and decree dated 4.4.2006 dismissed the appeal affirming those of the judgment of the trial Court. The plaintiff-petitioner being. aggrieved by dissatisfied with the said judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 9. Mr. A.K.M. Shamsuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner supports the Rule. He submits that both the Courts below should have found that the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi was transposed as defendant and the original defendant no.7 Nur Mohammad Sarker has been transposed as plaintiff in the suit and there was no inconsistency in the case of former plaintiff and the defendant no.7 and infect after such transposition the plaint was not amended to bring the actual case of Nur Mohammad Sarker in the plaint but same happened for the laches of the conducting lawyer of the petitioner and for the said technical defects both the Courts  below dismissed the suit as well as the appeal. 

 11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner in alternatively also submits that though issue no. 4 to the effect as to whether plaintiff (Nur Mohammad Sarker) has the right, title and interest into the suit land was framed in the suit, but the same was not decided on merit as the case of plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker did not find place in the plaint. So, for any reason if the Rule is discharged, the plaintiff-petitioner may be given a chance for filing a suit afresh to protect his interest into the suit land. 

 12. On the other hand. Mr. Md. Alamgir Mostafizur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party no. 1 opposing the Rule submits that the plaintiff Ahesha Khatun Bibi claiming some share in the partible land filed the suit in the year 1977 and though immediately after filing of the suit in the year 1978 the suit was decreed on compromise against the defendant. but for the reasons best known to Ayesha Khatun Bibi challenging the said decree dated 12.06.1978 filed an independent suit being no. 621 of 1978 and the said suit was decreed exparte on 15.05.1984. There after the original Title Suit being no. 621 of 1978 was restored in its original file and number but at that stage it was re-numbered as title Suit no.35 of 1987. 

 13. He further submits that the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi by that time was convinced that she had no good case as such she filed a petition for withdrawal of the suit and the same was allowed on 06.07.1987. But since she failed to fulfill the condition of depositing Taka 3,000/- in the Court as costs within 23.07 .1987 as such the-order dated 06.7.1987 was not effected at all and thereafter the defendant no.7 Nur Mohammad Sarker was transposed as plaintiff on 16.11.1988 and almost alter 9 years on 22.06.1997 the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi was transposed as defendant. 

 16. On going to the materials on record it appears that the suit has a very chequered history during its long pendency. The suit was started in the year 1977 and immediately after filing of the suit it was decreed on compromise on the basis of a solenama. Subsequently, the same was challenged by the plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi and the decree on compromise was set aside and the original suit was restored and re-numbered as Title Suit no. 35 of 1987. Thereafter, the present plaintiff was transposed as plaintiff from his earlier position of defendant no. 7 on 16.1 1.1988 and after 10 years of his such transposition the suit was dismissed by the trial Court on contest by its judgment dated 12.07.1998. 

 17. The trial Court though did not decide the title of the plaintiff but came to a conclusion that Jitu Prang died on 20.01.1961. The trial Court also observed that though Nur Mohammad Sarker became the plaintiff but there appears no case of Nur Mohammad Sarker in the plaint and ultimately the suit was dismissed by the trial Court on that count. 

 26. From the materials on record it appears that it is fact that the case of the added plaintiff was never considered either by the trial Court or by the appellate Court below as because his case was not brought into the plaint. The plaint was filed by Ayesha Khatun Bibi to protect her interest though the added plaintiff had purchased .69 acres of land from the said Ayesha Khatun Bibi. But in fact the specific case of added plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker was not considered by the Courts below as the same was not available in the plaint although issue was framed to that effect as to the whether the plaintiff has right, title and interest into the suit land. So, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case though the Rule is going to be discharged but the plaintiff-petitioner may be allowed to file a suit afresh to protect his interest into his purchased land subject to protecting the findings and decisions of the Courts below as to the death or Jitu Prang in the year 1961. If any suit is filed by the added plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker to protect his interest for his purchased land the issue as to the death of Jitu Prang as has been settled cannot be opened again.

parties:
Abdul Malek and others ------ Petitioners
-Versus-
Mosammat Rezia Begum ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda, J: This Rule arises out of an application under Section-15(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioners and directed against the order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 dated 31.3.1994 rejecting the application of the petitioners under Sections-151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed for setting aside the abatement order dated 12.9.1988 passed in Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 and to substitute the petitioners in place of their predecessor. 

 2. The short facts of the petitioner's case is that their predecessor Abdur Razzak was tenant under defendant opposite party herein namely Most. Rezia Begum. She was trying to evict the predecessor of the plaintiff petitioners from the suit premises by force without any due process of law as a result he filed Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 for permanent injunction against the aforesaid land lady. That there was a lease agreement in between the landlady and their predecessor Abdur Razzak, In the lease agreement there was a clause that all the terms and conditions of the agreement shall be binding and enforceable against both the parties and their heirs, executors, representatives and assignees and there was another clause in the said agreement that tenant shall be able to sub-let the premises or any portion of it etc. and also it has been further stipulated that the tenant shall be able to erect sheds in the vacant land at his own costs for his business and in paragraph 7 of the petition the petitioner tried to state that after being partitioned the suit premises had fallen in the share of one Khaja, who also subsequently executed another tenancy lease agreement in favour of the predecessor of the petitioners and in that agreement it was categorically stipulated that the tenant or their heirs shall not be asked to vacate the premises in question. 

 4. The petitioner further contended that though the tenancy was heritable the landlady on being instigated by some local people tried to evict the tenant in violation of the said specific terms and conditions and as a result the aforesaid suit for permanent injunction was filed. During the pendency of the suit said Abdul Razzak, the predecessor of the petitioners herein died (no date of death was mentioned). Thereafter the petitioners filed an application on 14.1.1987 to substitute them as plaintiff in place of their predecessor on the ground that their tenancy has been made heritable but the trial court by it's order dated 12.9.1988 rejected the petition and passed an order of abatement of the suit as a whole on the ground that so ice the tenancy is not heritable after the death of original tenant. The above finding of the Trial Court was wrong. 

 6. I have perused I he record and application for revision and heard the learned Advocate for the opposite party who produced the copy of the application filed by the petitioners in the court below under section 151 and 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure. I have also perused the same the ends of justice in which amongst ether grounds it was slated that the order dated 12.9.1988 was mistaken order passed by the trial court and for the ends of justice it is required to be set aside by reviewing the earlier order dated 12.9.1988 and the original Title Suit No. 186 of 1986 required to be restored to its original file and number and also to substitute the petitioners in place of their predecessors. The learned Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka by the impugned order dated 31.3.1994 rejected the petition of the petitioners herein on the ground that the suit was abated due to the death of sole plaintiff by an order dated 12.9.1988 passed by his predecessor and without filing appeal against the said order the present application filed after lapse of 5 years under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable and cannot be allowed. Moreover after the death of the tenant, his heirs cannot be substituted in his place and thus it was rejected. 

 7. I find no agreement whatsoever in the case record which ought to have been filed in the court below to substantiate the claim of the petitioners. The monthly tenancy is not heritable but it is a contract between individual and on the death of any of the parties the contract terminates. It is held by the Appellate Division in a case of Abdus Sattar and others Versus Suresh Chandra Das and others reported in 32 DIR(AD)-170. "That a tenancy is determinable at the will of either landlord or tenant and is a personal relation between the original landlord or tenant and is determined by the death of either of them. There is difference between leases as provided under Section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act (T. P. Act) arid tenancy defined under Section 106 of the said Act."

parties:
Md. Kheraj Mia alias Abdul Hakim ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Ashraf Mm and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
D.M. Ansaruddin Ahmed, J: This Rule issued on an application under Section 115 of the bode of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the, judgment and order passed on 31.12.1986 by the Munsif, 4th Court, Dhaka allowing Mis. Case No.79 of 1985 under Order 9 Rule of the Code using out of Title Suit No.416 of 1985 (originally Title Suit No. 327 of 1981 of the local Munsif's 6th court). 

 2. The above mentioned suit was instituted by the plaintiff (petitioner herein) against 5 defendants, that is, 4 brothers and 1 brother's wife for their ejectment as licensees from the suit premises which constitute the eastern, part measuring about 2 Kathas of land with structure thereon out of holding No. 213, West Bashabo, Dhaka. The 4 brothers filed a joint written statement and the 5th defendant filed a separate written statement in the suit. Subsequently on the death on defendant No. 4 his heirs including some minors were brought on record on 23.2.1983. Ultimately the court guardian submitted his report on 5.1.1985. On this day the plaintiff filed hazira but the defendants were absent and the suit was fixed for ex-parte hearing on 28.1.1985. On the date fixed the suit was transferred to the local 4th Court of Munsif in pursuance of an earlier order of the District Judge. The transferee court, after 2 or 3 suo motu adjournments, decreed the suit ex-parte on 23.3.1985. Subsequently the plaintiff got the plaint schedule and the decree amended by inserting the description of the suit holding under an order dated 18.5.1985. Thereafter, on 1.6.1985, defendant No.1 Abdul Kader, defendant No.3 Ashraf Mia and defendant No.4 (kha) Bacchu Mia filed the Misc. Case No.79 of 1985 under Order 9 Rule 13 for setting aside the ex-parte decree taking the plea that after transfer of the suit from the original court they were not informed about the proceeding. The plaintiff contested the rehearing case by filing a written objection and at the heating only 1 witness was examined on the either side. The learned Munsif has decided the point on limitation to favour of the petitioners for the reason that they filed Misc. Case within a period of 30 days from date of amendment of the decree. On the point as to whether the petitioners were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing in the suit the learned Munsif has also decided it in the affirmative believing the petitioners case that they were not informed about the transfer of the suit in spite of a definite order having been passed in the order sheet by the transferee court and that they had no knowledge of the progress of the proceedings in the transferee court. Me has also believed the petitioners contention that they for the first time learnt about the ex-parte decree when the plaintiff made an attempt to take possession of the premises through court on 16.6.1985. The learned Munsif has accordingly allowed the Misc. Case subject however to condition of deposit by the defendants petitioners of an amount of Tk. 1,000/- as cost to the credit of the plaintiff opposite party by 30.1.1987 and the order sheet shows that the amount was duly deposited. It is against this order that the plaintiff has obtained the instant Rule. 

 5. It will appear that while praying for setting aside the decree the defendants also made a prayer under Section 5 of the limitation Act for condonation of the delay. This fact is very much specifically mentioned in the order whereby the learned Munsif, after hearing the, defendant's learned Advocate, registered the case and directed issue of process upon the opposite parties. This is a clear evidence of the court below having condoned the delay by implication. Moreover, there is another question which has been considered by the court below. Subsequent to the passing of the ex-parte decree the plaintiff prayed for amendment of the plaint and consequential amendment in the decree also. The prayer was allowed on 18.5.1985 and the plaint as well as the decree were accordingly amended. Since them defendants could not get set aside the original decree without the amendment, they are, while praying for setting it aside, entitled to compute the period of limitation from the date of the amendment. In such view of the matter the learned Munsif has rightly held that the i.e. hearing case having been filed within 30 days therefrom is not barred by limitation.

parties:
Faijaner Nessa and others ------- Petitioner
VS
Md Ibrahim Khalil and others ------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, this Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-9 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 3-3-2015, passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Cumilla, allowing the Title Appeal No. 302 of 2011 reversing the judgment and decree, passed on 8-8-2011 by the learned Assistant Judge, Muradnagar, Cumilla dismissing the Title Suit No. 85 of 2001 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may deem fit and proper. 

 2. Relevant facts for disposal of the Rule are that the opposite party Nos. 1-9 as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No. 85 of 2011 for declaration of title stating, inter-alia, that the suit land appertaining to CS plot Nos. 783 and 784 under CS Khatian No. 339 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 300, originally belonged to Mona Gazi who built a mosque and dug a pond thereon. Karim Box was the Imam and caretaker of that mosque and his name was wrongly recorded in the CS Khatian No. 339 and subsequently in the SA Khatian No. 300. This wrong record cast cloud upon the title of the Poramtola Jame Mosjid waqf property. Under such circumstances, the plaintiff filed the suit in the Assistant Judge Court, Muradnagar, Cumilla for a decree of declaration that the suit scheduled property is the waqf property of Poramtola Jame Mosjid. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1-4, 6-9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 29 and 30 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint stating, inter-alia, that the suit property originally belonged to the predecessor of the contesting defendants namely Karim Box Hazi and his name was correctly recorded in the CS Khatian No.33. He died leaving behind his wife Anna Bibi, four sons and four daughters who got ownership and possession by way of inheritance. They transferred 2¼ decimal of land in favour of Poramtola Jame Mosjid by a deed of waqf nama dated 9-10-1975. Thereafter, they transferred 11/2 decimal of land in favour of a madrasha by a deed of gift dated 16-1-1991. Now they have been possessing 57¼ decimal of land. The plaintiffs have filed the false suit, hence the case of the contesting defendants. 

 4. Upon hearing, the learned Assistant Judge, Muradnagar, Cumilla dismissed the suit on 8-8-2011. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 302 of 2011 before the District Judge which was transferred to the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Cumilla. The learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Cumilla allowed the appeal on 3-3-2015 setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge Muradnagar, Cumilla. 

 6. Mr Md Mubarak Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners contends that the original Title Suit No.85 of 2001 as well as Title Appeal No. 302 of 2011 arising out of the said Title Suit No. 85 of 2001 were not maintain-able since both the Courts passed their judgments and decrees beyond their jurisdiction. He further contends that the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration that the suit property is the waqf property of Poramtola Jame Mosjid, but whether the property is a waqf property or not this question shall be decided by the waqf Administrator under section 50 of the waqfs Ordinance, 1962, not by any Civil Court. Mr Mubarak relies upon the decisions passed in the case of Khan Bahadur Abdul Hoque Dovash Waqf Estate vs Abdul Motaleb Chowdhury and others reported in 20 BLC 421. He further submits that as per decision passed in the aforesaid case, the waqf Administrator shall decide all questions as to whether the particular property is waqf property or not, this question will never be decided by a Civil Suit. Under such circumstances, he prays for setting aside both the judgments and decrees of the Courts Below. 

 7. On the other hand, Mr Zaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1-7, submits that there is no doubt, section 50 of the waqfs Ordinance provides provisions as to any question whether a particular property is waqf property or not, it shall be decided by the waqf administrator, but the said Ordinance does not debar or oust the Civil Court to determine the question and it is nowhere provided in the Ordinance itself that the Civil Court is barred from entertaining any suit asking for a declaration of that character and the Civil Courts jurisdiction has not been ousted in express terms by the said Ordinance. He further submits that the decision passed in Khan Bahadur Abdul Hoque Dovash waqf estate vs Abdul Motaleb Chowdhury and others reported in 20 BLC is not applicable in the instant case. He also submits that the jurisdiction provided in section 50 of the waqfs Ordinance, 1962 is cumulative, alternative, parallel and concurrent which can be exercised by a Civil Court in a Civil Suit or by the waqf Administrator on the basis of a petition filed before him. He adds that the trial Court committed an error of law without declaring that the land in question is the waqf property of the Poramtola Jame Mosjid, but the Appellate Court rightly decided that the property in question is the waqf property of the Poramtola Jame Mosjid which originally belonged to the CS tenant Mona Gazi who made a waqf in favour of the Poramtola Jame Mosjid . The learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite parties further adds that Karim Box was not the tenant of the disputed property rather he was only a caretaker, in spite of that, his name was wrongly recorded in the CS Khatian and after his death SA Khatian was prepared wrongly in the name of his heirs. He again adds that the Appellate Court rightly decided that subsequently the heirs of Karim Box created some forged documents. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties did not refer any decision in support of his submission. 

 15. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court and Appellate Court are hereby set-aside. The original suit is dismissed without any order as to cost. The plaintiffs may approach the Waqf Administrator-under section 50 of the Ordinance to decide whether the suit property is Waqf property of Poramtola Jame Mosjid or not. The judgment and decree shall have no effect in deciding the disputed question in accordance with the provisions of Waqf Ordinance, 1962.

lawyer:
Mr. Sheikh Reajul Hoque, Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Madhu Malati Chowdhury Barua, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellants.
