parties:
Abdul Gaffar being dead his heirs:1(a)Md. Sohel Mia and others ----- Appellants 
VERSUS
Md. Abdul Miah and others --------- Respondents
full_judgment:
MD. NURUZZAMAN, J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 06.07.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1113 of 2002 making the Rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree dated 14.11.2001 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.389 of 1999 allowing the appeal and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 10.06.1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhamrai, Dhaka in Title Suit No.188 of 1997 decreeing the suit. 

 2. Facts, leading to filing this civil appeal, in short, are that the respondent No.1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.191 of 1993 against the defendant No.1 and others in the Court of 2nd Assistant Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession stating, inter alia, that Hari Charan Rishi was the original owner of the suit property along with other properties and during the Cadastral Survey (in short, C.S.) operation the suit land and other properties were correctly recorded in C.S. Khatian No.497 in the name of Hari Charan Rishi who had been enjoying the suit land by erecting tin shed house thereon and used to reside with his family members in the suit land on payment of rents to the Zaminder. While Hari Charan Rishi had been possessing the suit land, State Acquisition (in short, S.A.) operation started and the suit land bearing C.S. Plot No.1230 was recorded in his name in the S.A. Khatian No.754. During S.A. operation 0.05 acres of the suit land was wrongly recorded in his name instead of 0.06 acres. After about two years of S.A. operation, Hari Charan Rishi died leaving behind two sons namely, Paban Chandra Rishi and Ram Chandra Rishi to inherit the properties including the suit land. Thereafter, while two brothers had been enjoying and possessing the suit land by inheritance, Paban Chandra Rishi died about two years before liberation of Bangladesh leaving behind only son namely, Pulin Chandra Rishi to inherit his father portion including the suit land. Thereafter, Ram Chandra Rishi died in the year 1977 leaving behind one son Shushil Chandra Rishi to inherit the share of his property. Pulin Chandra Rishi and Shushil Chandra Rishi who got the suit land by way of inheritance and while they had been enjoying the same, left the locality for the good of their business. They went to Jurain Rishi Para under Demra Police Station and were settled there. Before leaving of the locality Sukdeb Rishi, a neighbor of Pulin Rishi and Shushil Rishi was requested to look after the suit land on their behalf. After some time Pulin Chandra Rishi left for Jurain Rishi Para and went to the village Kuthai under Keranigonj Police Station and settled there. However, frequently both of them used to visit the suit land. Pulin Chandra Rishi and Shushil Chandra Rishi had been enjoying the suit land through Sukdeb Rishi sold the suit land to the plaintiff by executing a saf-kabala registered deed dated 13.03.1986 bearing deed No.2513 and handed over the possession of the suit land to the plaintiff on the same date. After purchasing of the above suit land the plaintiff was enjoying the suit land by mutating his name in the khatian and by paying rents to the Government. He constructed the pucca boundary wall surrounding the suit land. While he was peacefully possessing and residing in the suit land with his sister, another family member, the defendant Nos.1-7, in the first part of the month of September, 1991 claimed the suit land as their own and threatened to hand over the possession of the suit land in their favour on 20.02.1992 and they tried to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land but they could not succeed. Being disappointed they threatened the plaintiff with dispossession from the suit land at any time and, as such, the plaintiff has filed a suit for permanent injunction against the defendant Nos.1-7 in the Court of Second Assistant Judge, Dhaka being Title Suit No.52 of 1992. However, on 08.10.1992, the defendants dispossessed him from the suit land. Thereafter, he filed the instant suit withdrawing the Title Suit No.52 of 1992. 

 5. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 10.06.1999 passed the trial Court, the defendant as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.389 of 1999 before the District Judge, Dhaka. On transfer, the said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Eighth Court, Dhaka, who by his judgment and decree dated 14.11.2001 allowed the appeal and thereby reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The appellate Court below remanded the matter to the trial Court for re-trial. 

 9. Mr. Sheikh Reajul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that admittedly Hari Charan being the original owner of the suit land transferred the suit land in favour of Dr. Monoruddin by registered deed of sale dated 20.04.1948 and defendant-petitioner having produced said deed in the Court and same having been marked as Ext.’Kha’ without any objection and in view of the said transfer, the heirs of Hari Charan having lost their interest in the suit land, the trial Court was not correct in holding that the plaintiff has acquired title in view of sale deed of 1986 executed by the son of Hari Charan, P.W.3; that Pulin, a co-sharer of remaining 8 annas share in the suit plot having transferred his share on 22.10.1960 to Oisharaj and said document having been admitted into evidence as Ext.’Kha-1’ without any objection, the trial Court illegally passed a decree in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the entire suit plot. He further submits that the Court of appeal below having remanded the suit to consider as to whether claim of the plaintiff regarding dispossession from the suit land by defendant No.7 is true or not and the instant suit being a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession, the High Court Division erred in decreeing the suit without arriving at a finding regarding alleged dispossession of the plaintiff in the suit land by the defendant No.7 and, as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 10. Mr. Jagadis Chandra Sarker, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. He submits that the judgment of the appellate Court below appears to be manufactory, perverse and affecting the merit of the case resulting the failure of justice. The learned Additional District Judge disclosed in his judgment that the plaintiff examined three witnesses in this case to prove their respective cases. The appellate Court below further stated in his judgment that the defendant produced true copy of the (certified copy) of title deed of the same date, that is, on 23.04.1969 which was exhibited as exhibit Kha-3 and Kha-4 to prove their title. The appellate Court further mentioned in his judgment that although the defendants could not produce the original deed and also did call for Balam Book (Vollume) to prove the documents but still then in the contest of existence of these documents, the plaintiffs could not establish their title in the suit land. He next submits that the appellate Court below found in his judgment that the defendant could not prove their title by producing the original title deed or by calling upon the Balam Book from the subregistrar office and, hence, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute and passed the impugned judgment, and, as such, the instant appeal may kindly be dismissed. 

 12. Leave was granted to examine the submissions of the learned Counsel for the present Appellants that admittedly Hari Charan being the original owner of the suit land transferred the suit land in favour of Monoruddin Daktar by registered deed of sale dated 20.04.1948 and defendant-appellant no. 7 having produced the said deed in the Court and same having been marked as exhibit-'Kha' without any objection and in view of the said transfer, the heirs of Hari Charan having lost their interest in the suit land, the trial Court was not correct in holding that the plaintiff has acquired title in view of sale deed of 1986 executed by the son of Hari Charan, PW 3; that Pulin, a co-sharer of remaining half share in the suit plot having transferred his share on 22.10.1960 to Oisharja and said document having been admitted into evidence as Exhibit-'Kha-1' without any objection, the trial Court illegally passed a decree in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the entire suit plot. 

 13. That the learned Court of Appeal below having remanded the suit to consider as to whether claim of the plaintiff regarding dispossession from the suit land by defendant no. 7 is true or not and the instant suit being a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession, the High Court Division erred in decreeing the suit without arriving at a finding regarding alleged dispossession of the plaintiff in the suit land by the defendant No.7. 

 17. However, it is now well settled that the remand orders are not to be made as a matter of course. The Courts is required to properly appreciate the relevance of the evidence on record before making such Order of remand. This notion was expressed in the case of Probodh Ranjan Shome Vs. Md. Easin, reported in 4 BSCR(AD) 457. Since there is no necessity for taking any further evidence in the interest of resolution of the dispute on title, no order of remand necessarily be passed. The above view was supported by this Division in the case of Sukumar Sen Vs. Gouranga Dey reported in 42 DLR(AD) 18. 

 19. This is a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. So, the plaintiffs are to prove their chain of title and mode of possession and date and time of the alleged dispossession. 

 20. The plaintiffs-Respondent’s mode of ownership and possession over the suit land as made out in their written statement were that Hari Charan Rishi was the original owner of the suit property and the same were correctly recorded in CS Khatin No. 497 and during the SA operation the suit land bearing Plot No.1230 was recorded in his name, Hari Charan Rishi died after 02 years of SA operation leaving behind two sons namely, Paban Chandra Rishi and Ram Chandra Rishi. Paban Chandra Rishi died about two years before liberation leaving behind only son Pulin Chandra Rishi. After that Ram Chandra Rishi died in the year 1977 leaving behind one son Shushil Chandra Rishi to inherit the share of the property. Pulin Chandra Rishi and Shushil Chandra Rishi left the suit land for the good of their business and they went to Jurain Rishi Para under Demra Police Station and were settled there. Before leaving of the suit land Sukdeb Rishi, a neighbor of Pulin Rishi and Shushil Rishi, was requested to look after the suit land on their behalf. After some time Pulin Chandra Rishi left for Jurain Rishi Para and went to the village Kuthai under Keranigonj Police Station and settled there and occasionally both of them used to visit the suit land. Thereafter, since 1977 Pulin Chandra rishi and Shushil Chandra Rishi were enjoying the suit land through Sukdeb Rishi and thereafter they sold the suit land to the plaintiff by executing a saf-kabala registered deed dated 13.03.1986 bearing deed No. 24513 and handed over the possession of the suit land to the plaintiff on the same dated. After purchased of the suit land the plaintiff was enjoying the suit land by mutating his name in the khatian and by paying taxes to the Government. He constructed the pucca boundary wall surrounding the suit land. While he was peacefully possessing and residing in the suit land with his sister the defendant Nos.1-7, in the first part of the month of September, 1991 claimed the suit land as their own and threatened to hand over the possession of the suit land in their favour on 20.02.1992 and they tried to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land but they could not succeed. Being disappointed they threatened the plaintiff with dispossession from the suit land at any time and, as such, the plaintiff has a suit for permanent injunction. However, during pendency of the suit the defendants dispossessed them on 08.10.1992. 

 21. The plaintiff side was duty bound to prove the genealogy of their forerunner and mode of their possession and dispossession over the suit land. However, they skipped the burden of proving the chain of ownership upto 1977 that is prior to their deed of purchase. No certificate of death or inheritance of the concerned, Voter list, Nationality certificates were submitted and reliable oral evidences too were not adduced to establish their chain of title over the suit land. As the defendants made out their own chain of title with registered deeds alongwith possession over the suit land it was imperative on the plaintiffs to prove all of the facts relevant for the sake of establishing title, possession and dispossession alleged. On weighing the evidences it transpires that they were failed to discharge the duties. Nonetheless, the learned Judge of the trial Court decreed the suit ignoring these facts and drawn some irrelevant and self explanatory presumptions as to the aliveness of the CS owner during SA operation, awarding presumptive value of correctness of SA Khatians and inferring some sort of title from SA Khatian in favour of CS owner. Moreover, the trial Court strangely bypassed deeds of the defendants registered prior to the deeds of the plaintiffs without any convincing findings. High Court Division too relied on these grounds in decreeing the suit without considering the legal process and material on record of the suit, we are, therefore, of the view that it has committed Legal error. 

 26. In term of provision of Rules 1 and 2 of Order III of the Code of Civil Procedure attorney to act on behalf of the principal, which confines, only in respect of “acts” done by the power of attorney holder in exercise of power, granted by the instrument. Moreso, plaint was filed by the Principal, not through the power of attorney holder. Principal if testify, adverse party is entitled to be cross examined and can find out actual fact of occurrence. We, are, therefore, of the view that the attorney cannot depose for the principal in respect of any specific fact or occurrence or subject matter which only principal have a personal knowledge. In support of our above view reliance can be placed to the case of Janki Vashdeo Bhojwani and others -Vs- Indusind Bank Ltd. and others in Civil Appeal No.6790 of 2003, judgment on 06-12-2004 reported Manupatra/SC/0127/2004 at page SCC 587. 

 29. In the present case the predecessor of the respondents-plaintiffs Hari Charan Rishi sold the suit land to the predecessor of the appellant-defendants almost 38 years ago. Consequently, on this aspect of law too the respondents-plaintiffs title must be superseded by the deed of the other side. 

 “A record of rights has been described by Sir Henry Maine as a detailed statement of all rights in land drawn up periodically by the functionaries employed in setting the claims of the Government to its shares of the rental........Though it does not create a title, it gives rise to a presumption in its support, which prevails until its correctness is successfully impugned.”

parties:
Parsuram Malo and another ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Niyat Ali Dewan ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
In this civil revision leave was granted under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 22-7-2009 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka allowing the Civil Revision No. 313 of 2008 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 rejecting the application under Order XXII, rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. It appears that the present opposite party filed an application on 15-1-2006 under Order XXII, rule 10(1) read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for adding him as assignee in place of his vendors, defendant Nos. 1(1), 4 and 5 and the heirs of defendant No. 3 in Title Suit No. 215 of 1976, subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 and transfer to the court of Assistant Judge, Savar, Dhaka stating that during the pendency of the suit, he purchased 0.81 decimals of the suit land by four registered kabalas being Nos. 10490, 10491, 10492 and 10489 all dated 3-6-2004 and has been possessing the same by the aforesaid purchase. It was also stated in the application that the present suit was decreed in preliminary form by judgment and order dated 5-5-1987 and challenging the said decree the present applicant instituted Title Suit No. 367 of 2005 in the Court of Second Joint District Judge, Dhaka and the same is now pending. 

 3. The present petitioner contested the said application by filing written objection and upon hearing the parties, the learned Senior Assistant by order No. 46 dated 22-7-2008 rejected the application with a finding that the opposite party instituted Title Suit No. 367 of 2005 in the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka challenging the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 and declaring the same is illegal void ab-intio and not binding upon him and further found that in the application under Order XXII, rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure applicant failed to mention specifically how much land he purchased from whom, in which plot of land. 

 4. Against the order dated 22-7-2008, the present opposite party filed Civil Revision No. 313 of 2008 under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka and the same was eventually transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka for disposal. After hearing the parties, the learned Additional District Judge by judgment and order dated 22-7-2009 made the Rule absolute and set aside the order dated 22-7-2008 passed by the learned Assistant Judge on the finding that the original Title Suit being Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 relates to partition and after passing of the preliminary decree on 28-4-1987 no final decree has yet been passed in this suit and further found that the suit for partition kept pending till passing of the final decree. Thus there is no legal impediment to implead/add the petitioner as defendant in this suit and allowed to prosecute the suit as defendant. Moreover, High Court Division by judgment and order dated 15-4-2009 gave similar observation and directed to disposed of the Civil Revision No. 313 of 2008 filed by the present petitioner within two months from the receipt of the order and same was disposed of by judgment dated 22-7-2009. 

 6. Mr SRM Lutfor Rahman Akand, the learned Advocate argued this case on behalf of the petitioner. He firstly submits that this is not proper stage of the proceeding to implead the opposite party as defendant in Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 after passing of the preliminary decree in the said suit. Where the vendors of the opposite party were made party as defendants and the present petitioner got saham of '72 decimals of land and the defendant is the vendors of the opposite party got only '9 decimals of suit land and the said decree was upheld by the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 627 of 1998 by judgment and order dated 7-3-2000. He further submits that when the vendors of the opposite party had no saleable right, then purchase of the suit land from them, he is not entitled to add him as assignee in place of his vendors in the final decree of Title Sit No. 1 of 1985. He next submits that the vendors of the present opposite party surrendered possession of the suit land in favour of the petitioners and in pursuant to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 the RS record was corrected and after mutated their names they have been paying rents to the government. He also submits that the learned Additional District Judge without considering of the above vital aspect of the case allowed the revision to add the opposite party as assignee of his vendors in Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 and thus committed an error of law. He submits that the deed of declaration dated 3-6-2004 does not create any title over the suit land. He finally submits that the learned Additional District Judge failed to consider the findings of the learned trial court that the present opposite party filed Title Suit No. 367 of 2005 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka praying for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 is illegal, void and not binding upon him and that in the application under Order XXII, rule 10(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure there is no mention how much land purchase from whom in which plot of land and thereby committed gross error of law and accordingly prayed that Rule should be made absolute. In support of his contentions the learned Advocate refers decisions reported in AIR 1975 (SC) 733 and 7 BLT (HCD) (1999) 43. 

 7. Mr Md Ramzan Ali Sikder, appearing with Mr Md Motahar Hossain, the learned Advocates for the opposite party. Mr Md Ramzan Ali Sikder submits that the learned trial court failed to consider that the present opposite party in his application under Order XXII, rule 10(1) read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure sufficiently described the facts how much land he purchase from whom in which plot of land and accordingly, the learned Additional District Judge rightly set aside the order of the learned trial court. He further submits that the Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 being a suit for partition and has pending in which till now no final decree of partition has been passed yet, there is no legal bar to re-open the case of the entitlement opposite party share in the suit land. A suit for partition remains pending till the passing of the final decree. He next submits that the preliminary decree was passed in Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 without considering the title deed dated 29-7-1935 and if the said deed was produced by the defendants in the suit and considered, the preliminary decree would have been otherwise. 

 9. In the present revision the principal question to be decided is that after decreed the Title Suit No. 1 of 1985 in preliminary form whether the order of assignment passed by the Additional District Judge of the present opposite party as defendant in the said suit is maintainable or not. 

 14. I have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the application. It appears from the statements made in paragraph No.3 of the substitution application and paragraph No.3 of the supplementary affidavit that the reasons for delay in filing the application has been satisfactorily explained and which seems bonafide and reasonable. Accordingly, the application for substitution is allowed and for ends of Justice, the delay of 773 days in filing the revisional application is hereby condoned. The heirs of deceased petitioner No. 1 be substituted as petitioner Nos. 1(ka) and 1(kha) in place of deceased petitioner No.1 Parsuram Malo Accordingly, office is directed to note the same in the cause title of the revisional application. 

 18. The provisions are of an enabling character and entitle an assignee to do so, if so desired. It does not make incumbent upon an assignee to make the application if he thinks that his interests are being well looked after by his assignor. It is merely an alternative procedure which guards against the danger that the original defendants are no longer interested in the suit may not prosecute it or may even side with the adversary. Furthermore, under the said provision of the Code the right to apply is a continuing right accruing from day to day and is not subject to the law of limitation.

parties:
Entaj Ali (Md)------ Plaintiff-Petitioner
VS
Md Nurul Haque & ors------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as plaintiffs instituted a Title Suit being No. 17 of 1985 in the Court of Upazila Munsiff Debigonj, District-Panchagarh for a declaration of Title and confirmation of possession as well as declaration that the preparation of revisional records of right of the suit property is wrong. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff petitioner, in short, is that the suit, property originally belonged to Dadhiram Barman who is the CS recorded tenant. Dadhiram died leaving Aswani Barman and Tipri Barman, they are sister's son of Dadhiram Barman, Aswani Barman and Tipti Barman inherited the suit land along with other land as they are only heiti. Aswani died leaving his full brother Tipri Barman as his only heir. Hence the said Tipri Barman became the owner of entire properties of Didhiram including the suit land. The Plaintiff- petitioner purchased the suit land from the Tipri Barinan by a Registered sale deed and he has been possessing the same. But during preparation, of revisional records of right the suit land have wrongly been recorded in the name of defendant. Due to such wrong entry in records of rights the Title of the plaintiff might be clouded. Hence he filed the suit. 

 4. After serving of summons to the defendants and then the suit was decreed ex-parte on 21-12-1985. opposite-parties Nos. 1 to 6 were not the parties in the original suit yet they filed miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original Title Suit No. 17 of 1985 by setting-aside the Ex-parte decree and at the same time they filed a petition under Order I, rule 10 for adding them as defendants in the original suit. The learned Munsiff, Debigonj, after hearing both the parties allowed the petition under Order I, rule 10 by his order dated 274-1987 and directed to amend the plaint by, adding opposite-parties No. 1-6 as defendants in the original suit and also directed the plaintiff petitioner to add the Government of Bangladesh as a defendant. 

 6. It appears from the records that this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil. Procedure has been filed before this Court (Rangpur Session) in the year of 1987 being Civil Revision No. 55 of 1987 and the Rule was issued on 15-2-1987 upon the opposite-parties and pending hearing of the Rule, all further proceeding of Title Suit No. 17 of 1985 and Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 1986 of the Court of Munsif, Debigonj. District-Panchagarh was stayed. Notice was served upon the opposite-parties in time and made the Rule ready for hearing on 26-4-1987. 

 10. I have perused the judgment and orders of the courts below on record very carefully. The learned Munsif, Debigonj considered the documents of the parties. After hearing the parties and considering the materials on record and in the facts and circumstances of the case, the Court below allowed the petition under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and directed to amend the plaint by adding opposite-parties No. 1 to 6 as defendants in the original suit and also directed the plaintiff petitioner to add the Government of Bangladesh as defendant. 

 13. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs for ends of justice. The judgment and order dated 27-1-1987 passed by the learned Munsiff Debigonj, Panchagarh in Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 1986 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Civil Procedure Code arising out of Title Suit No. 17 of 1985 allowing the opposite-parties No. 1 to 6 to be added as defendants in the original suit and directed the petitioner to add the Government of Bangladesh as defendant in the original suit is hereby affirmed. 

 15. Accordingly, the court below is directed to dispose of the Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 1986 and Title Suit No. 17 of 1985 are expeditiously as possible, not later then 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment without any fail.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Md. Abu Zafor Siddique

lawyer:
Mr. Prabir Neogi, Adv. ------- For the petitioners 
Mr. Gopal Chandra Saha, A.A.G. with Mrs. Suchorita Sen Gupta, A.A.G. ------- For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Sree Sree Radha Ballav Deb Thakur and others ------ Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioners
Vs
Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Defendant-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J.:- The Rule have been issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.09.1993 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi in Title Appeal No.60 of 1991 affirming those dated 28.02.1991 passed by the Assistant Judge, Upazilla Puthia, District Rajshahi in Other Suit No.25 of 1990 should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in brief, are that the suit property along with other properties originally belonged to one Ram Krishna Sarker, Sree Krishna Sarker and Bijoy Krishna Sarker. By amicable family arrangement the suit property had been in exclusive share and possession of Ram Krishna Sarker. Ram Krishna Sarker setting up idol of the deity, Radha Ballav Deb Thakur in his dwelling house had been performing daily worship (Deb puja) and other rituals with utmost devotion. At the age of 71 years Ram Krishna Sarker dedicated the suit property as described in the schedule of plaint as debuttar property to the plaintiffs by a registered deed of endowment (Arpannama) dated 13' Karthik, 1349B.S. corresponding to 30' October, 1942 A.D (exhibit-5) and he himself as shebait had been performing Deb puja and other religious rites. As per terms of the deed of endowment, after the death of Ram Krishna Sacker his son Kanakadri Krishna Sacker became shebait and continued to perform Deb puja of the plaintiff's deity regularly. In 1945 Kanakadri Krishna Sarker left this country for India. Thereafter Niladri Krishna Sarker became shebait and has been performing Deb puja and other rituals of the plaintiff deity regularly. The further case of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners is such, that the suit property was wrongly recorded in the names of Niladri Krishna Sarker and his brothers in S.A. Khatian. But Niladri Krishna Sarker has been performing functions as shebait and enjoyment and possession of the suit property by the plaintiff deity had never been affected or obstructed in spite of such wrong recording. In R.S. Khatian the suit property has been recorded in the name of plaintiff deity, but in remark column of the R.S. Khatian it has been noted as 'Vested Property'. On 05.09.1979 A.D. the local tahsilder threatened to lease out the suit property as vested property necessitating institution of the suit. 

 3. Vis-a-vis; the case of the defendant-respondent-opposite parties in brief, is thus, that the original owners of the property described in the schedule of the plaint having left for India for good, the suit property was enlisted as vested and non-resident property and taking lease from the Government one Md. Elahi and Abdul Latif have been possessing the same. The further -case of the opposite parties is such, that there was no temple or bigraha in the suit property and had any bigraha been there, it was sent to India and the plaintiffs cannot be shebait. The suit lands had not been properly managed and as shebait the plaintiffs to grab the property filed the original suit on false allegations on the basis of some forged papers. The plaintiffs are not the heirs of ex-shebait and Niladri Krishna Sarker sold some portion of debuttar property as of his paternal property. The plaintiff-petitioners having no manner of right, title, interest and possession over the suit property are not entitled to get relief as prayed for. 

 4. The learned trial court after examining witnesses from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest and being aggrieved the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners preferred Title Appeal No.60 of 1991 in the Court of learned District Judge, Rajshahi which was heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi and the learned appellate court vide the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.09.1993 and 26.09.1993 respectively dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the impugned judgment and decree is neither proper nor in accordance with the provisions of law. The learned lower Appellate Court during disposal of the appeal committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and both the courts below illegally decided the merit of the suit against the plaintiffs and in favour of the defendants on the basis of surmise and conjecture. The learned Advocate Mr. Prabir Neogi on behalf of the petitioners further submits that the trial court as well as the appellate court were totally failed to assess the evidence on record properly and appreciate the actual position of law and there has-been no sifting of evidence rightly by the learned trial court as well as lower appellate court. The learned Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi committed error of law in not considering that Trust Board as mentioned in exhibit-5 and all the members of Trust Board either died or left this country the last shebait Niladri Krishna Sarker being died during the pendency of the suit his son Samirandra Krishna Sarker having all the qualifications of becoming a shebait performed Deb puja of Sree Radha Ballav Deb Thakur and looked after and managed the affairs of debuttar properties and others since of late shebait Niladri Krishna Sarker also having performed Deb puja & all the 6(six) sons of late shebait were substituted in his place. The learned counsel for the plaintiff-petitioners also submits that Ram Krishna Sarker got the suit properties in his `Saban' by amicable settlement and as such he had legal rights to endowment the suit properties as debuttar for the purpose of `Deb sheba and Deb puja' as described in the deed of endowment (exhibit-5) and as such the findings of the lower appellate court that Ram Krishna Sarker had no legal right to donate the suit properties as debuttar is absolutely baseless. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned- lower appellate court erred in law in not considering that from the evidence on record Radha Ballav Deb Thakur is still in the `Mandie at the residence of Rant Krishna Sarker at `Baneswar' and as such even if anyone of all the shebaits have migrated for India the properties of the bigraha cannot be declared as an enemy or vested and non-resident properties. It is from the evidence of the plaintiff's witnesses that Samarendra Kumar Sarker with other brothers has been possessing the suit properties on behalf of Radha Bailey Deb Thakur and the defendants have hopelessly failed to prove the possession of the defendants by giving lease. The learned counsel for the plaintiff-appellant -petitioners has drawn much emphasis to the following submissions that Sub-Section (6) of Section 9 of Act No.16 of 2001 (as amended by অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ (সংশোধন) আইন, ২০১১, (Act No.23 of 2011) which provides that the properties which is not enlisted in the `Ka' or `Kha' schedule of Bangladesh Gazette cannot be treated Vested and non-resident properties and in the said properties the Government has no manner of title, interest, right and liabilities as contemplated by law. The suit properties excepting .08 acres of land in R.S. khatian No.44/2 in Plot No. 296 out of total 14.80 acres of land is not enlisted in the `Ka' or 'Kha' schedule of the respective localities and the Government (Ministry of Land) published the list of `Ka' schedule vested properties of the concern Puthia Upazilla under Rajshahi District by Notification dated 08° February, 2012 in the Bangladesh Gazette, Extraordinary Issue, dated 08° April, 2012. In the said list in Serial No.102 only .08 acres of land appertaining to A.S. Khatian No.44/2, R.S. Plot No. 296 has been included out of 14.80 acres of land which is the subject-matter of the instant suit. The Government published list of "kha" schedule vested properties of the concern Puthia Upazilla by Notification dated 08th March, 2012 in the Bangladesh Gazette, Extraordinary Issue, dated in May, 2012 wherein the suit Property is not at all included. Act No. 16 of 2001 provides that under Section 13 Sub-section 1(kha) the suit which is pending in respect of such properties which is not enlisted as vested property in the Official Gagette is automatically abated to the extent of that portion of land. 

 8. As against the submissions of the learned counsel for the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners the learned Assistant Attorney General Mr. Copal Chandra Saha on behalf of the Govemment opposing the Rule submits that the suit of the plaintiffs is concocted and manipulated and papers produced are forged, created and not acted upon. The plaintiff's title paper i.e. the 'Arpannania' is a forged document which is not acted upon and by virtue of this 'Aipannama' no possession was delivered in favour of the plaintiffs as alleged and in fact, both the courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff-petitioners are not able to prove its case of possession of the suit property and there exist defect of parties in the suit which is apparent from the face of the records. The learned Assistant Attorney General Mr. Gopal Chandra Saha for the opposite parties further submits that there is no scrap of paper and a single witness from the side of the plaintiff-petitioners to substantiate that the plaintiffs have got possession in the disputed properties and it is evident from the papers on records that there are some left out parties whose presence are necessary for proper adjudication of the suit and both the trial court as well as the appellate court rightly decided that the suit is not maintainable under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act for want of possession and defect of parties. The learned Assistant Attorney General in support of his submissions referred some decisions of our Apex Court reported in 43 DLR (AD) 87 upon maintainability of the suit, 47 DLR (AD) 95 upon Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 4 BLT (AD) 150 upon Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 56 DLR 427, 39 DLR (AD) 237, 43 DLR 551 upon identification of the suit property, 28 DLR (AD) 57 and 51 DLR (AD) 55. The learned Assistant Attorney General lastly submits that the alleged shebait as stated from the side of the plaintiffs since not functioned properly the property in dispute is under the control and possession of the Government and the Government by leasing out the property to its lessee managing the some rightly and the learned trial court & the appellate court during disposal of the suit and appeal after proper sifting of evidence and appreciation of law decided the merit of the suit and appeal respectively and the Rule having no substance is liable to be discharged. 

 10. On perusal of the case 'record it transpires that the learned trial court during disposal of the original title suit being no.25 of 1990 decided the merit of the suit against the plaintiffs on the plea  that there exist defect of parties in the suit and two necessary parties namely Kanakadri Krishna Sarker and Amadri Krishna Sarker, 2(two) sons of Ram Krishna Sarker who are residing in India has been left out from the pleadings and the plaintiffs did not implicate them as parties to the suit whose presence are necessary to adjudicate the matter in dispute. In the last portion of the decision the learned Assistant Judge, Puthia opined that as per evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiffs the plaintiff's title to the disputed properties appears to be proved but only because the suit is bad for defect parties the plaintiffs are not entitled to get declaration of title. The learned appellate court vide the impugned judgment and decree upheld the decision of the trial court and it was further observed by the learned lower appellate court that the plaintiffs had no locus standi to file the suit as their title document the 'Arpannama' was not properly acted upon and since the suit is bad for defect of parties there is nothing to interfere with the judgment and dismissal decree of the trial court. It was also observed by the lower appellate court that after payment of rent no rent receipts were obtained year to year and submitted to prove the bonafide of the appellant-petitioners and the property in dispute cannot be treated debuttar for want of proof. 

 11. In the aforesaid context from the papers on record it appears that it is the specific case of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners that the suit property by amicable family arrangement had been in the exclusive share and possession of Ram Krishna and Ram Krishna setting up idol of the deity Radha Ballav Deb Thakur in his dwelling but had been performing daily worship there. At the age of 71 years he dedicated the suit properties as debuttar property in favour of the plaintiff deity by a registered deed of endowment (Arpannama) on 13u Karthik, 1349 B.S. corresponding to 30th October, 1942 A.D. (Exhibit-5), After the demise of Ram Krishna his son Kanakadri Krishna Sarker became the shebait and continued to perform 'Deb puja' of the plaintiff deity regularly. In the year 1945 A.D. Kanakadri left this country for India and thereafter, Niladri Krishna ,Sarker became shebait and has been performing 'Deb puja' and other rituals of the plaintiff deity regularly. It is also the specific case of the plaintiff-petitioners that despite during the S.A. Operation the S.A. khatian was wrongly recorded in the names of Niladri Krishna Sarker and his brothers but in the R.S. khatian the suit property has been recorded in the name of plaintiff deity, but in the remark column it has been noted as 'vested property' and for that noting while the concerned Tahsilder tried to lease out the property in favour of third party plaintiff's title to the suit properties has been clouded. To dispel that cloud plaintiff instituted the original suit for declaration of title. The very documentary evidence as adduced from the side of the plaintiff-petitioners marked as exhibit-3 series supports the contention of the plaintiffs. In the concern R.S. khatian in it's remark column the property is mentioned as vested property but the names of the plaintiffs has been duly recorded. The prayer for relief by the plaintiffs as cited in the prayer portion of the plaint is for declaration that the schedule properties appertaining to:C.S. khatian no. 164 and R.S. khatian no. 187 including other khatians as described in the schedule of the plaint comprising an area of 14.80 acres is liable to be declared 16 (sixteen) annas title in favour of Sree Sree Radhaballabh Deb Thakur seen as plaintiff no. 1 in the plaint and the time of cause of action cited therein is 05.09.1975 A.D. while the concerned Tahsilder tried to lease out the property in favour of third party. To substantiate the case of the plaintiffs they have adduced 5(five) witnesses. The witness no, 1 is Samarendra Krishna Sacker son of late Niladri Sarker. This witness deposed in support of the plaint case and the witness no. 2 Md. Ekramul Hoque is a `Maharar of the concern District Registry Office who after getting summon of the court brought the concerned volume book to prove the title document of the plaintiffs which is identical with the suit properties marked as 'exhibit-5'. The witness no. 3 for the plaintiffs is Vhim Charan Paul who deposed corroborating the case of the plaintiffs. The witness no. 4 Debendra Nath also states supporting the plaintiff's case. The last witness Suvash Kumar being one son of Niladri Kumar specifically states in his deposition that the suit properties are being possessed and looked after by proper management and they are as sons of Niladri Kumar Sarker being full-brothers do possess the property in dispute and they are performing all the religious activities concern to deity within the knowledge of all. 

 13. I have come across from the connected papers that the learned trial court in his judgment and decree opined that the plaintiffs have successfully proved title in the disputed properties but for defect of parties they are not entitled to get the relief as prayed for. In this context the learned Advocate Mr. Probir Neogi on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioners referred some decisions of our Apex Court reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151 & 10 BLC (AD) 41 and regarding burden of proof under the purview of Evidence Act's Sections 102 and 103 the decision reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 103 and 54 DLR (AD) 26. Consulting the relevant decisions of our Apex Court it is obvious to note that it is a settle principle of law that the suit shall not fail for reason of mis-joinder and non-joinder of the parties. No suit can fail by reason merely of non-joinder of parties. Order I Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure makes this legal position clear. Apart from this on careful scrutiny over the case records it is evident that Abdul Latif and Elahi are not the necessary parties of the suit. As lessee under the defendant No.1 their presence is not required for proper adjudication of the matter in dispute and it is within record that the defendant Government of Bangladesh is well within the plaint of the suit and they are contesting the case. The exhibited documents as it appears go to show that the rent receipts starts from Puthia Zomindari Estate upto the Government which has been duly marked as Exhibits 4-4(35) from the side of the plaintiffs. In view of the materials on record it is a glaring misconception of law as to onus probandi in a civil proceeding. Cumulatiye effect of Section 101, 102 and 103 of the Evidence Act is that unlike criminal cases, the fate of a civil suit is decided by the preponderance of evidence, in other words, comparative weight and worth of evidence led by the parties. In the instant case, the plaintiffs have established their case by producing unimpeachable documentary and credible oral evidence. All the documents forming the basis of the claim of the plaintiffs on the suit property were admitted into evidence and marked exhibits without objection. The testimony of P.W. 1 was corroborated by four other competent, credible and independent witnesses whose testimony remained unshaken in cross-examination. 

 18. Therefore; save & except .08 acre of land of R.S. khatian No.44/2 and R.S. plot No.296, the suit property i.e. remaining 14.17 acres of land is not vested property according to the provisions of Sub-section (6) of Section 9 of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ and the Government has no right, title, interest and obligation in respect of the said land and nothing to say anything about that portion of property. Thus, the sole basis of the defendant-Government's claim on the suit property falls through and the Government is estopped by law to raise any claim on the suit property except the said .08 acre of land, and that .08 acre of land also has to be returned to the real owner/claimant through the procedure as contemplated in Sections 10-15 of অর্পিত সম্পত্তি প্রত্যর্পণ আইন, ২০০১ 

 20. I have already come across that the trial court found title and possession in the suit land of the plaintiff. It dismissed the suit on the sole ground of defect of parties. 

 25. The impugned judgment and decree dated 20.09.1993 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Rajshahi in Title Appeal No.60 of 1991 affirming those dated 28.02.1991 passed by the Assistant. Judge, Upazilla Puthia, District Rajshahi in Other Suit No.25 of 1990 is hereby set-aside. 

 And the original Suit be decreed hi `part on contest save and except in respect of .08 acre of land appertaining to H.S. Khatian No.44/2 in H.S. Plot No.296 as mentioned in the schedule of the plaint in item no.6.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1999 of 2008
parties:
Shamsuddin Mollah ------ Petitioner
Vs.

full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 11.6.2008 of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 2454 of 2003 discharging the Rule obtained challenging the judgment and order dated 25.5.2003 of the First Court of Joint District Judge Dhaka passed in Title Suit No. 11 of 1992 rejecting the application filed by the defendant petitioner praying for cancellation of the appointment of the existing Advocate Commissioner and in his place to appoint another Advocate Commissioner. 

 2. The respondent No.1, filed the above ale Suit No. 11 of 1992 (originally Title Suit No.103 of 1978) praying for partition of the suit land as described in the Schedule A and B of the plaint on the Governments that the suit land belonged to late Aju Sk who died leaving behind 5 Sons and 4 daughters; Harunur Rashed was one of the sons of Aju Sk through his first wife and she is the daughter of Aju Sk through his second wife; after the oath of Harunur Rashid ejmali prospers she, by inheritance, got 7/192th and /48th shares from her father and 1768th and 7/192th shares from her sister Ayesha Khatoon in total 35/768th and 1/92th shares respectively from the practices described in A and B schedule of the plaint she had been in ejmali session of the same along with other sharers and was paying rents in ejmali; there being difficulties in making improvements in the suit property without partition of the same by metes and bounds and her request for partition Being not adhered to by the defendants, he had to file the above suit. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contest the suit and filed joint written statement. Then by her dated 7.10.95 Mr. Md. Abdul Noor Bhuiyan Bablu, Advocate, was appoint-as Advocate Commissioner for taking position of the respondent No.1 on commission at her residence and the armed Advocate Commissioner, after king deposition of the respondent No.1 commission, submitted his report in court on 5.5.97 but however the deposition of the respondent No.1 being taken the absence of defendant Nos. 1-2, 10 and 168, on their prayer the learned Subordinate Judge allowed them to cross examine the respondent No.1 on commission and Mr. Md. Abdul Noor Bhuiya was again appointed as an Advocate Commissioner for recording the deposition of the respondent No.1 in cross-examination and accordingly writ was issued on 18.6.2002 in favour of the above Advocate Commissioner, and thereafter the deposition of the respondent No.1 in his cross-examination was recorded but challenging the manner adopted by the learned Advocate Commissioner in recording the deposition in cross-examination, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, on 20.5.2003, filed two applications separately before the learned Subordinate Judge praying for cancellation of the appointment of Mr. Md. Abdul Noor Bhuiyan Babul as Advocate Commissioner and in his place to appoint another Advocate Commissioner. However the learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing, rejected the above applications. The defendant No. 1/petitioner the moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule as well as order of stay in Civil Revision No. 2454 of 2003 and, after hearing, the High Court Division, discharged the Rule.

full_judgment: 2. The petitioner filed the above writ petition on the avermants that they filed Artha Rin Suit No.03 of 2006 in the Court of Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Barisal praying for recovery of Tk.33,22,100/01 from the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 by sale of mortgaged properties and the respondent No.2, also filed Artha Rin Suit No.06 of 2006 in the same Court praying for recovery of Tk.1,11,52,626/-from. the respondent No.3 by sale of the same very mortgaged properties and the petitioner after coming to know about the above instantly filed an application in the above Artha Rin Suit No. 6 of 2006 under Order 1, Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 praying for adding them as party in the above suit stating that the properties describes in schedule Kha (1) of both the suits were mortgaged with the petitioner on 12.8.1997 by a registered deed of mortgage dated 12.8.1997 accompanied by a registered power of attorney and also by deposit of original the deeds and that schedule Kha (2) of Artha Rin Suit No.03 of 2006, which corresponds to schedule Kha (3) of Artha Rin Suit No.06 of 2006, also contains the properties mortgaged with the petitioner by registered deed of mortgage dated 7.8.2002 accompanied by a registered power of attorney and also by depositing original title deeds.

Vs.

full_judgment: 2. Short facts are, that father of the petitioners filed Title Suit No. 58 of 1970 in the 6th Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Barisal. The suit was decreed ex parte on 16-1-1971. The respondent No.1 brought Miscellaneous Case No. 15 of 1990 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that the summonses of original suit was not duly served upon the defendants and the names and addresses of the defendants were wrong and the summonses were shown served in collusion with the process server. The petitioners resisted the said application by filing written objection denying the material averments of the application and stating, inter alia, that the summons of the original suit was duly served and the ex parte decree was rightly passed since the defendants failed to appear and contest the suit. They further contended that the miscellaneous case was barred by limitation having been brought after 19 years of the ex-parte decree by the son of one of the original defendants after his death. Their further case is that one Abdul Kader, the defendant No. 3 in the said original Title Suit, brought a similar case against the same ex-parte decree being Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1971 which was dismissed on 24-3-1972. Thereafter, the second case brought by the son of another defendant (since deceased) is barred by principle of res judicata and hence the same is not maintainable.
